r.b: Graduating from the 0.5 to the 1.0 after two years took no adjustment period at all. At 58 my skin looks better than it did at 50. The boswellia and bisabolol in the base seem to keep the strong stuff calm.

Love what it does for texture, but in January my dry skin needed a rich cream layered on top or I'd flake around the nose. Works beautifully three nights a week from spring through fall. Just plan your winter routine accordingly.

Bought the 0.5 for fine lines at 34 and it ended up sorting out the constant congestion along my chin as a bonus. Took about six weeks and there was a rough patch around week three, but the payoff was worth it.

Moisturizer, then a pea of the 0.3, then moisturizer again. Doing it that way I've had zero flaking on my dry skin since the second week, and the fine lines between my brows have softened noticeably after two months.

r.t: Effective but the tube is small
r.b: It works, no argument there. Forehead lines were softer by week six on the 0.5. But 30 ml at this price when a pea size is all you need still stings compared to drugstore options. Paying for the stability and the elegant base, I suppose.

This is my third tube of the 1.0 and the crow's feet situation is genuinely better than it was a year ago. Texture is a thick cream that spreads thin. One warning, don't use it the night before a peel appointment. Learned that the hard way.
Six weeks of the 0.5 at night did more for the lines around my eyes than a year of expensive peptide creams ever managed.

Fair warning, I purged for a solid two weeks on the 0.5. Almost quit. Glad I pushed through because month two onward my skin has been the clearest and smoothest it has been in years. Docking a star for the rough start, but that is retinol for you.

After years of assuming retinol was off the table for me, the 0.3 proved otherwise. I buffer it over moisturizer and use it three nights a week. Mild tightness the first two weeks, nothing since, and my skin looks fresher overall. The tube keeps everything stable too, which matters with pure retinol.

r.t: Too much for my reactive skin
r.b: Even the 0.3 twice a week left me flaky around the mouth and slightly raw at the smile lines. I can only manage it once a week now, which means results are crawling. If your skin is reactive, budget months for the adjustment or look at gentler formats.

r.t: Tube beats a jar every time
r.b: Small thing, but I appreciate that this comes in a sealed aluminum tube instead of a jar so the retinol stays potent to the last squeeze. The 0.5 smoothed the bumpy texture on my cheeks in about a month. No fragrance, no sting, just quiet steady results.

My derm started me on the 0.3 and moved me up to the 0.5 after two months. Pea sized amount at night, every third night to begin, and by week five the rough patches on my forehead were visibly smoother. Whatever the bisabolol is doing, I never got the angry redness other retinols gave me.
Fifteen minutes before I do my makeup for any event, and my base has honestly never applied smoother than it does over this.
Solid mask, visible brightening by morning, but the eye holes sit tight against my eyes and I ended up trimming them bigger with scissors. Minor design gripe on an otherwise excellent product.

Most sheet masks slide around or gap at the nose but this one hugs properly and stays put the full twenty minutes. Loaded with essence without dripping down my neck. Skin looks lit from within for a couple of days after.
Results are lovely, my skin drinks up the essence and looks noticeably fresher. But the per-mask cost makes this a special occasion thing, not a habit. I save them for photos and presentations.
Long haul flights destroy my skin and one of these on landing night puts it back together. Cooling, calming, and the dull grey cast is gone by morning.

r.t: Bought a box for the bridal party
r.b: Handed these out to all five bridesmaids the night before the wedding and every single one asked where to buy them. Radiant, plump, zero irritation on anyone, including the bride with rosacea-prone skin.
So much essence in the packet that it dripped onto my shirt collar before I got it positioned. Wear an old tee and lean back. The glow the next morning earned back the star it almost lost.
One mask a month alongside my regular ZO routine and my tone stays even through summer. The green tea and aloe keep it soothing rather than tingly, which I didn't expect from a brightening mask.

Spent too long at the pool, came home pink, and this mask with its aloe took the heat right out while still brightening. Keep a second one in the fridge for the next weekend. Feels like a mini facial.

My cheeks tingled the whole twenty minutes and stayed flushed for about an hour afterward. The brightness the next day was nice, but my sensitive skin and the vitamin C in this seem to disagree. Patch test first if you are reactive.

Used one the morning of my sister's wedding and my skin photographed like I had eight hours of sleep instead of four. Twenty minutes, peel it off, pat in the leftover essence. The vitamin C and arbutin give a real glow, not just wetness.
The brightness is real but for me it fades within a day or two. Lovely as an event prep step, just do not expect one mask to change your skin long term. Four stars for honest, temporary radiance.
At 55 I was skeptical anything this small could matter, but a month of nightly use softened the vertical lines around my mouth enough that my daughter commented on it.
Week one was flaky, not going to sugarcoat it. Weeks two through four were the glowiest my skin has ever been. Buffer with moisturizer and start with twice a week.

Don't let the size fool you, this is the real 0.5% formula and it means business. A rice grain amount covers my whole face. The orange peel texture on my cheeks improved within the month it lasted me.

Not a gentle introduction to retinol, this is the strong stuff in a small package. My dry skin needed it buffered over moisturizer and limited to every third night. Results came anyway, just budget adjustment time.

r.t: Keeps my routine on the road
r.b: Half my month is hotels and this little tube means my retinol schedule never breaks. Same 0.5% formula, same results, just a size that survives carry-on rules.

r.t: Too aggressive for a vacation trial
r.b: Testing this on a two week trip was a mistake. My sensitive skin flaked and stung for most of the vacation photos. The formula is clearly effective but sample it at home first, not somewhere you want to look good.
Honestly every strong product should offer a trial format like this, and the retinol itself smoothed the crepey texture at my temples faster than expected.

Works exactly like the full size, which is the point, but even with a conservative amount mine lasted barely three weeks. Fine for a trial or a trip, frustrating as anything else. Price per gram is steep in this format.
Perfect for my two week Europe trip, sailed through security and kept my skin progress going. The ZCORE peptide formula feels identical to the full size my esthetician recommended.

Commitment issues with retinol? This solves them. I flaked lightly around the nose in week two, kept going, and by the time the tube ran out my forehead lines had clearly softened. Now I know the full size is worth it before spending big.

r.t: Cap worked loose in my bag
r.b: Product itself is excellent, my texture improved in three weeks of use. One star off because the cap loosened inside my toiletry bag on a flight and I lost a good quarter of the tube to my makeup pouch.

Grabbed the travel size to see if I could handle 0.5% retinol before dropping full-size money. Three weeks was exactly enough to know. Some dryness in week one, then the smoothest cheeks I've had in years. Full size ordered.
Nothing flashy, it just works, and three jars in my texture and tone are the best they have been this decade.

As a night cream it is lovely, rich without being greasy. But after two full months I can't honestly say the retinol side has done much. If you want visible correction, this is probably too polite. If you want comfort with a hint of ambition, fine.

Started my retinol journey here on my derm's advice and couldn't have asked for an easier ramp. No purge, no peeling, just gradually fresher looking skin over about eight weeks. Will graduate to something stronger eventually but this earned its spot.
Every other retinol has sent my skin into revolt within a week. Four months on this and not one flake, but the texture change is real. Whatever ratio of retinol to ectoin they landed on, it is right.
Minus thirty outside and my face isn't cracking for once. Rich enough for prairie winters but the retinol keeps working on tone underneath. Two birds, one creme.

The creme itself is a five. My gripe is putting retinol and vitamin C in an open jar where light and air get at them every night. Give me an airless pump and I'll hand over the fifth star. Scooping with a spatula in the meantime.
I alternate this with a 1% retinol, using this on recovery nights, and the combination keeps my skin progressing without ever tipping into irritation. Creamy but sinks in within a minute.
Feels like a plain rich moisturizer going on, no scent, no sting, but the vitamin C and retinol are clearly doing background work because my tone has evened out noticeably since May.

r.t: Second half of the jar went off
r.b: By the halfway point the creme had turned noticeably yellow and the texture went thin. Retinol and vitamin C do not belong in a jar, and at this price the packaging feels like a design failure. The first six weeks were genuinely good, which makes it more frustrating.

The polyglutamic acid in this is no joke. I wake up with my face feeling bouncy and soft, and after two months the sun spots on my cheekbones have faded a shade. It smells like nothing, which I appreciate.
Sixty-four year old skin finds most retinols too much and most moisturizers too little. This one threads the needle. Softer lines, less crepe on my cheeks, and comfortable every single night.

Gentlest retinol product I have used. The ectoin and polyglutamic acid keep it cushiony, so I get the smoothing benefits with none of the flaking my skin usually stages in protest. I use it straight, no buffering, four nights a week.

Over my usual moisturizer it rolled up into little bits within the hour, every single morning I tried. On bare skin it behaves fine, so it now lives in my gym bag for body use only. Effective sun protection, fussy about what sits under it.

High altitude sun is brutal and most water resistant sunscreens clog my pores within days. Two months into this one, clear skin and zero burns. It goes on white for a second then disappears on my light-medium skin.
Four hour rides with sweat pouring and my face is still protected at the end. Sensitive skin here and the zinc base has never caused redness. Slight sheen at first, gone in ten minutes.
Three sets in April heat here is a real stress test and it passed. No eye sting at match point, no white streaks in photos afterward.
Great for ski days, doesn't fail in wind or sweat. Just know there is a ten minute greasy phase after applying where you don't want to touch anything. Once it sets, it is matte enough.
Cottage season tested it hard, fishing to roofing to dock repairs, and I never burned once all summer.

Applied at the first tee, reapplied at the turn, finished the round with zero burn on a cloudless August day. It doesn't leave my hands so slick that I can't grip a club, which matters more than people think.

r.t: Tube empties fast on full body
r.b: For the face it is perfect. For two adults doing yard work and swimming, the standard tube barely lasts two weekends. Wish I had known about the larger size sooner because the per-use cost adds up.

Protection is genuinely excellent and it stays put through spin class. On my deeper skin tone there is a faint grey cast for the first while though. I work it in hard and it mostly settles, but photos right after application aren't flattering.

In and out of the ocean all afternoon and it held on exactly like the 80 minute water resistance claims. I use it on the kids too, no complaints about stinging, and the tube lives in our beach bag all summer.

r.t: No sting on sweaty trail runs
r.b: Two hour trail runs in July and this has never once migrated into my eyes. That alone puts it ahead of everything else I've tried. Rubs in fully in about a minute and my hairline doesn't break out.
On the pitch four evenings a week from May onward. Sweat, sun, no burn, no greasy drip. The vitamin E in it seems to keep my skin from feeling stripped after long days outside.
She asked what I had changed at my last appointment, before I said anything. That is the review. I pat one pump on damp skin morning and night.

r.t: Sat on top of my skin
r.b: The silicone-slip texture never fully absorbed on my oily skin, just formed a film that my SPF then slid around on. I can get comparable hydration from a basic HA serum at a third of the cost. Clearly works for others, didn't suit my skin type.
Foundation used to catch on the dry patches around my nose. One pump of this after cleansing and my base applies like my skin got resurfaced. Slight silky slip to the texture that makeup loves.
Exactly two pumps does face and neck, no waste, no guessing. Four months of daily use and the fine lines on my forehead are shallower in raking light. Understated product that earns its keep.

Furnace air and minus twenty walks were destroying my face until I added this under my night cream. The five weights of hyaluronic acid aren't marketing fluff, the hydration genuinely lasts through the night.

No complaints about performance, my skin drinks it in and stays plump through Chicago winter wind. But the bottle is small and at this price I hesitate every repurchase. Four stars with a wince at checkout.
Noticeable bounce in my cheeks by the second week, and the crosshatch lines under my eyes have visibly relaxed. A little goes far, so the price per month is less scary than the sticker suggests.

r.t: The dry patch fix I needed
r.b: Flaky cheeks since my twenties, and this is the first thing that keeps them smooth for a full 24 hours.

Tried it under three different sunscreens and two moisturizers over a month, and every combination balled up into rubbery crumbs by mid-morning. Waited between layers, used less, applied to damp skin, nothing helped. Returned it, disappointed given the hype.

Layering this over my retinol has cut the tight, squeaky feeling to zero. It has a unique cushiony gel texture, almost like a serum and a primer had a baby, and it never stings even on freshly exfoliated skin.

Recommended by my dermatologist after a resurfacing treatment, and it kept the tight, hot feeling manageable through the whole recovery. Still using it a year later on sensitive skin with zero reactions.

The smoothing effect is immediate, my smile lines look softened within minutes of applying. What sold me is that it isn't just an instant trick. Two months in, my skin holds hydration all day instead of going tight by noon.
Repurchased without hesitation, which at this price tells you everything. Firmness along my jaw and under my chin has genuinely improved, and it plays nicely under makeup.

Faithful morning and night use since February, and there might be slight firming at my jaw, or I might be talking myself into it. For this money I wanted certainty, not maybe. Texture and layering are faultless, results underwhelming so far.
Sits invisibly under moisturizer and SPF with no pilling, no residue, no scent. After about three months the skin along my cheekbones feels denser somehow, like it snaps back quicker.

The firming is real, my before and after photos agree. But this is a serious financial commitment for something you must use consistently for months. If the price were a third lower this would be an easy five.

Dramatic overnight changes don't happen at my age, but by month three my cheeks sit a little higher and the marionette area is softer. The sodium DNA and peptide combination seems gimmicky on paper and yet here we are.

Slots into an aggressive routine without adding any irritation. I use it every morning while my retinol handles nights, and the combination has my skin the firmest and calmest it has been in five years.
Between microneedling sessions my clinic suggested this, and the combination has kept my results going far longer than treatments alone used to. Light, watery-cream texture that vanishes in seconds.

r.t: Camera sees it before you do
r.b: Confession, I was ready to call it a dud until I compared photos from June and September. The improvement along my jawline is obvious in pictures even though the mirror kept me guessing. Strange but true, and I am continuing.
Skeptics should give it the full three months. That is how long it took me to believe, and now I won't be without it.

Purchased for my face and ended up loving it most for my neck. The crepey texture below my chin has smoothed out considerably since spring. One pump covers face and neck if you spread it while skin is slightly damp.

r.t: Real results on a long timeline
r.b: You will need patience. Nothing happened for the first eight weeks and I nearly gave up. Somewhere in month three the firmness changes crept in. Four stars because the wait is real, even if the destination is worth it.

r.t: Jawline is back on the map
r.b: Ten weeks of morning and night use and the softening along my jaw has visibly tightened. Photos from my daughter's graduation confirmed it was not wishful thinking. It is a slow burn product, commit for the full season.

Jumped to the full strength after a year on lower doses and within six weeks the deep lines across my forehead have visibly shallowed. It is strong, respect the adjustment period, but the results match the strength.

Rare product that treats my adult acne and my early wrinkles at the same time without shredding my face. The PhytoShield antioxidants apparently help with irritation and I believe it, because I've had none.

Dry skin here, and even the 0.25 pulled moisture out, so I buffer it between two layers of cream. Done that way it is excellent, forehead texture noticeably smoother since December. Just not a solo act for dry types.

Went too high too fast and paid for it with two weeks of red, flaking, stinging skin. Entirely my error in strength selection, but I also wish the packaging warned more clearly about stepping up gradually. Back on the 0.25 and rebuilding slowly.
Retinol in a pump bottle that never lets air degrade it, take notes everyone else. Dispenses the same dose every night, and after four months my acne scars have softened at the edges.

Well made and it works, my skin tone is more even and the crow's feet are softer after a season of use. There are cheaper retinols that get you most of the way there though, so the value question is fair. The elegant formula is what you pay for.

r.t: Best retinol I have rotated through
r.b: Rotated through four brands in three years and this is the one staying on my shelf for good.
The progression system is the smart part. Six months on 0.25, then up to 0.5 with barely a dry patch during the switch. My pores along my nose look half their old size. Take the slow road, it works.
Weeks two and three were rough, breakouts in places I never break out. It passed, and my skin now looks better than before I started. Knock off a star for the initiation ritual, but stay the course.

Turning 40 came with enlarged pores and a rough forehead I didn't sign up for. The 0.5 handled both inside of two months. I use it three nights weekly with a simple moisturizer and nothing else fancy.

r.t: No smell, no grease, no fuss
r.b: Dispenses as a light unscented lotion, sinks in before I finish brushing my teeth, and has steadily polished my skin over three months. The least annoying retinol routine I've ever kept.

Never used retinol before this, and the 0.25 with niacinamide in the base seems to have spared me the horror stories. Light lotion texture from the pump, absorbs in seconds, and my skin looked brighter within a month.

Honestly my melasma barely moved after a full twelve weeks of doing all four steps twice a day. My skin feels smoother and the pads keep my pores clear, so it is not a waste, but for this price I expected more fading. Probably better suited to newer, lighter spots than deep hormonal patches.

Glowy is the only word. The glycolic and salicylic pads give a mild tingle, then the brightening serum and Daily Power Defense sit weightless under moisturizer. My melasma band across the forehead is softer edged and my makeup sits better. Repurchasing before I run out.

Not every step earned a permanent spot on my shelf. The pads and the brightening serum evened out my upper cheeks in about two months, and Daily Power Defense feels lovely, but the polish is scratchier than everything else so I demoted it to Sundays. Pricey for the sizes too.

r.t: Skeptic converted, tone way more even
r.b: I was skeptical a kit without retinol could shift my hyperpigmentation, but the niacinamide and peptide brightening serum plus the acid pads did the job slowly and steadily. Around week ten the difference in photos was obvious. Pricey, yes, but the bottles have lasted me over three months.
Sun spots on my cheekbones that two IPL sessions could not fully clear finally faded after three months on this kit, and the routine is dead simple to follow.

r.t: Sun spots lighter by month two
r.b: Decades of sailing left my cheeks freckled with sun damage. I use the glycolic pads at night, the brightening serum morning and evening, and Daily Power Defense before SPF. Two months later my esthetician asked what I had done. At 61 with reactive skin I appreciated that nothing in this kit stung.

Solid results by week nine, the stubborn spot near my temple is half gone and my overall tone is brighter. One star off because the serum bottle is small for the cost and I'll need a second kit to finish the job.

As someone with deep skin who can't risk hydroquinone halos, this kit was the safest option my derm offered. The steps are clearly numbered on the boxes, nothing bleached or ashy, just gradual lifting of the dark marks along my jaw over about ten weeks.

Eight weeks in and the brown marks left from a bad breakout last winter are maybe seventy percent gone. Four steps sounds like a lot but the whole routine takes five minutes. No sting, no peeling, which is exactly why I picked the non-retinol version.

Bought this after a rough round of hydroquinone left me irritated and rebounding. This kit is slower but so much kinder. The exfoliating pads smell faintly medicinal, the serum is silky and fragrance free, and my mottled forehead has evened out over the summer without a single flaky day.

Results came, just slowly. Nothing visible for the first six weeks, then my post-pimple marks started to lift. Without retinol you have to accept the timeline. The morning serum pump also sputters when it gets low, which wastes product. Still finishing the kit and my tone is clearly brighter.

My dermatologist suggested this kit while I was pregnant because there is no retinol or hydroquinone in any of the four steps. The pads tingle for a few seconds and the brightening serum layers nicely under sunscreen. By week six the patch above my lip was noticeably lighter. The Daily Power Defense is the sleeper hit of the box.

Between the ramp-up schedule, mandatory sunscreen, and planning social events around peel days, this kit runs your life for two months. It works, my pigmentation and rough patches improved more than with anything else I've tried, but casual users should look at the non-retinol version.

r.t: Sun damage did not stand a chance
r.b: Twelve weeks, one ugly flaky stretch in the middle, and the mottled brown across my forehead is basically gone.

Two problems, one box. The brightening side faded the mask of pigment across my cheeks while the texture repair smoothed a decade of sun damage. Expect three weeks of flaking and tightness. I kept a bland moisturizer nearby and never skipped SPF. Photos at week twelve convinced my sister to buy it too.

Excellent system, stingy sizes. I ran out of the texture repair three weeks before everything else even using a pea at a time. Results on my acne scarring were worth it, but budget for a replacement tube mid-program.

Started this kit in December, which I don't recommend. Between the two retinols and forced-air heating my cheeks cracked, so I paused for a week and restarted at half pace. Now, at week ten, my dark spots are clearly fading and texture is much finer. Time it for spring.

r.t: Texture like glass by month three
r.b: Nothing over the counter ever touched the rough patches on my cheeks. Alternating the 1% retinol brightener and the 0.5% texture repair at night literally resurfaced my skin, and the niacinamide and glutathione step keeps the redness manageable. Started every third night, worked up to most nights.

Comparable to the series of light peels I used to get, honestly. The vitamin C morning step brightens fast while the two retinols do the heavy lifting overnight. My brown patches from years of running outside are the lightest they have been. Just know your face will shed for a couple of weeks.

Four stars only because the first month is genuinely hard. I flaked at my hairline, my smile lines stung, and makeup was pointless for two weeks. Once my skin adjusted the payoff was real, brighter, smoother, tighter pores. If you are retinol-naive, this is the deep end of the pool.

Six weeks of breakouts along my jaw before things calmed down, and I've used retinol before. The brightening results were starting to show when I finished the kit, but my skin barrier needed a month of recovery afterward. Sensitive types should think hard before committing to this one.

You earn these results. My whole face peeled through week three and I questioned everything, then it stopped and what came in underneath was smoother and brighter than my skin has looked since my twenties. Follow the ramp-up schedule, don't freelance.

Having failed with gentler routines, I wanted aggressive and got it. Using both the 1% and 0.5% retinols was intense at first, so I began twice a week each. Month one was flaky, month two was even toned, month three people started asking about my skin. Keep the enclosed guide, you will reference it.

Weeks two and three were rough, flaking around my nose and chin like I had a sunburn, but I buffered the 0.5% retinol with moisturizer and pushed through. By week eight my acne scars and the dullness were dramatically better. This kit does not baby you. Read the guide, go slow, use sunscreen religiously.
Deep smile lines softened, forehead smoothed out, and the whole transformation took about fourteen weeks of following the instructions exactly.

r.t: The whole routine in one box
r.b: Everything coordinates, which is the point. No guessing whether products conflict. The pump on the retinol doses exactly enough and the airless bottles mean nothing oxidizes. Firmer jawline by month two, smoother forehead by month three. My only note is to buy extra moisturizer for the adjustment weeks.

Followed the schedule exactly and still ended up with a raw, weepy patch on my chin at week three that took a prescription cream to calm down. Maybe my skin is the exception, but I couldn't finish the program and the cost stings almost as much as my face did.

Structure is what I was missing. Cleanser, pads, Daily Power Defense in the morning, the 1% retinol at night with clear instructions on frequency. My skin peeled around week three, then settled into the best texture of my forties. The kit format keeps me honest.

Yes you will shed. Yes it is worth it. I ramped from one retinol night a week to three, kept the glycolic pads to mornings, and slathered moisturizer in between. Week ten my daughter asked if I had gotten Botox. I hadn't.

The name is accurate. I made it to week five before persistent redness and stinging around my nose made me stop the retinol entirely. The cleanser and Daily Power Defense are lovely and I still use them, but half this kit sits unused. If your skin leans sensitive, start with their milder program.

Never had a routine beyond bar soap. My wife set me up with this kit and supervised the retinol nights. Three months on, the deep creases by my eyes have relaxed and the sun damage on my forehead is fading. The pads sting after shaving, so I space them out.

Round two for me. The first kit reset my skin last year and I took a break over the summer. Firmness around my mouth is the biggest change, plus my pores look half their old size thanks to the salicylic step. The routine card taped inside my cabinet door is falling apart from use.

r.t: Better than my last two lasers
r.b: My last two laser packages cost ten times this kit and did less for my forehead. The retinol is genuinely strong, my nose peeled like after a beach vacation, but the lines softened by month three. Daily Power Defense under sunscreen is a step I now refuse to skip.

Unforgiving is the word. I flew for work during week four and between plane air and the retinol my cheeks flaked through my foundation in a client meeting. Once I learned to buffer and time applications, results followed. Deep lines improved, skin firmer. Just respect the strength.

At 58 I wanted more than a nice moisturizer. The 1% retinol was intimidating but the kit walks you up gradually, and the glycolic pads keep the flakes moving along. Sixteen weeks later my forehead lines are shallower and my jawline looks more defined in photos. This is a commitment, not a pampering routine.

Even in Florida heat this program never felt heavy. The gel textures absorb fast and the 1% retinol at night did more for my crow's feet in ten weeks than five years of department store creams. Peeling was minimal for me, maybe because I went slow.

Somewhere in my fifties my skin went flat and dull. Six weeks with this at night and the bounce is back. It plays well over my prescription tretinoin and calms the dryness that used to force me to take breaks. Spendy, but I stopped buying two other products because of it.

r.t: Four stars for the price tag
r.b: Performance deserves five. My tight, flaky winter skin is gone and the cream layers beautifully over serums. But at this price for a small tube, I ration it like saffron, and rationing a moisturizer defeats the purpose. Will repurchase on sale only.

Post-menopause my face turned to paper. This is the first moisturizer in three years that keeps me comfortable past lunchtime. The vitamin C in it is the gentle kind, so no tingling, and my sun spots look slightly softer after two months. A tube lasts me about ten weeks.

Pea-sized amount does my entire face. The THD ascorbate means I get vitamin C benefits without layering a separate serum, which my reactive skin appreciates. Texture is like cold butter that warms and glides. Redness down, glow up, three months running.

Cold bathroom mornings make this tube genuinely hard to squeeze, and warming it under hot water became a ritual. The cream itself is wonderful, dense, calming, and my cheeks have not flared since I started. Minor packaging gripe on an otherwise excellent product.

Vitamin C, vitamin E, and serious moisture in one step means my evening routine went from twenty minutes to five. Skin feels cushioned, fine lines around my mouth look plumped by morning, and there is zero scent. My only wish is a larger size option.

Retinol wrecked my barrier in January and this cream rebuilt it. The texture is dense but spreads easily, no fragrance, no sting even on the raw spots beside my nose. Within four nights the flaking stopped. I now sandwich it around my retinoid twice a week.

Beautiful texture, wrong skin type. Two weeks in I had small bumps along my hairline and chin that cleared once I stopped. My mother, who is 68 with dry skin, took my tube and adores it. Combination and oily folks should probably look elsewhere.

r.t: Lovely, but summer is pushing it
r.b: Gorgeous in winter, a bit much in July. I get shiny by noon if I wear it during humid weather, so it has become a night-only cream from May to September. Hydration and softness are top tier. Just know this is a genuinely rich formula, not a whipped gel pretending to be one.

Chicago wind destroys my face from November to March and this cream is the only thing that keeps up. It is heavy in the best way, like a duvet for your skin, but never pills under makeup if you give it five minutes. The antioxidants are a bonus, the comfort is the point.
Dry Alberta air used to leave my cheeks scaly by February, and this thick, unscented cream fixed that in under a week.

Thick cream that melts in like a lotion. My winter-parched cheeks drank it up and I stopped waking with tight, itchy skin within the first week. The squalane gives it slip so a small amount covers the whole face and neck. At 67 this has become my non-negotiable night step.
Necklace lines softened noticeably by the twelve week mark and the cream never once made my touchy neck skin angry.

r.t: Fine, but my face cream ties it
r.b: Five months of faithful nightly use and the improvement is there but modest, maybe twenty percent softer lines. My regular retinol face cream applied to my neck seems to do about the same when I alternate. For a neck-specific product at this price I wanted a clearer win.

r.t: Tech neck rescue for a desk worker
r.b: Fifteen years of laptops gave me lines I noticed in every video call. This was my splurge and it earned it. Slight warmth the first few nights, nothing after. Around week eight the lines stopped catching shadows. I now apply it up to my jaw and down to my collarbone every night.

A warm tingling the first two weeks made me nervous but it passed. Lines are softer, skin feels denser. One star off because the retinol made my neck sun-sensitive and I learned that the hard way on a hiking trip. SPF on the neck is mandatory with this one.

Docked one star for the dispensing, the tube spits out more than needed once it is half empty and this isn't a cream to waste. Otherwise the firming is real, the smell is barely there, and my chest area (I apply it there too) looks brighter and smoother.

Skeptical me bought this after seeing my profile in a wedding photo. Believer me is on tube three. The glaucine complex supposedly works on the area under the chin, and whether that is why or not, my jawline reads sharper. Silky texture, faint pleasant smell, zero irritation.

Realistic expectations required. I saw nothing for the first two months, then a gradual smoothing that friends noticed around month four. It works, but the tube is small and the price isn't, so the cost per visible improvement is steep. Buying again anyway because nothing else has worked at all.

After sixty, my neck aged faster than my face. Four months of nightly use and the crepiness below my jaw has visibly smoothed. It has a light lotion-cream texture that absorbs before I put on pajamas, no sticky collar feeling. I went through one tube in about nine weeks.

Face retinol on the neck was always a disaster for me, instant redness and peeling. This formula with its 0.2% dose and the tripeptide blend is the compromise that works. Firmer feel in about six weeks, smoother look at three months. A pea-sized strip does my whole neck.

For the finer lines it did beautifully within ten weeks. For the two deep creases I've had since my forties, barely a dent after five months. So temper expectations by the age of your lines. Texture and tolerability are excellent, and it layers fine under fragrance-free body lotion.

Those horizontal lines from decades of looking down finally have some competition. The 0.2% retinol is gentle enough for my neck, which flakes if I even glance at my face retinoid, and by week ten the two deepest rings looked shallower. The tube nozzle keeps things tidy. Slow, steady, real.

Treated myself in February and by late spring the crepey texture on my throat had tightened up enough that I wore a scoop neckline without a scarf for the first time in years. Use it at night, warm it between your fingers first, and give it a minute to sink in.
Eighteen holes twice a week all spring, no burn, no breakouts, and my sunspots haven't darkened, which for me is a first.

Most sunscreens light my face on fire. This one, with the niacinamide and pure mineral filters, is completely calm on my reactive cheeks and the tint tones down my permanent flush. I use Fair and it adapts to my pale-but-pink complexion better than custom-mixed foundation did.

On my combination skin the luminous finish tips into shine by mid-afternoon, so I set my T-zone with powder. Otherwise it wears beautifully, never pills over my vitamin C serum, and one tube lasted me nearly three months of daily use.

Costs more per month than my gym membership if I use the proper amount, and with SPF you have to. That is the only reason for four stars. Performance is excellent, elegant tint, no flashback in photos, no irritation around my laser-treated areas.

Skin tint and SPF in one step cut my morning routine in half. Tan shade warms up perfectly on my medium-deep skin without oxidizing orange by afternoon. Dewy but not greasy finish. I have repurchased twice since spring.

Neither Fair nor Medium quite matches me, one goes slightly pink and the other slightly warm, so I mix them, which means buying two tubes of a not-cheap sunscreen. The formula itself deserves full marks, comfortable, protective, and pretty. The shade range needs to grow.

Colorado sun at 8000 feet is unforgiving and this kept me protected through a summer of trail runs. It looks like skin, feels like a light lotion, and doesn't migrate into my eyes when I sweat. The 12% zinc gives me confidence a chemical formula never did.

Wore this daily on a Broken Group Islands trip, reapplied at lunch, and came home without a hint of burn. It held up to salt spray and sweat better than any mineral SPF I have used. The Flex tint evened out my redness too. Zero stinging around the eyes.

Since my melasma flares with the slightest UV, I need a mineral SPF I'll actually wear every single day. This is it. Light coverage evens my tone enough to skip makeup, the zinc keeps my patches from darkening, and the antioxidant angle sold my dermatologist on it too.

Medium blends into my olive skin like a skin tint, not a sunscreen. No white cast, no gray undertone, and enough coverage that I skip foundation on work-from-home days. The squeeze tube travels well and a chickpea-sized amount covers my face. My new daily default.

Expecting light-medium coverage from the reviews, I found it barely tints at all over my acne marks, and the Deep shade leans slightly red on my skin. Sun protection seems solid and it never broke me out, but as a tinted product it underdelivers. I finished the tube as hand sunscreen.

Packed it for a March ski trip and it pulled double duty, SPF for the glare off the snow and a barrier against wind. The tint hid my goggle-line redness at dinner. It does need a thorough rub-in along the hairline, but the finish rewards the effort.

Made the mistake of wearing it under makeup exactly once, greasy by ten and my foundation slid right off. As a night barrier cream though, it is superb. Flaking from my exfoliation program calmed within two nights. Rich, unscented, effective, just not a day cream by any stretch.

Before my peel series my dermatologist told me to have this ready, and now I understand why. It sat gently on freshly peeled skin when even my usual sensitive-skin moisturizer stung. Between procedures I use it as a weekly overnight mask. My skin drinks it and wakes up calm.

Prescription steroid creams kept my flare-prone patches under control but never comfortable. This does the comfort part. The colloidal oatmeal takes the itch down fast and the glycerin keeps everything flexible instead of waxy. I use it on my face and the backs of my hands. Genuinely soothing.

r.t: Bought for my wife, kept for me
r.b: Her post-procedure jar ended up on my side of the counter after one desperate chinook-wind week. Heavy texture, melts on contact with warm skin, no scent at all. My razor burn and winter scale both cleared up. We now own two jars with our names on the lids.

Quebec winters chap my face on the walk to the metro. A thin layer of this at night and my cheeks stopped cracking for the first winter in years. It smells like nothing, feels like a heavy salve for ten minutes, then settles. One jar lasted the whole season.
Windburn, retinol flakes, post-flight face, this jar quietly fixes all of it overnight, every single time.

No actives, no acids, no drama. Just a dense cushion of a cream that fixed the flaking around my nose from my tretinoin nights. A jar sounds unhygienic but the cream is so thick a fingertip barely dents it. Small amount, big payoff.

Scooping a petrolatum-based cream out of a jar with wet bathroom hands isn't ideal, and I wish ZO offered a tube. The cream itself is a four-alarm dryness fix that saved my skin through an accutane course. Just keep a little spatula nearby and it earns its spot.

Two weeks of clogged pores along my cheeks and jaw despite using the thinnest layer possible. My skin skews oily and this is simply too occlusive for it. My mother uses my leftover jar happily, so it is a mismatch rather than a bad product, but oily and acne-prone folks beware.

My clinic sent me home with this after a laser treatment and it kept the raw stage comfortable without a single reaction. It is basically a sophisticated barrier ointment, petrolatum and shea doing the heavy lifting with zero fragrance. Too heavy for daily wear on my combination skin, perfect for repair weeks.

Flare season used to mean burning cheeks by evening. A pea of this pressed over my moisturizer locks everything down and the oatmeal keeps the reactivity quiet. It is occlusive, no question, so I keep it to nights, and my skin has been calmer this spring than any year I can remember.

When my ZO retinol program hit peak flake, this cream was the life raft. Thick, almost balm-like, with that colloidal oatmeal calm that settles stinging within minutes. I scoop a little with a spatula, warm it in my palms, and press it on at night. By morning the tight feeling is gone.
My monthly chin eruption is now one polite pimple instead of a constellation, which after fifteen years feels like a scheduling miracle.

Working ICU shifts in a mask wrecked my chin and cheeks. Six weeks on this system and the mask breakouts cleared while the constant irritation redness faded. The pads fit in my scrub pocket for mid-shift touch-ups. This kit understands stressed skin.

Thirty-four years old and still breaking out, until this kit. The cleanser plus salicylic pads combination stopped new pimples within a month, and the Daily Power Defense keeps my skin from feeling stripped. Texas humidity used to mean a greasy face by nine a.m. Not anymore.

Clear skin has a subscription cost now, because when I stretched out the pads to save money my congestion crept back. The system genuinely works, oil down, redness down, but replacing components adds up fast. Four stars for results, minus one for my wallet.

Zero clue what I was doing before this. The numbered steps and the included guide made it foolproof, and within six weeks the blackheads on my nose and the shine through my T-zone both backed off. My girlfriend keeps borrowing the pads. Buy your own, Sarah.

Three of the four products are excellent as is. The 2% salicylic pads run too strong for my reactive skin when used daily, so I keep them to twice a week and the system still works. Redness improved, breakouts rare now. Wish ZO let you tailor the strength at checkout.

Nobody makes products for people who have rosacea and acne at the same time, except apparently ZO. The Rozatrol step soothes while the 2% salicylic keeps my chin clear, and neither fights the other. Twelve weeks in, my cheeks are the calmest they have been since my twenties.

r.t: Middle of the road for me
r.b: Helped the oil, did little for the redness, which was my main reason for buying. After three full months my flushing is maybe ten percent better while a basic azelaic acid cream I used before did more. The pads and cleanser are good enough that I will finish them.

Photos don't lie, my before and after at eight weeks shows visibly less flush across my nose and cheeks. Rozatrol is the star for me. The pads were too strong daily at first, so I built up from three times a week. The kit format takes the guesswork out.

r.t: Effective once you survive week one
r.b: Drying at the start, no way around it. My cheeks felt tight and I nearly quit, then eased to every other day and everything balanced out. Two months later my skin is clear and the redness across my nose is halved. Start slower than the instructions suggest.

Twenty years of blotting papers and my forehead is finally matte by default. The salicylic pads morning and night cleared the little congestion bumps, and Rozatrol dialed my redness down enough that people stopped asking if I was hot. Took about five weeks to hit stride.

Other oil-control routines left my face squeaky and flaky, which just made it produce more oil. This kit controls shine without the desert feeling, I think because the Daily Power Defense step adds back what the acids take. Ten weeks in, clearer and calmer.

r.t: New scars yes, old ones shrug
r.b: The gel itself is easy to love, dries clean, no scent, never irritated the skin around it. My fresh knee scar responded beautifully. The ten year old one on my elbow barely budged after three months, so keep expectations realistic on older marks.
Sixteen weeks of twice-daily use on my tummy tuck incision and it is a flat, pale line instead of the rope I was bracing for.

Recovering from a breast reduction, my anchor scars were dark and raised. I've been massaging this in twice daily since month two and the difference at month five is significant, especially where the incisions were thinnest. The dimethicone base feels slippery going on but sets to nothing.

Two months in and my shoulder scar is maybe ten percent less red. I apply morning and night without fail. Maybe my skin is stubborn, but at this price I hoped for more visible change by now. Will finish the tube and update.

Our son split his forehead open on a coffee table. Once the stitches came out we applied this every morning and before bed. Kid-tolerable, no burning, dries fast so he stopped fussing. Eight months later you have to hunt to find the mark.

Decent results if you commit to the full twelve weeks. My thyroid surgery scar is smoother and less pink, but the gel feels slightly tacky for a few minutes, which was annoying under a collared shirt in summer. Set time was a non-issue in winter.

Used this twice a day on my shoulder surgery incision for three months. It forms a light flexible film, no smell, no sting. My surgeon commented at the follow-up that the scar was healing flatter than expected. One tube covered the whole course.

Crashed my bike in June and had ugly road rash scarring down my forearm. Applied this once everything had fully closed. The bulbine and centella combo seems to calm the redness quicker than the plain silicone sheets I used on an older scar, and it is far less fussy than sheets.

r.t: Works but the tube is tiny
r.b: Works as promised on my appendectomy scar, noticeably flatter and lighter by month three. Docking a star because the little tube goes quickly if you are covering anything bigger than a small incision, and the price adds up over a full scar protocol.

On the advice of my OB I went with this one because it had centella on top of the silicone base. Applied morning and night starting at week four postpartum. The scar went from angry red to a thin pale line in about ten weeks, and it never stuck to my waistband.

Mohs surgery left a divot and a red line beside my nose. My derm handed me a sample of this and I bought the full tube. It sat well under sunscreen every morning, which mattered since the area could not see sun. Five months later people can't tell.

After my mole removal in March I started this on my dermatologist's advice. Twice a day, a thin layer of the silicone gel over the spot on my shoulder. It dries invisible in about a minute. By week six the raised pink line had flattened and faded to almost nothing. Genuinely impressed.

Skin gets thinner every year and this is the first moisturizer that makes mine feel padded again. No fragrance issues, no clogged pores, and my foundation stopped settling into the lines around my mouth after roughly two months.
At 62 I've tried more creams than I can count. This one earned its shelf spot in a month. Firmer jawline, fewer dry flakes, and it plays nicely under my morning sunscreen on days I use it AM too.

This replaced a much-hyped night cream that cost nearly the same and did half as much. Three months in, the deep smile lines are shallower and my skin bounces back when I press it. My derm mentioned the 18 percent Proxylane concentration is unusually high and I believe it.

Solid moisturizer with a slow payoff. The first month I only noticed hydration. Somewhere in month two the elasticity changes crept in. Knock a star for the price, which I can't pretend is comfortable, but I did repurchase.

r.t: A single pump covers face and neck
r.b: You need exactly one pump for face and neck, so a tube lasts me close to three months. I apply it as my last PM step. The texture reminds me of thick pastry cream but it absorbs, and my neck is visibly less crepey since Christmas.

Broke me out along my chin and jaw within ten days, little clogged bumps I never get otherwise. My skin leans combination so maybe this is truly meant for properly dry, mature skin. Texture and pump were lovely, results weren't, and my clinic doesn't take returns.

Menopause wrecked my skin barrier and everything stung. This didn't. Thick, cushiony, faint pleasant scent that disappears fast. By week eight the slackness around my mouth improved enough that my sister asked what I changed.

Nice cream, but heavy for my combination skin in July. I moved it to nights only and cut back to half a pump on the T-zone. Used that way it is excellent, my cheeks look fuller and the flavonoid blend seems to keep redness down.

Rich without being heavy, which is rare. I use it at night over my retinol and my barrier stopped complaining within a week. The glycyrrhetinic acid must be doing something because the usual winter retinol redness never showed up.

Quietly luxurious packaging, no scraping a jar, no oxidized top layer, the airless pump delivers the same cream on day one and day seventy. The formula firmed the area under my chin over about ten weeks. A splurge, but I stretched it to eleven weeks of nightly use.

Good but the price genuinely stings for the size. Performance-wise I have no complaints, softer neck, calmer skin, plays well over my vitamin C at night. I just wait for my clinic's points events to restock.

Fifty eight, postmenopausal, and my skin drinks this up. It is a dense cream but it melts in as you massage, no greasy film by the time I finish my hair. After about six weeks my cheeks looked plumper and the crepey texture along my jaw softened. The airless pump keeps it fresh to the last dose.

Expensive for the size, so I keep it to mornings only. Used that way one unit lasted about three months and the under-eye area does look fresher and less crinkly. Would be five stars at a friendlier price.

Twelve weeks to see real change, and I mean real. The fan of fine lines at my outer corners is softer, and concealer no longer cracks there. The growth factor and neuropeptide combo apparently needs patience, so give it a full season.

Four months in and the lines under my eyes are maybe thirty percent softer. I like the metal applicator and the serum never migrates into my eyes at the gym. Progress is real but gradual, plan accordingly.

Crepey lids were my main concern and this is the first eye product to make a dent. I use it AM and PM, a rice grain per eye. Around week ten the skin looked smoother and my eyeshadow stopped creasing so badly.
Gentle enough for my reactive eye area, which has rejected almost every eye product with actives. No stinging, no redness, just a cool glide and a slightly tightened feeling as it dries.

r.t: Cold metal tip is the point
r.b: I keep this in the fridge so the metal tip turns ice cold, absolute bliss on allergy season eyes. Beyond the gimmick, the hyaluronic base hydrates well and my dark circles read less purple after a couple of months.

Love the cooling applicator, less sure the results justify the cost against my old drugstore caffeine gel. Puffiness control is better here, I'll give it that, and the texture is more elegant. Lines haven't changed much at week nine though.

It stung whenever I got it too close to my lower lashes, and my eyes water easily so that was often. Kept lower on the orbital bone it was fine, but results were mild for me after two months. The cold tip was the highlight.

Morning puffiness is basically gone since I started this. I'm a 51 year old man with zero routine beyond sunscreen, so the fact that I kept using it says a lot. The gel sets quickly and doesn't sting, and a tiny bead from the applicator covers the whole area.

Dark circles run in my family and nothing topical ever helped. This did not erase them, but paired with better sleep they are visibly lighter and the hollow area looks plumper. Sixteen weeks of consistent use. I'll repurchase.

r.t: That cooling tip earns its keep
r.b: That metal tip is cold in the best way. I sweep it from inner corner outward every morning and the de-puffing is immediate, before the actual serum even kicks in. Three months later the etched lines under my eyes have softened noticeably.
A little goes far, thankfully, because the unit is small for the money. Results are legit, less puffiness within days and smoother texture by month two. Just wish ZO sized it more generously.

Prime the brush before judging it. Day one I thought mine was broken, then suddenly powder for days. Now it is my favourite step. Matte but not flat, and my sensitive skin has never once reacted to it.

Handy but pricey per gram, and the refill cartridges exist so use them. As a between-reapplications layer over my morning lotion SPF it is brilliant. As your only sunscreen I suspect most people underapply.

Reapplying sunscreen over makeup was the gap in my routine for years, especially living in Arizona. This closes it. Twist, shake, buff on. The brush is soft, the powder finely milled, and I've had zero flashback in photos.

Finally, a top-up that survives my toddler-chasing life. It lives in the stroller cup holder. Brush on both our faces before the park, done. My dermatologist confirmed the mineral filters are fine for her too.
Matte finish, zero flashback, and it sets my tinted moisturizer better than my old finishing powder did. Two products in one as far as I am concerned. The Tan shade suits olive undertones nicely.

Hard to trust the coverage, honestly. With a cream I know how much I applied. With this brush I'm guessing, and I still caught some colour on my nose in June wearing it alone. Fine for touch-ups over real sunscreen, not as a standalone.

r.t: No white cast on deep skin
r.b: No white cast on my deep skin tone, which almost never happens with zinc oxide and titanium dioxide at these percentages. I use the Deep shade and it warms my complexion slightly rather than greying it out. Impressed enough to buy one for my mother.

Wish the lock was more secure. Mine twisted open in my gym bag and dusted everything in SPF powder, which is a very expensive way to protect a duffel. Product itself is lovely, fine texture, no scent, no breakouts.

r.t: One in the car, one at work
r.b: Keep one in my car and one at my desk. Reapplication finally happens because it needs no mirror and makes no mess. It goes right over foundation without disturbing it and knocks the shine down at the same time. Genuinely changed my sun habits.

Great concept, but you have to work for even coverage. I do three passes in circular motions or I end up with stripes of protection, which defeats the purpose. Once you build the habit it is excellent, hence four stars instead of three.

Golf season essential. I brush it over my face, ears, and part line at the turn and it takes thirty seconds, no greasy hands on my grips. The zinc and titanium formula has kept me burn-free through two full summers. Medium shade blends into my tan perfectly.

Perfect for my job doing site inspections. I can't rewash my face and reapply lotion sunscreen at noon, but I can absolutely swipe this on in the truck. No burn since I started, even through July on scaffolding.
Light, almost watery texture that I doubted could do anything. Three months later the crepiness on my cheeks has visibly improved and my esthetician asked what I added. This is the only change.
One pump covers face and neck if you press rather than rub. I have finished a full bottle and started the second, mainly because the firmness along my neck is the best it has looked in years.

Started this after a microneedling series on my clinic's advice. Zero sting on freshly treated skin, which shocked me, and the redness settled faster than after my first two sessions without it. The TriHex peptide blend is apparently the point and I'm a convert.

Pleasant to use, results are quiet and cumulative rather than dramatic. My tone looks more even and the texture finer after four months. If you want overnight wow, this isn't that. If you want your skin slightly better every month, it is.

Week ten and my jawline looks tighter in photos, which is the only place I trust my own judgment. Texture is light, almost lotion-like, with a slight fresh scent that fades in seconds. Layers under moisturizer without a trace.
Fragrance is subtle and gone in a minute, which matters to me. One pump after shaving each morning. Skin looks less tired, and razor irritation calmed down as a bonus I did not expect.

Three months of faithful morning and night use and honestly not much to report beyond nice hydration. My skin is 63 years old so maybe expectations should be modest, but for this price I expected the peptides to show me something.

My injector sells this and I assumed it was an upsell. Wrong. Between filler appointments my skin holds its bounce longer, and the fine crinkles on my cheeks have smoothed since spring. One pump AM and PM, the airless bottle lasted just under three months.

Patience required. Weeks one through six I saw nothing and nearly quit. Weeks eight through twelve the elasticity changes showed up, subtle but real. It is a marathon product with a sprint price, so budget accordingly.

Paired with tretinoin nightly, zero irritation, which no other active serum has managed for me. The niacinamide in it probably helps. Six months in, my skin is the most resilient it has been in my forties.

Silky is the right word, it glides on and vanishes, then makeup goes over it five minutes later without pilling. I noticed firmer cheeks around week nine, and my week sixteen photos convinced my skeptical husband to start it too.

Firmer? Maybe slightly. Smoother? Yes, definitely. I docked a star because at this price I want to be certain what I'm paying for, and after ten weeks the changes are subtle enough that I keep second-guessing my mirror.

Stings a little on my cheeks for the first thirty seconds, every single morning, even after months of use. Not enough to quit, because the brightening results are real, but sensitive skin folks should patch test first.

Half a dropper each morning covers face and neck, so the bottle stretches further than the price suggests. My tone is the most even it has been in years and the dark marks from a bad desert summer are basically gone.

Oily skin approved. Every vitamin C serum before this one either pilled or broke me out. This is basically water-weight, sinks in fast, and my overall tone looks brighter since January. The 2 percent phloretin is apparently the discolouration workhorse and I believe it.

r.t: A decade of C, this wins
r.b: Been using vitamin C serums for a decade and this is the one I keep returning to. The ferulic acid stabilizes it properly, my bottle never turned that scary dark brown, and my skin reads brighter within days whenever I restart after a lapse.

Turned noticeably darker by month three even stored in my cabinet, and the last quarter of the bottle smelled sharper and did less. When fresh it brightened well. For this money I expect the formula to survive a Canadian winter indoors.

Dries down in seconds flat, which matters when you get ready in fifteen minutes. Skin looks brighter and the rough texture on my forehead improved by month two. The scent is odd for the first ten seconds, then gone.

Mottled patches on my cheekbones have softened around the edges after three months, used under my tinted SPF every morning. Not a miracle, melasma never fully leaves, but this is the best topical progress I've had outside prescription options.

Effective but that scent takes getting used to, somewhere between hot dog water and pennies. It vanishes fast, thankfully. Marks faded, skin brighter, all the good stuff happened. Just breathe through your mouth for the first minute.

Post-breakout marks were my whole reason for buying, and by week eight the stubborn ones along my jaw were noticeably lighter. Layers cleanly under moisturizer with no pilling. Will repurchase despite the hit to my wallet.

Sunspots I have carried for years faded noticeably over one summer of daily use, which nothing else had touched. Four drops on dry skin every morning before SPF. The serum stayed a pale amber for the full four months it took me to finish the bottle, stored in a dark cabinet.

r.t: Vitamin C my oily skin tolerates
r.b: Switched from C E Ferulic because it felt too rich for my oily T-zone, and Phloretin CF fixed everything. Dries down in seconds, no residue under sunscreen, and the post-acne marks on my chin faded within about seven weeks.

Dropper is messy and the bottle rim gets sticky and stained amber over time. The serum itself performs, clearer tone and fewer clogged pores, and it plays fine with the salicylic elsewhere in my routine. Function five stars, form three.
As a scrub in the shower it is perfect, the steam softens everything first and the beads feel cushioned instead of scratchy. My forehead bumps cleared up over about a month of twice-weekly use.

Smoothest my skin has felt in years, full stop. Once weekly, ten minutes, rinse with a washcloth. The lactic and glycolic do the chemical work while the beads handle the physical side, and neither overdoes it.

Blackheads on my nose finally look smaller after about six weekly uses. I leave it on the full ten minutes, then work the beads over the congested spots. Nothing else in years of trying has made a visible dent there.

Better as a scrub than a mask for me. The clay is too mild to pull much from my very oily skin, but as a two-minute scrub the acid and bead combo outperforms anything else I own. Buying again for that use alone.

Ten minutes, rinse, done, and my texture problems retreat for the week. It even calmed a brewing breakout on my chin once, I assume the clay pulled it out early. The tube format is far more hygienic than a jar of clay.

Tingles for the first minute, maybe ninety seconds, then it settles like a normal clay mask. Rinses off easily without scrubbing your face raw. My skin looks polished and slightly glowy for a couple of days after each use.

Lovely results but drying if you get greedy with contact time. Ten minutes means ten minutes. I left it on while doomscrolling and paid with flaky patches. Used correctly it delivers smoother texture and smaller-looking pores.

r.t: Learned my lesson the hard way
r.b: Overdid it and paid for it, a week of tight red cheeks from doubling up with my retinol nights. Partly my fault, but the label could warn more clearly about combining actives. Used alone and sparingly it is decent.

Dual duty, quick scrub on rushed weeks or a proper clay mask when I have time. The glycolic gives a gentle tingle for the first minute, nothing alarming. My skin feels smooth afterward without that stripped clay tightness.

Once a week is plenty. I got ambitious and used it three times in one week and my cheeks let me know. Respected as a weekly treatment it is excellent, and one tube has lasted me five months and counting.

Sunday night ritual now. Ten minutes as a mask while I tidy the kitchen, then I massage it with wet fingers for thirty seconds so the jojoba beads polish everything off before rinsing. Skin looks freshly facialed every Monday morning.

r.t: A clay mask that doesn't strip
r.b: Clay masks usually leave me tight and flaky for two days. This one has enough slip, and the kaolin and bentonite are balanced so my cheeks stay comfortable. I use it Thursdays before date night because the smoothness under makeup is unreal.

Rice grain amounts, seriously, anything more just wastes it. Used that way the tube outlasted my guilt about the price. Firmness along my lower lid improved somewhere in month three and has held since.
Pricey, and you feel it at repurchase time every three months. It works, my under-eye area is smoother and makeup behaves, so I keep paying. I just wish SkinMedica sold a larger tube at better value.
Crow's feet softened around week eight, and by month four even my unsentimental teenager noticed. Morning and night, ring finger, gentle pats. The tube looks tiny but mine lasted fourteen weeks.

Tiny tube, three months of twice-daily use and still going. That math helped me forgive the sticker shock. Lines at the outer corners look finer and the whole area reads less tired even on bad sleep weeks.

r.t: Good, but is it that good
r.b: Not sure it beats my old peptide eye cream at a third of the cost. There is improvement, the firmness especially, but the gap between good and this price is where my fourth star lives. Trying one more tube before deciding.

r.t: Stays exactly where you put it
r.b: Thick but it stays exactly where you pat it, never migrating into my eyes overnight, which ended my relationship with three other eye creams. No sting, no scent worth mentioning, and my morning puffiness settles faster than it used to.

Slow and steady improvement, nothing dramatic week to week, but my three month photos show smoother texture and lighter circles. Four stars because the pace demands faith, and faith is expensive at this price point.

Concealer sits better over this than anything I've tried, no creasing by 3 pm anymore. It is a thick cream but it absorbs fully if you pat it in and wait a minute. Two months in, the crinkles when I smile look softer.

Gave me milia after about five weeks, little white bumps under both eyes that took ages to clear. My derm said the formula may be too occlusive for my skin. Nothing against the results others get, but my skin voted no.

An esthetician I trust put me on this after I complained about crepey under-eyes at 52. She was right. The growth factor blend needs about ten weeks to show off, but the change in texture is obvious even in magnifying mirrors, my personal enemy.
Under-eye brightening that actually shows up in photos. By week six the brown tinge under my eyes had lifted enough that I skip concealer on weekends. The cream is rich but a tiny dab does both eyes.

Fine lines at 47, and this is the first eye cream where I noticed the difference before my husband did. Softer, brighter, smoother by week nine. Pairs fine with my retinol as long as I keep them to opposite ends of the day.

r.t: Morning wake-up call for oily skin
r.b: This took the place of my old cleanser and my weekly scrub. Skin feels polished daily instead of sandblasted once a week, which my reactive cheeks appreciate. Zero purging when I started, just gradually clearer skin over about six weeks.

Keep one tube at home and one in the gym bag. Washes off sweat and sunscreen fast, never leaves that tight feeling, and the light exfoliation stopped the little bumps I used to get along my hairline from helmet straps.

Five stars for the cleanser itself. The flip cap earns none. Gel collects around the opening and crusts over if you aren't wiping it down every few days, and it is easy to squeeze out twice what you need. Skin looks clearer though, so I keep buying it.

r.t: Does the job twice a day
r.b: Twice a day, every day, and my T-zone has never looked better. The exfoliation is gentle enough that I can still use my retinol at night without irritation. One tube lasts me a solid three months.

r.t: Great in summer, harsh in January
r.b: Love this from May through October when my skin runs oilier. Once the heaters come on I can only handle it at night, otherwise my cheeks flake around the nose. The beads are satisfying and it rinses clean. Four stars because I still need a gentler backup half the year.

Most scrubby cleansers tear my face up. This one uses smooth jojoba beads so I get the polish without redness, and the niacinamide seems to keep my cheeks calm. Pores along my nose look noticeably tighter after about a month of morning use.

Expected a proper scrub based on the description but the beads are sparse and the exfoliation is barely there. It cleans fine and smells pleasant, just nothing my drugstore salicylic wash wasn't already doing for a third of the price. Would work better for someone who wants very gentle.

Solid daily wash and the texture improvements are real, my makeup sits smoother now. I just have a hard time paying this much for something I rinse down the drain in thirty seconds. Waiting for restock sales and buying two at a time.

Been repurchasing this for over a year. A dime-sized squeeze foams just enough to move around the face, the beads give a mild scrub feel, and my chin stopped breaking out about three weeks after I started. Calgary winters normally wreck me and this one has never left my cheeks tight.

After years of angry hormonal breakouts along my jaw, this cleanser plus the ZO pads finally calmed things down. By week four the new spots slowed to almost nothing. It lathers lightly, the beads never feel sharp, and it removes sunscreen at night if I massage a full minute.

My ZO rep put me on this when my forehead was full of tiny clogged bumps. The gel carries little round jojoba beads that polish without scratching, and the salicylic acid keeps new congestion from forming. I use it every morning before vitamin C. Skin feels clean, never squeaky or stripped. Faint citrus scent that rinses off completely.

Started using the last bit of each squeeze on my chest and shoulders in the shower and the body breakouts cleared too. On my face it is the first cleanser that manages oil through a full workday. Citrusy but subtle, and a little goes far.

Those little colorless bumps across my forehead that never turned into real pimples but never left either? Gone in about five weeks. One pad, whole face, every other night to start, then nightly once my skin adjusted.

Swipe the smooth side across the whole face first, then use the textured side on stubborn spots. My esthetician taught me that and it made these even more effective. Chin and nose stay clear now, and the tub looks tidy on the counter instead of like a pharmacy item.

Genuinely works faster on my whiteheads than the benzoyl gel my doctor gave me, and without bleaching my pillowcases. There is a medicinal smell on application that fades in about a minute. Would not use right after the exfoliating polish though, learned that the hard way.

Jumped in nightly and regretted it, my cheeks went tight and red for a week. Backed off to three nights a week and now they are perfect. Blemishes heal faster and the texture on my forehead smoothed out. Just respect the acids in these.

Annoyingly, the last dozen pads in the tub are always half dry no matter how tight I close the lid. I flip the tub upside down every few days now, which helps. Results are legit, clearer skin and smaller looking pores after six weeks, hence four stars anyway.

Use half a pad on my T-zone every morning and I stopped blotting by noon. The witch hazel gives it a proper astringent kick without leaving my skin flaky. A tub lasts me about two months cutting the pads in half.

Fridays my skin is congested from long days in makeup. A pad each night over the weekend and Monday skin is smooth and calm again. The glycolic gives a slight glow beyond just breakout control, which I didn't expect from an acne product.

Smells like straight rubbing alcohol and stung every single use, even at twice a week. After ten days my cheeks were flaking around the corners of my mouth and I had to stop. Probably fine for resilient oily skin but my face wanted nothing to do with these.

Week one brought a small purge on my chin and I nearly quit. Glad I held on, because by week two everything started clearing and three months later I get maybe one spot a cycle. Sting is mild, smell is sharp but brief.

One swipe after cleansing at night and my breakouts have dropped off dramatically. The pads are soaked in a 2% salicylic solution with glycolic and mandelic in there too, so you feel a mild tingle for maybe thirty seconds. By week three my chin was the clearest it has been since high school.

Still wear a mask at work and the constant jaw breakouts were driving me crazy. These pads ended that within a month. I swipe every night after cleansing, let it dry a minute, then moisturizer. The pad itself is nicely quilted and holds plenty of solution.

Nightly in summer, twice a week in a Minnesota winter, otherwise my cheeks flake. When dosed right these keep me almost completely clear. Wish they sold a bigger tub because the sixty count goes fast between my wife and me.

Deeply hydrating, and the tripeptide really does seem to smooth the surface over time. Two small gripes, the slanted tip gets messy once the tube is half empty, and you have to store it upright or product pools in the cap.

Between the dry cold outside and furnace air inside, my lips usually peel from November to March. This year they didn't crack once. I apply after brushing my teeth morning and night and reapply after coffee. That is the entire routine.

Right after my lip filler appointment my injector recommended this while everything was swollen and dry. It kept the flaking away during healing and I've used it daily since. The applicator tip lets you smooth it on without touching tender lips with your fingers.

r.t: Lovely but the tube is tiny
r.b: Honestly the nicest lip treatment I've used, glides on thick and my lips stopped peeling within days. Docking a star because the tube is small for the price and I go through one about every six weeks applying twice daily.

At 61 my lipstick had started feathering into the little vertical lines around my mouth. Two months of this twice a day and the bleeding is far less noticeable. I dab it slightly past the lip border as instructed. Worth every penny for that alone.

Picked one up at my med spa on a whim and loved it enough to gift it to my mom and both sisters. Everyone comments on how it feels cushiony instead of sticky. My lips drink it in within twenty minutes and stay smooth for hours.

No cinnamon sting, no menthol tingle, just gradually fuller looking lips over about three weeks. The peptide approach takes patience but my lip lines are visibly softer now. I wear it overnight and under lipstick during the day.

Was worried it would look glossy but it settles into a natural finish within a few minutes. My chronically chapped lips healed in under a week and stay comfortable with one morning application. Even my barber asked what changed.
Thick layer before bed and I wake up with lips that feel brand new. It has a very faint sweetness, no real fragrance, and it doesn't migrate onto my pillow the way my old sleeping mask did.

Comfortable and moisturizing, but so is my twelve dollar drugstore treatment. I finished the whole tube waiting for the plumping and line-smoothing effects and honestly couldn't see a difference in photos. Not bad, just not worth the premium for my lips.

Every February my lips crack no matter how much balm I pile on. This actually repaired them instead of just coating them. The texture is a thick cushiony serum from a slant-tip tube, and the hyaluronic plus the shea and cupuacu butters keep them soft through a whole workday.

Took a solid six weeks before I noticed my lips looking fuller, so don't expect an instant plumper. What you get right away is deep comfort, the shea butter richness without any waxiness. Four stars for the wait, five for the feel.

Cold wind, hot yoga, a night of bad sleep, my face used to broadcast all of it. Three months into Mystro and my skin just absorbs the chaos. Texture is smoother too, though that felt like a bonus rather than the point.

Two weeks after a fraxel session my derm had me start this. The tight, shiny feeling resolved much faster than after my first treatment when I used nothing special. It has a slight peachy tint in the bottle from the astaxanthin but goes on invisible.

You won't wake up transformed. What happens instead is your skin just stops having bad days. Fewer random spots, less tightness after cleansing, makeup sits better. Four stars only because the price demands obvious results and these are quiet ones.

Living at altitude with ski weekends means wind, sun, and dry air constantly. This serum under my moisturizer keeps the windburn redness from ever settling in. Absorbs in seconds, no residue, and one pump covers my whole face.

Pink cheeks have been my baseline my whole adult life. After eight weeks of twice daily use the background redness is noticeably softer, enough that I skip color corrector most days. The niacinamide and adaptogens do slow, quiet work. No sting, no scent, no pilling.

I wanted to love this. Applied faithfully every day for two full bottles and saw no change in redness, texture, or the stress breakouts it supposedly targets. At this price point that is a painful experiment. Returning to my basic niacinamide serum.

Performs exactly as promised for my reactive skin, calmer and more even within a month. The pump gives a consistent dose and the bottle lasted eleven weeks. I just wince at the reorder cost every single time, which keeps this at four stars.

Flying always trashes my skin for a week. Took this on a three week Europe trip, used it every morning and evening, and came home with the same skin I left with. The airless pump survived my carry-on and dispenses the exact right amount.

Somehow this serum keeps the peace between my retinol nights and my acid mornings. Since adding it I've not had a single irritation flare. Hard to explain what it does until you skip it for a week and your skin reminds you.

Everything active used to burn my face, even the so-called sensitive formulas. This one goes on like a water-thin lotion with zero reaction, and after two months my skin tolerates my vitamin C again. My derm called it a barrier retrainer and that matches my experience.

Fifty three, and my skin had turned unpredictable, oily forehead, flaky cheeks, sudden red patches. This evened all of it out over about six weeks. I use two pumps in the morning under moisturizer and SPF. It has become the one product I refuse to run out of.
