Sits under retinol, vitamin C, sunscreen, makeup, whatever, and never pills. That alone puts it ahead of the last four hydrating serums I tried. Bonus that my skin has that pushed-back firmness by week eight.

My clinic sent me home with this after microneedling and the difference in downtime was obvious, redness settled in a day instead of three. Now it is my everyday first layer, one pump morning and night.

The serum itself is great, hydrating without heaviness. My gripe is mechanical, a full press dispenses nearly double what my face needs and you can't half-pump it reliably, so I share the extra with the backs of my hands. At this price I'd rather it went further.

No fragrance, no sting, nothing to react to, and yet it is not boring. The tripeptide firming angle showed up around week six as a subtle lift through my cheeks. My barrier has been happier all summer.
On its own it wasn't quite enough for my dry cheeks, the hydration flashes off unless I follow with a cream within a minute or two. Used correctly it is lovely. Used lazily it undersells itself.
Mile-high dryness is brutal and this outperformed serums twice as thick. It feels like water going on but my face stays plump through ski days. The pump has never clogged or sputtered.

Expected a basic hyaluronic serum and got something better. It is slightly viscous out of the pump, spreads thin, and drinks in fast with no tackiness once it settles. My dehydration lines around the eyes filled in within days, and after two months the peptides seem to be earning their keep too, my jawline looks a touch tighter.

She suggested this over the regular CE Ferulic because I still get hormonal breakouts at 38, and it was the correct call. No congestion, no added shine, and the fine lines starting around my mouth look softer after two months. Store it away from light and use it up within six months or it goes orange.

Results are legit, my dark spots from picking are fading and my skin looks fresher overall. Docking a star because the herbal medicinal scent is strong every single morning and never stopped bothering me, even after months of use.
On my third bottle. It layers cleanly under everything, never pills, and the glow it gives is real without any greasiness. My esthetician noticed the difference before I said anything.

Every application stung a little around my nose for the first three weeks, and my cheeks stayed slightly pink for an hour after. It calmed down eventually and my skin does look brighter, but at this price I wanted a smoother ride. Probably better suited to tougher skin than mine.

r.t: The smell fades, results do not
r.b: Fair warning: this smells like a health food store for about sixty seconds. Push past that. Three months of daily use and my skin tone is more even than it has been in years, and my T-zone produces visibly less oil by afternoon. I use four drops every morning before moisturizer and SPF.

r.t: Matte finish is not a lie
r.b: Genuinely matte. I can apply this, wait two minutes, and go straight to zinc sunscreen with zero pilling. After about seven weeks the overall tone of my skin looks clearer and the midday shine on my nose has calmed down a lot.

r.t: Held up through a Houston summer
r.b: Humidity here is brutal and most antioxidant serums slide right off my face by lunch. This stayed put under my sunscreen all summer. My forehead is less shiny, old blemish marks are fading, and I've not had a single clogged pore from it.

Does what it claims. Less shine, brighter skin, no breakouts from it. But the price for 30 ml is hard to swallow, and the amber bottle makes it impossible to see how much is left. Four drops daily got me about fifteen weeks. I'll repurchase, grudgingly.

I switched from CE Ferulic because it felt too rich for my combination skin, and this one is a completely different experience. Watery texture, sinks in fast, no greasy film. By week five the red spots left over from winter breakouts had faded more than anything else I have tried. Dropper is standard SkinCeuticals, works fine as long as you don't touch it to your face.

Not much has ever touched the brown marks my breakouts leave behind, until this. The 15 percent L-ascorbic acid plus the salicylic seems to be the right combo for my skin. Texture is almost like water, absorbs in seconds. A bottle lasts me about four months at four drops a day, which softens the price a little.

Took a solid two months before I saw anything worth writing about, which for this price tested my patience. But my texture is smoother now and the blackheads on my nose are less obvious. It never stung or broke me out, so the slow burn was worth it in the end.

r.t: Vitamin C that respects oily skin
r.b: Finally found a vitamin C serum that does not leave me shiny by ten a.m. Four drops in the morning after cleansing, and it dries down completely matte. The salicylic acid in it seems to keep my chin breakouts quieter too. Six weeks in, my post-acne marks are noticeably lighter. The herbal smell is odd for the first minute but disappears.
Love the results on my crow's feet, hate that the last quarter of the tube is nearly impossible to squeeze out through that narrow tip. I cut mine open and scooped out two more weeks of product.

There is a mild instant plumping effect within twenty minutes that got me through the first month while the longer term results kicked in. Now at week ten my crow's feet are noticeably finer. The pointed applicator makes it easy to be precise and not waste product.

For two months my wife put this on my forehead lines every night as an experiment. I finally looked closely in March: they are visibly shallower. It feels like a light gel, no scent, no sting, and a tube apparently lasts a while when someone else applies it for you.

Nothing happened for the first six weeks and I nearly returned it. Somewhere around week eight my smile lines started looking less carved in. If you buy this, commit to a full tube before judging. Texture is pleasant, a silky gel that dries fast.

Little product, exact placement, zero waste. I use it on my elevens and the vertical lip lines that started showing at 55. Three months later the lip lines cause less lipstick bleed and the elevens look softened. Unscented, comfortable, plays well under my night cream.

Applied with the little precision tip morning and night, right into the two lines between my brows. Around week six I noticed makeup no longer settling into them. They aren't gone, I'm 61, but they are shallower and my forehead looks rested. A tube lasts about ten weeks used on three areas.

Used a full tube on my forehead over eleven weeks. Mild improvement, maybe, in certain lighting. My lines are deep and set, and I suspect this works better on early lines than established ones. It also balls up if I apply moisturizer too quickly afterward, so I have to stand around waiting.

It does soften expression lines, my crow's feet look better after two months of consistent use. But the tube is small for the price if you treat more than one area twice a day. I ration it to just my eye corners now.

Twelve weeks of twice-daily use on my nasolabial folds and the change is real. Not filler-level, but the lines catch less shadow and my foundation sits better. I layer it first, wait a minute, then moisturizer. The Argireline plus the layered hyaluronic acid seems to actually do something here.

My injector suggested this to stretch the time between Botox visits, and it honestly does. The gel has a slight silicone slip, dries down invisible, and the crow's feet that usually reappear by month three stayed soft until month four and a half. Worth it for that alone.

Deep horizontal forehead lines from years of squinting. Eight weeks in, the two worst ones look about half as deep in morning light. It never pilled under sunscreen either, which surprised me for something this concentrated.

Realistic expectations required. My deep elevens are maybe twenty percent improved after three months of religious use, which I'll take at 58, but this is no needle replacement. Nice under makeup though, almost like a blurring primer on the spots where you apply it.

Spring allergies wreck my under-eyes every year. This spring I used this gel every morning and the swelling was under control by the time I left the house. Cool, lightweight, sinks in clean under sunscreen. First eye product I have finished to the last pump.

On no-makeup days this is fantastic, tight and smooth in minutes. Under concealer it needs a full five minute wait or things start pilling. Knock a star off for the choreography, but the de-puffing itself is the best I've used.

Instant is a strong word in skincare but this one earns it. I watch the skin under my eyes smooth out over ten minutes, like it has been gently pulled taut. Great before video calls. The airless pump dispenses a tidy amount, no waste, no scooping.

However thin I applied it, once it dried the film would ball up into little white bits the second anything touched it, sunscreen, concealer, even my glasses. The tightening was real for the twenty minutes before the flaking started. Returned it.

Put this on at 6 a.m. before my sister's wedding, after crying through the rehearsal dinner the night before. By photos at nine, no bags. The silica gives a soft-focus finish that made concealer almost optional. It has become my day-of ritual for anything important.

The optical silica does not look powdery or obvious, it just quietly diffuses the shadow under my eyes. Paired with the de-puffing, my whole eye area reads fresher. Half a pump per eye is plenty. Bottle is lasting longer than I expected.

Skeptical of anything promising instant results, but you can feel a light tightening as it sets and the mirror agrees. Puffiness down, and the crepey texture under my eyes looks smoother for hours. Thin layer is the trick. Pile it on and it flakes.

Bags are visibly reduced every morning, no argument there. My hereditary dark circles didn't budge in three months, blur or no blur. If circles are your main issue, temper expectations. For swelling it is excellent.

One pump split between both eyes, tap it in, and within about five minutes the bags I wake up with have visibly tightened. There is a faint cooling feel as it sets. I keep it next to my toothbrush so I never skip it. Small pump but a little goes far.
Impressive lift within minutes, but by afternoon the skin under my eyes feels a touch tight and thirsty. I now layer a drop of eye cream on top once it sets and that solved it. Would still buy again.

Keep it in the fridge. Cold plus the caffeine is a one-two punch that flattens my morning puffiness in minutes. I'm 45 with hooded eyes and this is the only thing that makes them look more awake without makeup.

Two kids under three and I look human again by 7 a.m. The caffeine and whatever the algae complex is doing shrink the puff fast, and the slight blurring effect softens the dark circles enough that coworkers stopped commenting. Dries down in a minute or two if you keep the layer thin.

No cast on my medium-deep skin, which is rare and appreciated. The finish leans dewy though, and by mid-afternoon my T-zone needs powder. If you are oily, plan for touch-ups. Otherwise this is the most cosmetically elegant mineral SPF I've tried.

Reactive skin, rosacea prone, and most SPF makes me itch within an hour. Wore this daily for four months, including through a Florida vacation, with zero reactions. It leaves a soft natural finish, not greasy, not flat matte. Genuinely hard to find and worth the price to me.

Bought it for the no-cast claim, kept it for how soothing it is. Through an Ottawa winter my usual chapped red patches around my nose never showed up. I credit the allantoin. Goes on smooth even over flaky bits.

Performs beautifully, truly invisible, gentle on my reactive cheeks. But I go through a tube in six weeks using the proper amount for face and neck, and at this price that stings more than the sunscreen ever did.
Use it face and scalp daily. No shine dome effect, no residue on hats, no sting when I sweat on the seawall run. First zinc sunscreen I have finished a full tube of instead of abandoning in a drawer.

Texture is closer to a good lotion than a sunscreen. I skip moisturizer on humid days and just use this. No white cast, no pilling under powder, no stinging eyes at the gym. Repurchased before the first tube ran out because I got nervous.

Zero complaints about the sunscreen itself; it never irritates my skin and vanishes on application. My gripe is practical: the cap cracked in my beach bag two weeks in and the tube gets messy. Product five stars, packaging three.

On my very fair dry skin it applies well and feels soothing, but there is a persistent sheen that reads sweaty in photos rather than glowy. Fine for errands, not for events. I also wish the water resistance held up better through a hot yoga class.

Deep skin tone here and I have been burned, figuratively, by every so-called invisible mineral sunscreen on the market. This one actually disappears. Creamy out of the tube, spreads easily, and within a minute there is no trace. My reactive cheeks didn't flare once all summer.

Sits perfectly under foundation with no shifting or graying. One squeeze covers my face and neck, absorbs in under a minute, and my combination skin stays comfortable all day. My teenager with eczema-prone skin borrows it constantly, which says a lot.

Been through maybe fifteen mineral sunscreens. This is the first with 10 percent zinc that my seborrheic-dermatitis-prone face tolerates every single day. Elegant texture, invisible finish, does not cling to dry patches. Only wish the tube were bigger.

Post-IPL my derm said mineral only, nothing fragranced. This checks every box: unscented, zero sting even right after treatment, and it layers over my serums without balling up. The bisabolol seems to actually calm my cheeks rather than just not irritate them.

Acne-prone but flaky, the worst of both worlds. This hydrates deeply with nothing that clogs. Eight weeks in, no new congestion and my skin stopped overproducing oil to compensate. The gel feels like nothing on the skin once it settles.

Used it after microneedling on my nurse's suggestion. Zero sting, immediate relief from the tight feeling, and my skin drank it up for days. It has stayed in my routine long after healing. Unscented and clean-feeling in the best way.

No fragrance, no sting, no pilling under sunscreen. Just a light gel that makes every moisturizer I own work better. I have sensitive skin that protests most serums and this one has never caused a single problem in eight months.

Oily skin that still dehydrates in Alberta winters is an annoying combination. This gel fixed it. Water-light, absorbs in seconds, and my moisturizer step became optional on milder days. A bottle lasts me four months.
Absorbs nicely and adds a bit of plumpness, but honestly I cannot tell it apart from hyaluronic serums a third the price. If money were no object I'd keep it around. It isn't, so I'll not.

CE Ferulic alone left my cheeks tight by noon. Two drops of this on top and the tightness is gone without adding any oil. They clearly designed it as a layering piece and it plays that role perfectly.

Does the hydration job well and never breaks me out. The tacky phase lasts a good sixty to ninety seconds on me though, and if I rush my sunscreen it drags. Minor thing, but at this price minor things count.

In winter I layer it under Triple Lipid, in summer it replaces moisturizer entirely under SPF. Fine lines on my forehead look softer when my skin is this well hydrated. It has that faint tacky grip for a minute, which actually helps my next layer spread evenly.

Rarely repurchase anything, but this earned it. Light gel, sinks in fast, plays under everything, and my skin has looked quietly healthier since February. Nothing dramatic to report and that is exactly the point.

Nightly under my cream and I wake up with that bounce dehydrated skin forgets it can have. The panthenol seems to keep my face calm through acid nights too. Dropper is easy to control, three drops covers everything.

Genuinely nice hydrator that livened up my dull winter skin within a couple of weeks. Four stars because 30 ml of what is mostly hyaluronic acid and B5 is priced like a specialty treatment. Cheaper dupes exist; this one is just more elegant.

Three drops pressed onto damp skin between my retinol and moisturizer stopped the flaking within a week. It is a clear gel, no scent, slightly tacky for a minute, then gone. Simple product done extremely well.

Swapped my retinol for this during pregnancy with my derm's okay and honestly might not go back. Skin stays glowy and smooth, zero sting, and it doesn't pill under sunscreen. The pump gives exactly the right amount, no dropper mess.

Very good with one caveat: if I use it the same night as my prescription tretinoin my face gets tight and flaky, so it lives on my off nights. On that schedule it keeps the glow up between retinoid nights with no drama.

The bumpy texture on my forehead that no scrub could fix has mostly leveled out after a month. This is sneaky exfoliation, it feels like a hydrating serum going on but resurfaces like an acid. Fragrance-free, plays fine under moisturizer.

Maybe my expectations were off, but after a full bottle over three months I see only a mild improvement in texture. Nothing negative happened, it just underwhelmed. If you have real texture issues, an actual acid or retinoid will move faster.

Can't tolerate retinoids at all, and this has become my texture treatment instead. Pores look cleaner, the little closed comedones are gone, and my skin has an even, polished look by morning. Also layers beautifully with the B5 gel when winter hits.

Nearly seven weeks passed before my texture changed enough to notice, which is a long time to keep faith at this price. Results are real now, smoother cheeks and smaller-looking pores, but pack patience with your purchase.

Nothing obvious for two weeks, then people started asking if I had been on vacation. It smooths and brightens gradually while hydrating, no flakes, no peeling phase. I use two pumps at night and my vitamin C in the morning.

Resurfacing-wise it delivers, my skin looks brighter and feels sanded smooth in a good way. The hydration claims are oversold for my dry skin though; I still need a proper serum and cream on top or I feel tight by midnight.

Sixty-three years of weather on this face. Three months of this every night and my wife says my skin finally feels like skin again. No irritation whatsoever, which at my age and with my patience is the whole battle.

Consistent soft radiance since week three, and no purging or peeling at any point. Withholding the fifth star only because the pump started sputtering and spitting product once the bottle got half empty.

Acids make my face angry, so a resurfacing serum with zero sting felt too good to be true. Six weeks of nightly use and my cheeks are smoother than any glycolic ever got them, minus the redness. Watery texture from the pump, sinks in instantly.

Foundation used to cling to the dry patches around my nose by 2 p.m. A month of this at night and those patches are gone, so my base applies like a filter. Feels like water, smells like nothing, works like an acid without acting like one.

Here is the thing: nothing flashy happens, your skin just steadily looks more rested, firmer, and smoother until one day an old photo shocks you. Ten months and two bottles in. Unscented, absorbs in under a minute, works for my combination skin even in summer.

Using it morning and night on face, neck, and chest since January. By month two the crepey texture on my neck looked tighter, and by month four even my skeptical hairdresser commented. It is a substantial cream that somehow absorbs without residue. The airless pump is hygienic and precise.

Always thought expensive creams were pure marketing. My wife's bottle changed my mind when my perpetually dry neck stopped flaking inside two weeks and the lines from looking down at my phone softened by month three. I bought my own so we stop fighting over hers.

Menopause turned my skin to paper, and this cream gives it substance again. Plumper cheeks by week three, firmer feel along the jaw by month two. The SYN-AKE peptide sounds like a gimmick but something in here is pulling real weight.

Committed for twelve weeks before I could honestly say my neck looked different. It does now, slightly lifted and less crepey, but anyone expecting a one month miracle at this price will be disappointed. Texture and pump are faultless.

Silky, cushiony, spreads over face and throat with one and a half pumps. My makeup applies better over it than over my old primer. Six weeks in, the fine lines across my neck catch less light. This is the first neck product I have actually finished.

The results on my neck are real and the texture is the nicest I've used. But twice-daily use on face, neck, and chest empties the pump in about seven weeks and the repurchase hurts every time. I now save it for neck only.

Peptides over promises: my jawline looks firmer and the skin on my neck bounces back when pinched, something I tested weekly like a nerd. Four months in. No fragrance issues, no breakouts, and the airless pump keeps everything fresh to the last dose.

r.t: Broke me out along the jaw
r.b: Beautiful texture, but within ten days I had clusters of small bumps along my jawline and neck exactly where I applied it, and they cleared when I stopped. Tried reintroducing twice with the same result. My skin is normally not fussy, so this one stung at this price.

Twenty years at a desk gave me rings around my neck. This has visibly softened the two shallow ones since March; the deep one is a longer project. The cream feels luxurious without being heavy and never pills over my morning antioxidant serum.

Simplified my whole routine. Rich enough for my dry 60-year-old face, absorbs fast enough that I can dress right after doing my neck. The horizontal necklace lines are softer after three months. Expensive, yes, but it replaced two products.

From spring to fall it is perfect on its own. In a Winnipeg February my dry cheeks needed an oil on top or I felt tight by evening. The firming effects are gradual but honest. Four stars as a moisturizer, five as a treatment.

Colorado sun at elevation is unforgiving and I used to burn through lesser sunscreens on a single hike. Two summers of fourteeners with this and not one burn. It is water resistant for real, still working after creek crossings and heavy sweat.

Applied it on my toddler and myself all through June. Rubs in fast, leaves a light sheen rather than a white film, and has no perfume smell, just a faint clean scent that fades. The 226 gram bottle is genuinely economical compared to buying multiple small tubes.

Sand, sweat, and ocean dips every Sunday and I stopped coming home pink. Reapply once mid-session and it truly lasts. Light sheen on the skin but no grease slick, and it has never broken out my chest or back.

Protection is flawless, no burns all year including a Mexico trip in January. Docked a star because it leaves a noticeable shine that shows up in photos, and the big bottle is awkward to pack for carry-on travel.

Performs exactly as promised through runs and open water swims. Getting the last fifth out of the large bottle takes patience and shaking. Also a touch shiny on the face for daily office wear; I keep it strictly for sport days.

With three kids in summer soccer, sunscreen negotiations happen every weekend. This goes on smoothly, doesn't sting when they sweat it into their eyes, and one coat lasts a tournament morning. The large size stretched from June to late August, which no other bottle has managed.

Swim, bike, run, sweat: this stays put through all of it. I apply once before long Saturday rides and my cyclist tan lines have basically stopped getting worse. No greasy hands on the handlebars after applying, which matters more than people think.

Lives in my golf bag from May through September. Goes on my arms, legs, neck, and face before every round, never greasy on the grip, never stings my eyes on hot days. A single big bottle covered the entire season with some left over.

Both my daughters react to most drugstore sunscreens with bumps and redness. Zero reactions with this one all summer, and the zinc-based formula gives me peace of mind. It spreads easier than the pure mineral ones we tried, so nobody hides when the bottle comes out.

We bought the big 226 gram size for our Muskoka week and it handled two adults and three kids for the entire trip. Nobody burned, nobody complained about stinging eyes, and it rubbed in without the ghost-white look. Refilling the beach bag with one bottle instead of four little tubes is the dream.

On the water four days a week all season. Salt spray, sweat, sun off the waves, and this held for full mornings between reapplications. Vitamin E or not, what sold me is that my forearms stopped peeling for the first summer in years.

Great on arms and shoulders, no burns hiking. On my face it slid into my eyes during a hard run around mile four and stung for a solid ten minutes, which is the one thing a sport sunscreen should never do to me. Body only from now on.

It took a good month before I saw more than basic moisturizing. Around week five my skin started looking bouncier, so the TriHex stuff may be real, just not fast. Nice that it is unscented. Knocking a star for the pace and the price.

Airless pump means the last bit is as fresh as the first, which matters when a cream costs this much. One pump does my whole face. My skin drinks it in overnight and I wake up without that tight morning feeling I've had for years.

Bought it for post-shave irritation and dry Manitoba winters. Works for both. Now my wife uses it over her retinol nights so we are going through it twice as fast. Would appreciate a bigger size option.

Calgary chinooks destroy my skin every January and this is the first moisturizer that kept the windburn redness off my cheeks. I layer it over the Restorative Skin Complex at night. Two pumps covers face and neck. A jar this rich would feel like petroleum, somehow this doesn't.

Cream itself is lovely, my flaking around the eyebrows stopped in about ten days. The pump started sputtering with maybe a fifth left and I had to bang it on the counter to get product out. For this price the packaging should work to the last gram.

Sent home from my clinic with this after a Halo treatment and it kept the tight, sandpapery feeling away for the whole recovery week. Thick cream out of the airless pump but it melts in without sitting greasy. Now I use it every winter night. Zero sting even on freshly resurfaced skin.

Used this twice a day for a week after microneedling on my derm's instructions. Redness settled faster than my previous session where I just used a drugstore cream, and nothing stung going on. The TriHex peptides are supposedly working underneath but honestly I bought it again for the texture alone.

r.t: Wonderful at night, heavy for day
r.b: Too rich to sit under sunscreen and makeup for me, it takes a long time to fully settle. As a night cream though it is lovely, and my skin looks calmer in the morning. Four stars because I wanted a do-everything cream and this is strictly PM in my routine.

No fragrance, no essential oils, no drama. I react to almost every rich cream and this one gave me nothing but comfort. By week two the flaky patches around my nose were gone. It is expensive, but I stopped needing a separate barrier balm, so it evens out.

Whipped, dense, a little goes far. The tremella and shea combo reads heavy on paper but it absorbs before I hit the pillow. Three weeks in, the crepey feel on my cheeks softened noticeably. My esthetician noticed before I said anything.

Pilled under my mineral SPF almost every morning and felt like a film by afternoon on my oilier T-zone. My dry cheeks liked it fine. If your whole face is dry this probably deserves five stars, mine isn't, lesson learned.

Genuinely rich texture, almost balm-like, yet twenty minutes later my face just feels cushioned, not coated. The oat kernel extract seems to be doing something because the itchy patches along my jaw stopped within days. Pump is airless so nothing oxidizes or gets gunky.

r.t: Weirdly effective for something so simple
r.b: Skeptical because the ingredient list is basically two things, but the 120 ppm hypochlorous concentration seems to matter. Post-shave bumps on my neck are way down. I use it after cleansing, let it dry, then serum. Bottle lasted me about two months of daily use.

Hard to justify the cost when the ingredients read like fancy water, and yet my dermatitis patches flare less when I use it consistently. I ration it to twice a day. Wish the bottle were bigger for the price, hence four stars.

Rosacea flares used to take days to settle. A few mists of this morning and night and the heat comes down by evening. Nothing else in my routine changed, so I am crediting this little spray. No residue, no film, my moisturizer goes right over it.

Does calm my skin down, no question. The catch is it evaporates quickly and if I don't follow with moisturizer within a minute my face feels tighter than before. Fine once you learn the rhythm. Four stars for the extra step it demands.

Hockey mom who plays herself twice a week. Misting under and after the helmet cleared up the forehead bumps I have fought for two seasons. Takes two seconds, dries in maybe thirty. My teenager started stealing it, which says everything.

Finished the whole bottle over six weeks on normal skin with no procedures in between and noticed very little beyond a nice cooling feel. I suspect this shines post-treatment or on reactive skin. On boring healthy skin it was a pleasant shrug.

Keep it in my gym bag and mist after every workout before I can shower. The chin breakouts I blamed on sweat basically stopped within a month. It is just hypochlorous acid and electrolyzed water, but the concentration and the nozzle are better than the cheap ones I tried.

r.t: Bought for procedures, kept for daily
r.b: Originally got it for after my wife's microneedling appointments, then read up on hypochlorous and started misting my own face post-run. Ingrown hairs and random chin spots both improved. It is the least fussy product on our shelf.

Spritzed this every few hours after microneedling and had noticeably less crusting and tightness than my first session without it. The mist is ultra fine, no sting at all on raw skin. Smells faintly like a swimming pool for about ten seconds, then nothing.

r.t: My reactive skin's new best friend
r.b: Every toner I've tried in five years stung. This doesn't, at all. It has quietly replaced that step for me morning and night. Redness after cleansing settles in minutes instead of an hour. Buying a backup before I run out.

There is a definite chlorine whiff when you spray, which nobody warns you about with hypochlorous. It fades fast and the results are real, my post-waxing redness settles in half the time. Just do not expect a spa smell.

After my laser appointment the nurse misted this on and the cooling relief was instant, so I bought a bottle at the front desk. Been using it post-treatment and honestly just on hot days. The spray pattern is even and never spits.

Read up on the peptide studies before buying, went in with modest expectations, and still got more than I hoped. My forehead moves fine but rests smoother, if that makes sense. Half a dropper covers the whole upper face. No fragrance issues, no purging.

Within two weeks the 5% niacinamide had my skin looking brighter and more even. The expression line payoff came slower, around week eight for me, mostly on the forehead. It layers cleanly under sunscreen with zero pilling, which vitamin serums don't always get right.

Recommended by my injector to maintain results, and I can actually tell when I skip a week because my elevens start creeping back. Light texture, sinks in fast, no sting despite the 5% PHA. Plays fine under retinol nights too.

Two months in, my deeper elevens are maybe ten percent softer while the fine lines around my eyes improved more. If you expect frozen-face results you will be disappointed. As a supporting act between tox visits it earns its keep, barely, at this price.

Went in for my regular appointment and she said my lines had held better than usual. Only new thing in my routine was this serum. Texture is like a light lotion, dries down satiny, faint clean scent. A bottle lasts me about ten weeks using it once a day.

Product itself is quietly effective, my forehead texture is smoother and lines less etched after two months. The glass dropper though pulls up more than you need and it runs down the neck of the bottle. A pump would suit this texture far better.

Six weeks of nightly use and the horizontal lines on my forehead catch less light. I get tox twice a year and this stretches the smooth window between appointments. The milky serum spreads easily from the dropper and the niacinamide gives a nice glow on top.

Retinol wrecks me, so a peptide route was my only option for the lines around my mouth. Three months in they look softened, not erased, and my redness never flared once. The PHA exfoliates so gently I forgot it was in there.

Not ready for injections, so I gave this three months. The frown line between my brows is shallower in photos and my makeup no longer creases into it by noon. The peptides plus PHA combo also smoothed the texture across my forehead. Worth every penny for a needle skeptic.

The serum stays slightly tacky for about five minutes, which drives me crazy when I am rushing in the morning. Results are legit though, my bunny lines and forehead look smoother after seven weeks. Moved it to evenings and we get along fine now.

Faithfully applied it every single morning for three months and photographed my crow's feet at the start and end. I genuinely cannot see a difference. Skin felt nice and hydrated, tone slightly brighter, but for this money I needed the lines to budge. Returned my second bottle.

r.t: Smile lines softened by month two
r.b: One dropper every morning before moisturizer was my whole protocol. First month, nothing but nice hydration. Somewhere in month two the crow's feet at the corners of my eyes stopped being the first thing I saw in mirrors. Patience required, results delivered.

r.t: Too much for my sensitive skin
r.b: Between the acid pads and the scrub my barrier waved a white flag around week three, red and tight along my cheeks. Dropped the pads to twice weekly and things settled, but at that pace the kit isn't doing what it promises. Better suited to resilient, oilier skin than mine.

r.t: Worth it for the pads alone
r.b: Those complexion renewal pads are the best chemical exfoliant I've used, and I have used many. The whole kit lasted me almost four months, which softens the sticker shock. Skin is clearer, smoother, and my ingrowns after shaving are way down.

Fair warning, the pads sting for real at first. I had to start every other night for two weeks before my skin adjusted. Once it did, clearer and brighter skin, no argument. The polish is great but do not press hard, let the crystals do the work.

My skin coach insisted on getting skin ready before starting Wrinkle and Texture Repair, and she was right. Six weeks of the kit and my skin handled the retinol with barely a flake. The pads tingle for a few seconds, that is it.

Nurse here, still masked all shift. The pads at night keep my chin and jaw clear for the first time in years, and the cleanser gets the day off without stripping. Polish stays at twice a week or my sensitive spots complain. Kit number two already ordered.

Wash, polish on weekends, wipe with a pad at night. Even I can follow that. Two months later my girlfriend asked if I got a facial. Oil control through the workday is the biggest win, my forehead used to be a mirror by 2 pm.

Pads and cleanser earn five stars from me. The polish felt too aggressive for anything more than once a week on my skin, even with a light hand. If your skin runs thick and oily you will probably tolerate it more often. Solid starting point overall.

r.t: Skeptic to subscriber in six weeks
r.b: Figured a kit this simple couldn't move the needle. Six weeks later my texture is smoother, the bumps along my hairline are gone, and my skin tolerates the pads nightly now. Buying the components separately when these run out.

Honestly the exfoliating polish is the star for me, those magnesium crystals scrub without shredding, and the glycolic pads keep things clear in between. Blackheads on my nose that survived a decade of pore strips are visibly reduced at week five.

Dull, rough, thirty-something skin going in. By the third week the pads had smoothed the little bumps on my chin, and the polish leaves that fresh, slightly pink glow every Sunday. The gentle cleanser is unremarkable in the best way, no tightness after.

Love the system, hate the math. Using the cleanser twice daily means it empties weeks before the polish and pads. ZO should size these to finish together. Results wise, smoother texture and fewer clogged pores by week four, no complaints there.

Started ZO with this three months ago. Cleanser morning and night, polish twice a week, pads every evening. My texture changed noticeably inside a month, pores around my nose look tighter and the afternoon shine is gone. Simple enough that I actually kept the routine.

Adding this to an existing retinoid routine proved too much, my cheeks got flaky and irritated by week two even alternating nights. On its own it is a fine, gentle exfoliating serum. If you already use a strong retinol, think hard about whether you need both.

Apply at night, wake up smoother. It sounds like ad copy and I am as surprised as anyone. Six weeks in, the rough patch on my chin from years of surfing sun is nearly gone. Tingles the first few nights, then your skin stops noticing.

For the first two weeks this stung more than I expected around my nostrils, enough that I nearly quit. Glad I pushed through because the glow at week four is real. Start slow if you are sensitive. Also the dropper drips if you move too fast.

I used to do an at-home glycolic peel every Sunday. This nightly serum gives the same smoothness with none of the downtime or flaking. The 7.7% acid blend sounds intense but it is remarkably civilized. Makeup sits better, pores look cleaner.

Little bumps across my forehead that no cleanser ever touched are basically gone after two months of nightly use. It plays fine with my retinol on alternate nights. Slight tingle on nights after shaving, otherwise drama free.

Acids usually leave my face hot and angry. This one goes on like water from the dropper, tingles faintly for a minute, and that is the whole event. Three weeks in my skin looks polished, like I exfoliated without the aftermath. The taurine buffering seems to be more than marketing.

Melasma-adjacent dullness had me looking tired constantly. Within three weeks on this my overall tone looked lit from within, and by week six two small dark patches near my temple had faded noticeably. It layers beautifully, thin and watery, then gone.

Results are genuinely good, smoother texture and a brighter look within a month. But a bottle at nightly use goes fast, and at this price that stings more than the acids do. Waiting for sales to repurchase, which tells you my exact level of devotion.

At 54 my cheeks had that crosshatched dry texture. A month of this every evening under moisturizer and it has visibly softened. No flaking, no purge, just steady renewal. The dropper bottle looks small yet three months later I still have product left.

Straight glycolic serums made me flake at the corners of my nose. This multi-acid blend with phytic acid gives the same Saturday-morning glow without a single flake. I even use it the night before events now. Nearly weightless texture, absorbs before I count to ten.

All the reviews had me expecting a resurfacing miracle. What I got after eight weeks was a mild, pleasant glow I could probably get from a good lactic acid at a third of the price. Zero irritation to its credit. Just underwhelmed relative to the cost.

r.t: My C E Ferulic works harder now
r.b: Using this at night and my vitamin C in the morning turned my dull winter skin around in under a month. Texture on my forehead is smoother and the serum itself vanishes in seconds, no residue, no smell to speak of.

r.t: The last step my barrier needed
r.b: Overdid the acids last spring and my barrier was a mess, tight, shiny, stinging at everything. Two weeks of a gentle cleanser plus this cream and I was back. It feels rich going on and then just becomes comfortable skin. Keeping it in the rotation permanently.

Prone to eczema flares on my cheekbones every spring. This is the first moisturizer rich enough to prevent them without triggering the little bumps I get from heavy occlusives. I wake up plump and calm. My derm approved it without hesitation when I showed her.

Beautiful cream on bare skin at night, but it pilled over my vitamin C serum and under sunscreen no matter how long I waited. My combination skin also felt smothered by day three of daily use. One for truly dry faces, not mine.

Sixty-one year old skin is thin, dry, and picky. This cream leaves it comfortable for a full day and my foundation stopped catching in the dry creases beside my mouth. The airless pump delivers the same dose every time, no digging in a jar.

Sandwiching my prescription tretinoin between layers of this saved my winter routine. Zero flaking since November. It is unscented, dense, and one pump genuinely covers my whole face. A jar would tempt me to overuse it, so the airless packaging is probably saving me money.

Takes a solid few minutes to fully sink in, and if I apply anything on top too soon it balls up. Learned to make it my true last step at night and now we get along. Deeply moisturizing, my flaky chin surrendered within a week.

Ingredient nerds, this is the one. Urea and sodium PCA pull water in, ceramides and cholesterol seal it, squalane keeps it comfortable. My heels know urea well but my face had never met it. Dry patches along my jaw gone in ten days.

Yes it costs a lot. It also ended my flaky forehead within days, works over any serum without pilling, and one pump does face and neck. I bought it in August ahead of the cold and ended up using it year round at night.

Months after finishing accutane my face still felt like paper. Two pumps of this at night changed everything within a week, no sting on the raw corners of my mouth, no clogged pores despite the richness. It has that thick cream feel without any greasy shine.

October through April this cream is unbeatable on my dry skin. Come summer humidity it feels like too much, so into the drawer it goes. Four stars because the price hurts when it only earns its keep seven months a year.
Evenings after hockey the rink air leaves my face raw, and one pump of this dense, fragrance free cream has everything smooth and settled by morning.

Winnipeg in February is a skin destroyer and this cream held my face together all season. Rich, almost buttery, but it absorbs by the time I finish brushing my teeth. Not a single flake this winter, first time in years I can say that.

Wanted this to work so badly. The brightening was starting to show around week three, but so were small closed comedones along my jaw and hairline, and by week five I had to stop. My oily skin apparently reads this as too rich. Fine texture, wrong face.

Packing one pump bottle instead of a serum, a moisturizer, and prayers that my dropper does not leak in the suitcase. Skin stayed bright and hydrated through two weeks in dry mountain air. It has quietly become the anchor of my morning routine at home too.

From May to October this is all my skin wants in the morning. Once furnace season hit I had to layer a heavier cream over it, which defeats some of the one-step appeal. Brightening is gradual and real. Just know its hydration ceiling if you run dry.

Picked this up to deal with sun spots from a careless summer. Two months of morning use and the two on my cheekbone are noticeably lighter in photos. The kakadu plum and green tea give it a fresh feel and the hydration is enough that I skip serum entirely.

r.t: Five star cream, one star cap
r.b: Five stars for the product, my dull skin looks alive again after six weeks of morning use. Zero for the packaging, the cap popped off twice in my bag and the pump dispensed all over everything. Decant carefully if you travel with it.
Coworkers keep asking if I changed my makeup, but it is just five weeks of this light, cushiony vitamin C cream every morning under sunscreen.

L-ascorbic serums always burned my face. This cream version with THD ascorbate gives me the brightening without any of the drama. Light lotion texture from the pump, absorbs quickly, sits perfectly under mineral SPF. My post-blemish marks faded faster over six weeks.

Surprised how calming this is for a vitamin C product. My usual pink cheeks look settled and my skin has that healthy, rested look by week three. A single pump covers everything. My teenage daughter keeps borrowing it, which is its own five star review.

r.t: Brightening that shows on deeper skin
r.b: Plenty of vitamin C products claim brightening and deliver ash. This one evened out the hyperpigmentation around my beard line within about seven weeks with no grey cast and no clogging. Pump bottle keeps the C stable too, my last dropper serum went orange in a month.

Tried a dozen morning moisturizers that balled up under my zinc SPF. This one dries down clean in under a minute and the sunscreen glides over it. Bonus that my skin tone looks fresher, and the sodium hyaluronate keeps things plump through office air conditioning.

Give it eight weeks, not two. I almost gave up at the one month mark, then my post-shave dark marks started fading and the overall tone caught up. Nice light cream, no scent worth mentioning. Four stars for the patience required at this price point.

r.t: Vitamin C and moisturizer in one go
r.b: Ditched my separate vitamin C serum and moisturizer for this and my mornings got five minutes shorter. THD ascorbate is the gentle kind, no sting, none of that hot dog water smell some C serums have. Tone looks brighter and more even after about a month.

Foundation used to cling to the rough patches on my cheeks and now it just glides. Pores around my nose look tighter too. My single complaint is the opaque airless pump, since I never know how much is left until it sputters. Otherwise a quiet workhorse I reorder without thinking.

My dermatologist suggested this after tretinoin left me raw and peeling. The difference is night and day. Same smoothing effect over about ten weeks, none of the irritation, and the built-in salicylic keeps the small bumps on my chin from surfacing. Worth every penny for skin that hates harsh actives.

Fair warning, I purged for about two weeks before things turned around. By month two my skin was smoother and clearer than baseline, so it earned its spot, but that early stretch was rough enough that I nearly quit. Start with two nights a week.
One pump, once a night, and my skin looks better at 41 than it did at 35. That is the whole review.

r.t: Does what it claims, costs plenty
r.b: Texture is noticeably smoother after two months and breakouts are down maybe seventy percent. My only gripe is sticker shock at repurchase time. I'll buy it again, but only when it goes on sale.

Six weeks in and the dark marks from old breakouts are fading faster than with anything else I have tried. I apply it every other night under a plain moisturizer, no sting, no dryness. The zinc PCA seems to keep my midday shine in check too.

Breakouts are smaller and heal faster now that the salicylic acid rides along with the retinoid. Docking a star because the bottle emptied in about seven weeks at one pump a night, and at this price that hurts.

Hormonal breakouts along my jaw have calmed way down since I started this in June. It goes on like a thin lotion, absorbs in under a minute, and I wake up without that greasy film other night serums leave. Around week five the texture on my forehead smoothed out as a bonus.

Flaking has ruined every retinol I tried before this one. Three months in and nothing, no peeling, but the change is real. My cheeks are smoother and the clogged pores along my jaw are mostly gone. The airless pump doles out the same amount every night, which I appreciate.

r.t: More than my skin can handle
r.b: I wanted to love this but even twice a week it left my cheeks tight and pink by morning. The pump is nice and it never pilled, it is simply too strong for my reactive skin. It now handles the breakouts on my back instead, so not a total loss.

r.t: Replaced two products in my routine
r.b: This took over my alternating retinol and BHA nights and does the job of both in one pump. Fewer steps, fewer clogged pores, and my skin stopped getting confused by the back and forth. No scent to speak of, and it layers cleanly under a ceramide cream.

r.t: Handles breakouts and lines at once
r.b: Adult acne plus early fine lines is an annoying combination and this actually addresses both. One pump at night after cleansing, no purge, and by week four my chin was noticeably clearer. The light lotion texture sinks in fast and has never pilled under my moisturizer.

Really nice mild gel that melts off makeup residue without stripping. My only annoyance is that the pump dispenses more than I need, so I share the extra with my neck. Skin has looked a little brighter since week three, which I credit to the gentle botanical acids.

Even mid-flare, when almost everything burns, this doesn't. The panthenol seems to take the edge off the redness, and there is no perfumey scent to aggravate things. Been through two bottles and my cheeks stay calm through cleansing now.

r.t: Second cleanse hero in dry climate
r.b: Living at altitude, most cleansers leave me tight within minutes. This one takes off the last traces of mineral sunscreen as my second cleanse and my face stays comfortable while I wait to apply toner. The pump gives exactly the right amount in one press.

r.t: The prep step I was missing
r.b: Started this when I began a stronger vitamin C and the difference in how it applies is obvious, way less tingle and no blotchiness after. The gel is silky rather than foamy, and one pump covers my whole face. Two months in, my skin tone looks more even overall.
Zero residue after rinsing, and my retinol stopped stinging on application within the first week of using this. Didn't expect the cleanser to be the fix.
After about six weeks there is a mild glow I attribute to the botanical AHA blend, nothing dramatic but real. Wish the bottle were bigger, because two pumps per wash empties it in under two months.

Honestly hard to rave about a cleanser, but my serums do seem to absorb quicker since switching, which I assume is the whole prep-the-skin point. Rinses completely clean. Four stars because I'm not fully convinced a cheaper gentle cleanser couldn't do most of this.

Lovely texture, but by evening my T-zone needs more degreasing than this can offer on its own. I ended up double cleansing anyway, which defeats the purpose at this price. Now it is my morning cleanser only, where it is fine.

An aesthetician sent me home with this after microneedling and it did not sting even on freshly treated skin. It is a low-lather gel with a faint earthy smell from the fulvic acid, and my face felt clean but cushioned afterward. Still using it months later.

Skin feels soft and prepped, my retinol no longer tingles going on, and the light botanical scent disappears on rinsing. But fifty-plus dollars for a cleanser is a stretch, so it loses a star on value alone.

r.t: Held up through a Winnipeg February
r.b: Calgary winters usually leave my face flaky no matter how gentle the cleanser. Not this year. Between the panthenol and whatever else is in here, I got through February without a single dry patch, and my hyaluronic serum layers on smoother afterward.

Do not be alarmed by the tea-colored gel, that is apparently the fulvic acid. Barely any foam, yet it takes off everything, and my sixty-year-old skin never feels tight after. My vitamin C sinks in noticeably faster on skin washed with this.

r.t: Wish it came in a twin pack
r.b: Handy little cleanser that lasted me about three weeks of nightly use. Does what the big one does. Selling these in pairs would make more sense for anyone who travels monthly.
Fourteen days through Portugal and my face never once freaked out. That is all I ask of a travel cleanser.

Went through security at Trudeau without a second look and lasted my entire twelve-day trip to France with washes morning and night. No fragrance sting, no tightness, even with hard hotel water. My combination skin stayed completely predictable the whole trip.

Most gel cleansers leave my forehead squeaky and then twice as greasy by noon. This one cleans without triggering that rebound shine, which surprised me from such a gentle formula. The travel size convinced me, and the full pump bottle is on my counter now.

Threw it in my bag for a ski weekend expecting the usual windburned tight face at night. Washed with this and my skin actually felt comfortable enough to skip my heavier night cream. It is now permanently packed.

The flip cap popped open somewhere over the Atlantic and half the tube ended up coating my dopp kit. What survived was a perfectly nice gentle cleanser, but between the leak and the price for such a small amount, I'll decant the full size into a proper travel bottle next time.

Same reliable cleanser as the full size, and it slid right into my carry-on liquids bag. Per millilitre though, you pay a real premium for the small format. Buy it to trial the formula, not to save money.

Nice and mild, but the light lather means I need a second pass to fully remove mineral sunscreen at night. For morning washes it is exactly right. Green tea in the ingredients, no scent that I can detect.

Smart way to trial the formula before dropping money on the big bottle. Two weeks of twice-daily use told me everything, gentle, rinses clean, no breakouts. Full size ordered before this one was even empty.

Hotel tap water usually wrecks my face by day three of any trip. Used this through a week in Vegas and my skin stayed calm and soft, no flaking around my nose at all. The glycerin must be doing overtime.

Perfect size for post-spin face washes. The gel lathers just enough, rinses fast in a busy locker room, and the oat amino acids keep my face from feeling stripped before I head back to the office. This little tube earns its keep.

Traveling usually means my skin rebels. This small tube kept things boring, in the best way, across four hotels in one week. No perfume, a soft gel texture, and my cheeks never got that hot tight feeling after washing.

Alternating this with my retinol turned out to be the combination my skin was waiting for. Texture on my cheeks smoothed out within the first month and I get fewer of those deep, slow-healing spots. No pilling, no residue, just a barely-there liquid with a slight tingle.
Cheek pores I have stared at in the mirror for a decade are visibly tighter after eight weeks. Enough said, reordering.

At my age the breakouts were supposed to stop, and they never did. This is the first serum that respects that I also have wrinkles to think about. Breakouts down to almost nothing since January, and the glycolic keeps my skin tone bright. It stings a touch on application, worth it.

r.t: Plays nice with my retinol nights
r.b: So thin and watery that it disappears into skin instantly, which makes layering effortless. I follow with a peptide serum and cream and nothing pills. Two months in, my skin looks polished, pores smaller, the odd hormonal spot gone within days instead of a week.

Word of warning, the liquid is thin as water and races down your fingers if you hesitate. Dispense onto your palm quickly. Results are legit, clearer skin by week five and a smoother jawline, but the price and the messy dropper keep it at four stars.

Blackheads on and around my nose have thinned out dramatically since mid-September. I use three or four drops at night, moisturizer on top, done. It is basically water in texture so it spreads everywhere fast. Glad I ignored the price and bought it.

Only every third night works for my skin, so progress has been gradual, noticeable smoothing around week six rather than week three. It does sting for thirty seconds going on. If your skin is tougher than mine you will probably get there faster.

Miami humidity turns my face into an oil slick by mid-morning most of the year. A month of this every night and the shine is legitimately reduced through the afternoon, plus the rough patches on my forehead are gone. Dioic acid is apparently the unsung hero. The dropper makes dosing simple.

Expect a minute of tingling when it goes on and a slightly medicinal, alcohol-ish scent. Push through, because by week four my texture was visibly smoother and the little clogged pores on my chin had mostly cleared. Not one for the scent-sensitive.

Used nightly, this flaked me out around the mouth and nose within two weeks, and my skin is only moderately dry to begin with. Scaling back to twice a week fixed the flaking, but at that frequency results crawl. Probably brilliant for oily skin, just not mine.

Every month like clockwork my chin would erupt, and since starting this in February those flare-ups have shrunk to maybe one small spot. Skin looks glowier too, which I didn't expect from an acid serum. I apply it after cleansing at night, wait a few minutes, then moisturize.

Nothing else in my routine treats both problems at once. The watery serum takes seconds to absorb, and within three weeks the bumps along my chin flattened while the fine lines near my mouth looked softer. Four drops does my whole face. There is a faint clinical smell that vanishes quickly.

r.t: Slow and steady, emphasis on slow
r.b: Solid product, but temper expectations on speed. It took a full twelve weeks before I saw a convincing difference in my crow's feet, and at this price I wanted faster. No irritation at all in dry Colorado air, which counts for something.

Around week seven I noticed my concealer was sitting smoothly instead of collecting in the lines under my eyes. That was the moment I became a repeat customer. Small dab, once nightly, no irritation ever.

It works, my undereye texture is smoother and concealer no longer settles into every crease. The tube is tiny though, and the cost per gram is genuinely hard to justify. Four stars for the wallet, five for the skin.

r.t: A little goes a very long way
r.b: Half a rice grain per eye is truly enough, my first tube lasted four months. The cream has a soft peach tone that disappears on application and plays fine under my morning eye SPF. Lines from squinting at screens all day are fainter, and no dryness even in January.

Sensitive eyes here, the kind that water at strong creams. Not a single night of stinging in four months, and the crepiness under my eyes has plumped up noticeably. I keep it on my nightstand and apply it last, after my face retinol has dried down.

Patience required. Months one and two were just nice hydration, then somewhere in month three the lines at my eye corners started looking softer and shallower. The peptide and retinoid combination apparently needed time to compound. Now on tube number two.
No fireworks, just steadily better skin around my eyes every week since late July. Sometimes that is exactly what you want.

r.t: First eye retinoid I could tolerate
r.b: Regular retinol eye creams always left me red and crepey before they helped anything. This one never irritated once, even applied close to the lash line on the orbital bone, and after about two months the etched-in lines under my eyes are shallower. Genuinely impressed.

Three weeks in, tiny milia-like bumps appeared under both eyes and didn't clear until I stopped using it. Frustrating, because the texture is lovely and my lines were starting to look better. My esthetician thinks the formula is just too rich for my skin. Yours may fare better.

Under-eye crepiness had me avoiding close-up mirrors at 58. Five months of this every night and the skin looks thicker and smoother. I even pat a little on my upper lids without trouble. A tube lasts me about three months using a tiny amount.

Ten weeks of nightly use and the fan of lines at the corners of my eyes has genuinely softened. The cream is rich with a slight peachy tint from the astaxanthin, but it absorbs clear and never migrates into my eyes. A rice grain per side is plenty.

Thick enough to feel like it is doing something, yet it sinks in fully before I hit the pillow, no smeared residue on the pillowcase. Through an Edmonton winter my undereyes stayed hydrated and the fine dryness lines vanished within the first month.
Store it in the fridge, apply it cold, and thank me later. My dry skin loves the slight richness the vitamin E gives it, and the tightness I used to feel by noon has been gone since around week two.

First serious skincare purchase of my life and the learning curve was zero. Cleanse, four drops, moisturizer, sunscreen. By week three the dry dull patches on my cheeks looked alive again. I get why this has been around for two decades.

Bottle number two just arrived and I opened it the way other people open sneakers. The first one erased most of a stubborn patch of dullness on my forehead and made my pores look tighter, probably just from the evened-out tone.

The dropper is my enemy. It dribbles down the bottle neck and I have wasted a noticeable amount of an extremely expensive serum. Results are good, my age spots are lighter after four months, but the packaging needs a redesign.

Two months in and the difference shows up mostly in photos, less gray, more even, like a subtle filter. I use three drops, let it dry while I make coffee, then sunscreen. Zero pilling under anything I layer on top.

Six months of daily use and the difference is documented, my wife took monthly photos. The deep crease between my brows is unchanged, fair enough, but the overall tone, the spots, the texture around my eyes, all measurably better.

Hype is real and I say that as someone who returns most expensive skincare. The 15 percent ascorbic acid with ferulic is the original recipe everyone copies for a reason. Six weeks to visible brightness, three months to fading spots.

r.t: The only vitamin C worth it
r.b: Bought this after a pharmacist friend called it the only vitamin C worth the money. The ferulic acid supposedly stabilizes the whole formula and I believe it, my bottle stayed pale yellow to the last drop. Skin is brighter and old razor marks on my jaw faded.

Freckles I wanted to keep stayed, sun damage I wanted gone faded, which felt like luck but apparently is just consistent use. Only gripe is the dropper picks up serum on the outside of the stem and gets slippery.

Retinol at night, this in the morning, sunscreen always. That trio simplified my skincare and improved my skin more in six months than the drawer of products I used to rotate through. The ferulic acid keeps this stable to the last drop.

You can feel that it is a serious formula the moment it goes on, slightly watery, a faint metallic smell, absorbed in under a minute. Ten weeks in and the dullness I blamed on commuting and bad sleep is gone.

Winter here destroys my skin every year, and this was the first one my face stayed bright instead of gray and patchy. I layered it under a heavy ceramide cream every morning and the two never pilled once.

Layered under my moisturizer it causes zero irritation, which shocked me given my history with actives. A gentle tingle the first week, then nothing. Four months later the redness marks from old breakouts have faded and my skin barely reacts to weather swings anymore.

After my third bottle I can say this is not placebo. The hyperpigmentation from an old acne phase is maybe 70 percent gone. I keep it in a dark cabinet and finish each bottle within three months so it never oxidizes on me.

Took a chance despite my reactive skin and mostly won. A mild sting the first ten days, then calm. Tone is more even and a red patch on my chin has quieted. Four stars because sensitive folks should know the adjustment period is real.

Three weeks was all it took for coworkers to ask if I had been on vacation. It is watery, slightly slick from the vitamin E, and settles fast. I keep the amber bottle in a drawer away from light and it stayed the same pale champagne color throughout.

Ordered during a sale and now I understand why people pay full price. The dropper gives exact control, four drops covers my face and neck, and the brightness kicked in around week four. My bottle never turned dark.

Yellow tint to the serum transferred a faint tinge to my white pillowcase the one night I applied it before bed, so keep it to mornings. Otherwise it earns the hype, brighter skin, softer lines, no irritation whatsoever.

For oily skin I expected this to feel heavy, but three drops disappear in seconds and my midday shine is actually less aggressive than before. Old acne marks on my chin faded by around week five. The savory smell is a fair trade.

Smells like hot dog water, I said what everyone thinks. You forgive it quickly because the glow is real and my skin texture is the smoothest it has been in years. Docking a star because a bottle this small should not cost this much.

Expensive habit that I keep questioning. My skin is brighter, no argument, but at over two hundred dollars a bottle I expected the deeper lines to budge too, and after eight months they haven't. Buying it again is a coin flip every time.

Four drops every morning under sunscreen, that is my entire routine, and people have started commenting on my skin. It layers beautifully, never pills, and one bottle lasted me just over three months.

Half a bottle in, my skin tone is noticeably more uniform and the little lines by my eyes catch less light. The texture is almost thinner than water, spreads easily, dries down clean. The savory scent is gone within a minute.

Post-IPL my clinic recommended adding this to protect the investment, and the results have held beautifully for eight months. Pigment has not crept back the way it did after my first round of treatments years ago.

Slight sting on application and a smell I can only call meaty, neither of which stopped me finishing the bottle because the results are legit. Softer lines across my forehead, brighter overall. Just wish the experience matched the price.

At 52 I have tried a lot of antioxidant serums and this is the one that made my esthetician ask what changed. Fine lines around my eyes look softer and the sun damage on my forehead has faded meaningfully since spring.

This replaced three other products in my morning routine. A few drops from the dropper, press it in, done. The vitamin E adds just enough slip that my dry cheeks do not feel stripped, and the glow by week three was noticeable in photos.

Compared it side by side with a cheaper dupe for two months, this on the left cheek, the dupe on the right. Left side won on brightness and the fading of one stubborn spot. Placebo is impossible when your own face is the control.

Pricey, yes, and on my oily T-zone the finish reads slightly greasy until it fully sets. Still, my acne marks faded faster than with anything else I've used and my skin tolerates it with zero irritation. Would love a mattifying version.

Can't do the smell, I really tried. It hits like broth every morning and lingered on my skin for close to an hour, and on top of that I got small itchy bumps along my jaw in week two. Returned what was left. Clearly works for others, not for me.

On my fifth bottle. The consistency between batches is perfect, always the same pale yellow, same quick-absorbing feel. Sunspots along my hairline have lightened and my barber noticed. A grown man doesn't expect compliments at the barber.

The smell is genuinely strange, like hot dog water, and it took me two weeks to stop noticing it. Results are real though. Redness around my nose calmed down and my tone looked more even by week six. Four stars only because of the scent and the price.

Genuinely brighter skin in under a month, and I'm the least consistent person alive with skincare. Even applying it maybe five mornings a week the change was obvious enough that my roommate asked what I switched.

It stings for about thirty seconds every single morning, even after three months. My skin does look brighter and a little firmer, but with sensitive skin I have to skip days after retinol nights, which slows everything down. Good product, tricky fit for me.

Received a sample from my derm after a consult and finished it in ten days, then bought the full amber bottle. Two months later the sun damage on my left cheek, the driving side, has faded noticeably.

There is a reason every dermatologist I have ever seen name-drops this serum. The L-ascorbic acid concentration is at the top of what skin can actually use and it shows, brighter within a month, an old sunspot on my temple half gone by month three.

Not going to lie, the price stung more than the serum. But my melasma patch is lighter, my makeup sits better, and I stopped using a separate brightening product. Wish the bottle were bigger for what it costs.

Okay so nobody warned me about the two week purge. Small breakouts along my cheeks, then they cleared and took some of my older marks with them. Now at month three my skin looks better than before, but brace yourself early on.

r.t: The one my clinic insisted on
r.b: Between appointments at my clinic this is the one product they insisted I keep using at home. Brightness holds steady, the fine lines on my forehead look softer, and one bottle carries me about three months using four drops a day.

Melasma across my upper lip had resisted everything short of lasers. Six months of this every morning under a mineral SPF and it is faint enough that I skip concealer most days. Nothing else changed in my routine, so the credit goes here.

Turned orange on me within six weeks, even stored in a cool dark drawer with the cap tight. At this price oxidation that fast is unacceptable. The two weeks it was fresh my skin did look brighter, which somehow makes it more frustrating.

My dermatologist pushed me toward this for two years before I caved. She was right. The 15 percent L-ascorbic acid is no joke, my forehead lines look softer and my overall tone is brighter. The amber glass bottle also keeps it stable longer than the cheaper serums I tried.
Wish I could give it four and a half. Brightness, check. Softer lines on my forehead, check. But the bottle lasted me barely ten weeks using the recommended drops, and at this price that math hurts.

Honestly it took almost two months before I noticed anything, so patience is required. Now at month four my post-blemish marks fade way faster than they used to. Slightly tacky finish for the first few minutes, which bugs me under makeup.

Age spots on my cheekbones had been multiplying for a decade. Ten months of this every morning and two of them are gone completely while the rest have softened. My only regret isn't starting at 40 instead of 61.

A little goes a long way, so despite the sticker shock a bottle lasts me a full season. Glow is real by week three. It does leave the faintest tacky feel that my bangs stick to at the gym, hence four stars.

r.t: Asked if I had work done
r.b: I was skeptical that any serum could justify this price. Then a colleague asked if I had something done. Three months of daily use, five drops each morning, and the crepiness on my cheeks has genuinely improved. Refilling forever.

Works, but so does my old drugstore vitamin C at a fifth of the price, at least on my skin. The finish is a touch oily for me and I didn't see a dramatic difference by bottle end. Maybe my expectations were inflated by the hype.

Everyone talks about the smell and yes, it is odd for a few seconds, but nobody warned me how fast the results come. Brighter by week two, smoother by week five. I store it in its box away from light and the formula stayed stable all winter.

Ran out for two weeks between bottles and watched my skin slowly go back to dull, which is the most convincing review I can give. Four stars only because the price forces those gaps in the first place.

Sun damage from thirty years in Arizona is no small thing, and this is the first product that visibly lightened the mottled patches on my cheeks. My derm confirmed the improvement at my annual check. I apply it religiously before SPF 50.

r.t: Worth every penny, four months in
r.b: Been using this every morning for four months now. Four drops after cleansing, wait a minute, then moisturizer and SPF. The watery texture sinks in fast and my sun spots from last summer have visibly faded. Yes it smells odd, sort of salty, but that disappears in seconds.

Never thought a serum could make me look forward to mornings. Four drops, a minute to sink in, then SPF. The hyperpigmentation on my cheekbones from years of skipped sunscreen has faded to almost nothing since I started in early spring.
Under makeup this behaves perfectly, no pilling, no balling up with primer, and by week four my foundation looked better because the skin under it looked better.

Gifted a bottle by my sister who works at a medspa, and I finished it convinced. My combination skin drank it up with no pilling under SPF, and by the end my chin was clear of the lingering marks from winter breakouts.

First impressions matter and this delivered in week one, the persistent dry patch on my left cheek that laughed at everything else simply faded. The texture is dense but spreads thin and even. I follow with nothing at night, it is enough on its own. Already planning the repurchase.

For mature skin this is close to perfect. The cholesterol-heavy formula makes sense for skin like mine that lost its bounce, and after roughly eight weeks my face feels padded again instead of papery. My only note is to warm it between fingers first, it spreads much easier that way.

r.t: Worth it, barely, but worth it
r.b: Pricey but I keep coming back because nothing at half the cost performs like this. It smoothed the dehydration lines on my forehead in about three weeks and sits perfectly under my tinted SPF. I dock a star because the bottle is small and I resent how quickly I fall in love with expensive things.

Took about a month before I saw anything beyond basic moisture, and I nearly gave up at week two. Glad I stuck it out. The crepiness on my cheeks softened noticeably by week five and my skin stopped drinking three layers of serum to feel normal. Slow starter, strong finisher.

Retinol users, this is the buffer you want. I apply it fifteen minutes after tretinoin and my usual week two peel simply didn't happen this cycle. The scent is faint to me, more plant than perfume. My derm confirmed it will not interfere with the retinoid. Excellent.

r.t: Sceptic to loyalist in one bottle
r.b: Skeptical at first because the marketing around lipid ratios sounded like nonsense to me. Six weeks later the persistent rough patch on my jawline that survived three other creams is gone. It goes on thick, warms into the skin, and my face feels cushioned rather than coated. I stand corrected.

r.t: The brand earned my trust again
r.b: Been using SkinCeuticals vitamin C for years but their moisturizers never tempted me until this one. It fixed the rough patches by my ears that I assumed were permanent, took maybe three weeks. Dense texture, spreads easily, faint botanical smell that vanishes. Now the two products bookend my whole routine.

Started using it after my dermatologist mentioned the lipid ratio research behind it. Results are real, less tightness, fewer flakes, smoother texture by week four. The caveat is that in summer it feels like too much for me, so it becomes a winter-only product, which makes the price harder to justify year round.

Three bottles in and I have zero interest in trying anything else. My cheeks used to feel tight an hour after cleansing, now they stay comfortable all day. I pair it with C E Ferulic in the morning and the two together made my skin look genuinely healthy for the first time in years.

Halifax winters are a damp cold that gets into your bones and apparently your face. This cream kept my skin comfortable through the whole season, no chapped patches along my jaw for the first time in years. It goes on thick, absorbs in a minute, and one bottle took me from December to March.

r.t: Only thing that calmed the itch
r.b: Nothing else calmed the itchy tight feeling I get every February, and I tried five different barrier creams this year, this one did it in four nights flat.

Works, but be warned the pump gets airy in the last fifth of the bottle and you end up shaking it like ketchup. Formula-wise it is the best barrier cream I've used, cracked winter skin healed in about a week and stayed healed. I just wish the last 10 ml were easier to extract.

Expensive, yes, and I hesitate every time I reorder. But nothing else keeps my skin comfortable through an Edmonton February, and a little truly does go far, one pump does my whole face and neck. If it were 20 dollars cheaper I'd buy it without thinking. Four stars for the wallet damage only.

Second winter with this cream and it remains the only thing standing between my face and the parking lot wind tunnel at work. Absorbs fully before I leave the bathroom, never pills under sunscreen, and the slight herbal smell has honestly grown on me. Buy it when it goes on promo and stock up.

Winter in Calgary destroys my face, the dry wind cracks the skin around my mouth every year. Not this year. Two pumps at night, one in the morning under SPF, and by early December the usual rough patches never showed up. It smells a bit like lavender and something fatty, which I don't love, but the results shut me up.

Decent but I expected fireworks at this price and got a reliable candle. It moisturizes well, no irritation, no pilling, but after three months I can't point to a single dramatic change beyond soft skin, which cheaper creams also give me. If money is no object, sure. Mine is an object.

r.t: Repurchased twice, that says it all
r.b: Repurchased twice now, and I am ruthless about cutting products that coast. My barometer is how my skin handles a week of skiing, and this year I came home without the usual windburn peel. Goes on like a rich balm, finishes like a normal cream. The airless pump uses up cleanly to the last week.

Love that it comes in an airless pump instead of a jar, I refuse to buy jar moisturizers anymore after learning how fast actives degrade. The cream itself is a rich, faintly herbal-smelling cushion that fixed my winter cheek flaking in ten days. Minnesota winters are no joke and neither is this.
Rich without being greasy, absorbs in about ninety seconds, and kept my face comfortable through minus 30 windchill walks to work, second bottle already.
