If your skin is truly dry, this is the one. If you are oily, walk away, it will be far too much. I'm firmly in camp desert and it erased the ashy look I'd get by mid-afternoon. Only gripe is the pump gets stubborn near the end and I know there is product left in there I can't reach.

Smells like a herbalist's shop for the first thirty seconds, that is my one real complaint. The performance is hard to argue with, my dehydration lines plumped up within two weeks and it never once pilled under my vitamin C in the morning. By now I barely notice the scent, but it is there.

r.t: Finally got through winter without flaking
r.b: My derm recommended this after I complained about constant flaking around my nose every January. It is a thick cream but it sinks in within a minute or two, no greasy film. By week three the flaking was gone and my foundation stopped catching on dry patches. The airless pump dispenses exactly the right amount. Worth the splurge for me.

You need barely a pea-sized pump for the whole face, so don't be put off by the small bottle. Mine lasted three and a half months of nightly use. Skin feels rebuilt rather than coated, and the rough texture on my chin resolved by the one month mark. Genuinely impressive formula.

Every fall I start this up again like clockwork, usually mid-October when the furnace comes on. Within a week my skin transitions without the usual angry tight phase. I have recommended it to three coworkers and all of them repurchased. The pump design keeps it fresh to the last drop.

Great under makeup, which shocked me for something this rich. I let it sink in for five minutes, then foundation glides on and does not cling to the dry spots by my nose anymore. My mother borrowed it for a wedding weekend and immediately bought her own bottle.

Fine, I admit it, my daughter was right about this one. She put me onto it after my usual cream stopped coping with my thyroid-related dryness. Six weeks of nightly use and my face no longer feels stretched over my cheekbones by morning. The pump is tidy, the cream is rich, the results are real.

Menopause wrecked my skin barrier almost overnight, everything itched and burned. The 2 percent ceramides and 4 percent cholesterol ratio in this actually rebuilt things. It took a solid month, not overnight, but the itching stopped first, then the rough texture, then the dullness. Pricey and worth every dollar in my case.

Genuinely surprised. I'm 63 and have tried every department store cream since the eighties. This is the first one where strangers commented, a pharmacist asked what I use. Skin looks padded and calm, the deep lines are still there but everything around them looks healthier. Two pumps nightly, one every morning.

A little goes a long way, which softens the price per use math considerably. One pump covers my face and neck with a bit left for the backs of my hands. Four months on the same bottle. Skin is calmer, smoother, and my winter eczema patches beside my nose never returned this year.

At 58, my skin just stopped holding moisture on its own. This cream changed the texture of my whole face in about a month, softer, less crosshatching on my cheeks. I use it morning and night, and one bottle lasts me around ten weeks. The airless pump means no scooping cream out of a jar with fingers, hallelujah.

It melts in on contact, which I didn't expect from something that looks like frosting coming out of the pump. No residue on my pillow, no shine at my hairline. My fine lines around the eyes look softer after two months. The 48 ml lasts longer than the size suggests.

Six weeks in and the crosshatch texture on my cheeks has visibly relaxed. I take a photo of my face monthly, same light and angle, and the difference between March and May was obvious even to my husband. Two pumps at night is my sweet spot. Nothing pilled over it, ever.

r.t: Better than expected, scent is odd
r.b: Honestly wasn't expecting much beyond a fancy price tag, but my barrier was wrecked from overdoing acids and this fixed it in about two weeks. The smell is the only drawback, sort of herbal and waxy at the same time. It dissipates quickly but I notice it every single application.

r.t: Face and neck in one pump
r.b: One pump covers my face and neck if I warm it in my palms first. My neck was the real test, crepey and always irritated by fragranced creams, and this smoothed it without any reaction. Eight weeks in the improvement is obvious in photos. Buying a second bottle just for my mother.

The pump sputters and spits half doses about a third of the time, which drives me nuts at this price point. The cream itself is genuinely nice, my skin felt smoother within a couple of weeks, but I fight with the dispenser every morning. Three stars until they fix the hardware.

Used it nightly for two months before writing this. Fine lines around my mouth are softer, the crepey texture on my cheeks is smoother, and I haven't had a single dry patch since starting. It plays nicely over serums and never pills, even when I'm impatient and layer too fast.

Cannot get behind the smell, full stop. It reads medicinal and fatty to me and it lingers just long enough to bother me every night. I also developed two tiny milia under my eyes by week three. Texture and moisture were genuinely good, but between the scent and the bumps I gave it away.

The 2:4:2 ratio sounded like marketing until I read the research my derm sent me. Whatever the mechanism, my skin is measurably less flaky and the fine lines around my mouth have softened over two months. It absorbs faster than creams half as rich. Genuine science in a pump bottle.

r.t: Slow burn but it convinced me
r.b: On the fence for the first three weeks because at altitude my skin is a special kind of parched and this seemed merely fine. Around week four something shifted, smoother forehead, no more flaking eyebrows. I still think the pump wastes a little product when it sputters, but the cream earned its fourth star.

Bought this after a facialist raved about the 2:4:2 lipid ratio. It does what it promises, my cheeks stopped feeling tight by the second week, and it layers beautifully under sunscreen. Knocking a star because the price for 48 ml stings and I go through a pump and a half per use in winter.

r.t: Too heavy for my combo skin
r.b: Not for me at all. My cheeks liked it but my T-zone revolted, clogged pores across my forehead within two weeks even using a single pump at night only. I get that it is designed for dry, mature skin, but I wish I had known how occlusive it feels before spending this much. Returned what was left.

Post-menopausal skin in a desert climate is a brutal combination and this handles it. I apply on damp skin after a hyaluronic serum and stay comfortable through 40 degree days in air conditioning. Texture improvement showed around week five. My aesthetician spotted the change before I said anything.

Heavy. Too heavy for anyone with functioning oil glands, in my opinion. I bought it for winter and even then it left me shiny by noon. My mother has classic dry mature skin and it looks incredible on her, so I handed it over. Know your skin type before spending this much.

After my Fraxel session my derm told me to use something bland and lipid-heavy while healing. This was gentler than the plain drugstore cream I tried first, no sting on raw skin, and the tight shiny feeling eased within days. I kept using it after healing because my skin has honestly never looked better.

r.t: Fixed my patches, mind the amount
r.b: Dry patches around my nostrils and between my brows disappeared within two weeks, which no ceramide cream from the drugstore ever managed. Word of caution, more isn't better. When I got generous with three pumps I woke up with a slightly congested chin. One pump, thin layer, perfection.

This cream saved my face after I got greedy with glycolic acid and burned my barrier. Everything stung, even water. Two weeks of this morning and night, nothing else except sunscreen, and my skin calmed completely. It has earned a permanent spot even now that things are healed.

r.t: Like a lipid smoothie for your face
r.b: The texture reminds me of softened butter that melts on contact, thick out of the pump but it spreads thin and disappears. I sandwich it around tretinoin nights and my peeling stopped almost completely within ten days. My esthetician noticed the difference before I told her I switched.

Since starting tretinoin last fall my skin was in open rebellion until this arrived. I do a thin layer before and after on heavy nights. Peeling stopped, redness faded, and I kept every bit of the retinoid progress. The fatty acids and cholesterol do the repair work while the tret does the renovation.

I broke out along my chin the first two weeks, small closed comedones that I never get normally. Backed off to every other night and it settled, and to be fair my skin does feel less tight now. I want to love it given what I paid, but I am watching my chin like a hawk.

r.t: Works great, smells like a health store
r.b: There is a scent, and nobody warned me. Kind of herbal, kind of like plant oils, definitely noticeable for the first minute. Past that, the cream itself is outstanding, my flaky chin cleared up in under two weeks and makeup sits better. If you are scent-sensitive, sample first.

Was gifted a sample at a medspa appointment and used it for five nights. That was enough. Bought the full size before the sample ran out. My cheeks stopped looking gray and tired, and blush sits on smooth skin now instead of catching on dry bits. No irritation whatsoever on my reactive skin.

r.t: The one my skin waits for
r.b: This is the first moisturizer that actually repaired my barrier instead of just sitting on top of it. I use one pump at night over my retinol and the stinging I used to get is gone. Skin looks plumper, less crepey around my jaw after about six weeks. The scent is herbal and takes getting used to, but it fades fast.

r.t: Calmed my reactive skin right down
r.b: I have rosacea-prone skin and most rich creams make me flush. This one is loaded with ceramides and cholesterol instead of fragrance-heavy fillers, and my redness actually settled after a couple of weeks of nightly use. No stinging, no clogged pores. The pump keeps everything hygienic, which I appreciate.

Layered over my retinol as the last step, this stopped the dryness and irritation that made me quit retinoids twice before. It is thick enough to buffer but never blocks the active from working, my texture kept improving. Two months in, the corners of my mouth no longer crack in the morning.

r.t: Cheeks love it, T-zone tolerates it
r.b: Combination skin here, so I use it on cheeks and jaw only and skip my nose and forehead. Used that way it is excellent, no more flaky cheekbones and my redness is down. Applied all over it was too rich and I got a couple of small bumps. Zone application is the trick.

Started this last spring and my photos from back then are startling now. The horizontal lines on my forehead are half as deep, and my skin bounces back when I press it, which it didn't do at 61. I stay religious about sunscreen over it since even low-dose retinol deserves respect.

Seventy this year and still vain, thankfully. This serum has given my cheeks back some spring and faded the blotchiness that crept in over the last decade. My daughter applies it for me on days my hands are stiff, and even she noticed the change. We call it my expensive habit.

Very good serum, real results on the fine lines around my mouth after about ten weeks. My only complaints are the price, which stings at renewal, and that the last few pumps sputter and spray unevenly. I'll repurchase, probably during a sale.

Works, genuinely. Cheeks firmer, tone brighter, fine lines quieter after three months. But at two pumps twice daily the bottle empties in about six weeks, and the cost per month is hard to swallow. I have scaled back to one pump at night and the results are holding.
One pump covers my face and neck if I move fast, and after three months of firmer, brighter skin it has become the single product I'd never cut from the budget.

Everything firming I tried before triggered a flush. This hasn't, not once in five months. My cheeks are noticeably tighter and the burning feeling I get from most actives simply never happened. I apply it to fully dry skin and wait a minute before moisturizer, as my derm suggested.

Perfectly pleasant serum that did perfectly average things for my skin. Slightly smoother texture after two months, maybe a touch brighter. For this money I wanted more than maybe. The quick-drying gel and the precise pump are the best parts.

Compared honestly against a growth factor serum costing nearly double, this held its own and then some. Skin is firmer at the cheekbones, tone is more even, and the metered pump wastes nothing. I apply it after my vitamin C in the morning with no conflict.

Through an Edmonton February this needed a rich cream over top or my skin felt stripped by morning. Spring and fall it is perfect alone under SPF. The firming earned it a permanent spot regardless. Just know what it is, a treatment step, despite a price that suggests it should do everything.

Years of messy droppers made me appreciate this precise airless pump more than I expected. The serum itself has kept its promises, firmer cheeks by week eight, softer eye lines by week twelve. I warm one pump between my fingers and press it in at night before my heavier cream.

Splurged on this last Valentine's Day and just reordered on the exact same date a year later, which tells you everything. Softer expression lines, brighter tone, fastest-absorbing serum I have owned. My only wish is a travel size.

Sixty-two years old and my barber asked what I was doing differently. Two pumps at night, that is all. It absorbs before I hit the pillow and I've had none of the peeling I remember from prescription retinoids years ago.

Full coverage foundation is a job requirement for me and most serums ruin it. This sets to a smooth base with zero pilling, even over primer. Twelve weeks in, I actually need less foundation because my tone has evened out. That is the real win.

Tingles slightly for the first minute, nothing unbearable, but after three full months I can only say my skin looks marginally brighter. No change in firmness that I can detect. It may work better for others, but at this price I expected more than marginal.

Retired teacher, 66, never used a serum in my life until my daughter set me up with this one. The frown line between my brows has softened enough that people say I look less stern. Simple to use, no smell, dries fast. That is all I ask.

Bought this for my mom last Christmas and she talks about it more than the trip we gave her. She says her face feels firmer when she does her morning massage and her creams glide on better. Ordering her a refill this year plus one for myself.

This replaced both my peptide serum and my beginner retinol, which almost justifies the sticker shock. Texture is a clear gel that sets to a soft velvet finish in about ninety seconds. Four months in, the lines across my forehead have gone from obvious to faint.

Alberta winters usually mean flaky cheeks by December no matter what I do. This year, with this serum morning and night, nothing flaked. Skin stayed smooth and the lines by my eyes kept fading. Even my skeptical sister borrowed a few pumps and then ordered her own bottle.

Tone improvement came quickly, five weeks maybe, and my dark patches from summer faded well. Firming has been subtler, more of a squint-and-see-it change at month three. Still happy overall. If firmness is your only goal, give it more time than I have or look elsewhere.

Crepiness on my cheeks has bothered me for years. After roughly ten weeks of this twice a day, my skin looks smoother in daylight, which is the harshest test there is. No fragrance, no sting, just a faint tightening feel as the gel sets. The pump gets full marks from my arthritic hands.

Cleanser, this, sunscreen. That is my entire morning and it works better than the ten-step routine I abandoned. Skin is firmer through the cheeks and my smile lines have relaxed. The pump dispenses the same amount every time, which I did not know I needed until now.

On its own this left my dry skin feeling tight within an hour, so it is strictly a middle step for me, never the last one. That said, the firming is legit. My nasolabial folds look less pronounced after three months and the tone across my cheeks is more uniform. Wish the bottle were bigger for the price.

Uneven patches on my cheeks have faded noticeably since I added this in the summer. Not gone, but makeup is optional now on good days. It layers under SPF without pilling, and the plant growth factors agree with my skin far more than the stronger retinol I tried before.

Picked this up on my clinic's advice while healing from microneedling and never stopped. The plant growth factors are supposedly the star, and something is clearly working because my skin looks denser, for lack of a better word. No scent, no sting, dries fast. One pump does my whole face.

r.t: Broke me out along the chin
r.b: Gave it six weeks and got small closed comedones along my chin and jaw the whole time. They cleared within two weeks of stopping, so I am confident it was this. Texture and pump are lovely, and I know acne-prone skin is picky, but I can't use it.

Three bottles deep and the improvements haven't plateaued. The marks left from old breakouts keep fading and the lines on my forehead are basically invisible in normal lighting. For anyone on the fence, commit to ten weeks minimum before you judge it.

Whatever they did with this texture, it is perfect. Thin gel, sets quickly, and then moisturizer and sunscreen glide over it without a single pill. After four months my cheeks look plumper and the vertical lines above my lip catch less lipstick. Worth the splurge for me.

Vacation photos used to be a reality check. This year my face looked as good in candid shots as it does in my bathroom mirror, and this serum is the only thing that changed since last summer. Two pumps every morning, sunscreen over top, done.

Most anti-aging serums sit on my oily skin like a film. This one is a thin gel that absorbs completely, so I can wear it in the morning without turning greasy by noon. Improvement in the lines around my eyes is modest after ten weeks, hence four stars, but it fits my routine perfectly.

First pump of the day always comes out half-sized, so I do a small priming press before applying. Minor annoyance on an otherwise excellent serum. Real firming through my mid-face after about two months, and it has never pilled under my mineral sunscreen.

The serum itself was fine, mildly hydrating with subtle results, but the airless pump started sputtering air about halfway in and I never got the rest out, even after storing it upside down and tapping it for days. For over two hundred dollars that isn't acceptable.

Honestly, the feel of this gel is what keeps me coming back. It melts in like water, sets inside a minute, and everything on top applies flawlessly. The firming and tone results arrived around week nine as a bonus. My mother now steals pumps whenever she visits.

Nothing happened for the first six weeks and I nearly returned it. Somewhere around week eight my tone started evening out and the fine lines on my forehead softened. Month five now and I'm glad I stuck it out, though the slow start and the price keep this at four stars.

Hydrating enough for summer, nowhere near enough for a Portland winter, so I sandwich it between a hydrating toner and a heavy cream from November on. The firming gains are real though. My jaw looks cleaner in profile photos than it did in spring. A star off for the small bottle at this cost.

Gentle enough that I keep forgetting it contains retinol at all. Changes came slowly, brightness first around week four, then firmness closer to week ten. I'd love a larger size, because the small bottle disappears quickly when you use it twice a day.

r.t: The snake peptide is not a gimmick
r.b: SYN-AKE sounded like pure marketing to me. Snake venom peptide, sure, whatever you say. Ten weeks later the elevens between my brows are visibly softer when I frown at the mirror. Two pumps every morning before sunscreen, absorbed in under a minute. Eating my words.

I run the extra half pump down my neck, and the crepiness there has improved more than I expected, arguably more than my face. Fourteen weeks in. Zero smell, zero sting, dries matte. The clinic that recommended it has since heard from three of my friends.

r.t: Skin looks rested, I am not
r.b: New baby, no sleep, and yet people keep telling me I look well. This serum morning and night is doing the heavy lifting. It absorbs before the baby starts crying again, which is exactly the speed I need. Softer lines around my eyes by month two.

Desert air destroys my skin and this holds the line. I keep it in the fridge and the cool gel in the morning is my favorite step of the day. Firmness along my jaw is noticeably better since March and my makeup sits smoother. The airless pump also means it never goes funky in the heat.

Twelve weeks, the medspa said, before judging it. At exactly twelve weeks I compared selfies and the difference in my forehead lines was obvious enough to show my husband. It never stung, never pilled, never smelled like anything. Rebuying without hesitation.

Took a solid two months to see anything, which tested my patience at this price. The texture is a light watery gel with barely any scent, and it sinks in fast. My forehead lines are softer now and my wife noticed before I did. Four stars because the airless pump gives no clue how much is left.

After an IPL session my clinic told me to use this while I healed, and the redness settled faster than my previous round without it. I kept going, and three months later my tone is the most even it has been in a decade. The low-dose retinol has never once irritated me.

Florida humidity makes most anti-aging products slide off my face by ten in the morning. This gel absorbs completely and stays put. Pores along my cheeks look tighter and the early elevens between my brows have smoothed out since spring. Slightly tacky for the first minute, then perfect.

At 58 my main issue is sagging, not spots. Three months of morning and evening use and my cheeks hold their shape better, the crepey texture on my chin is smoother, and I've had zero flaking despite the retinol in it. It sits nicely under my night cream too. Costly but earning its keep.

Every retinol product before this gave me at least one rough month. This one, nothing, presumably because the dose is low and the growth factors carry the load. Crow's feet are visibly finer and my cheeks feel denser. Nightly for me, moisturizer after, sunscreen always the next morning.

Results are real, my tone is more even after two months, but the finish stays slightly sticky no matter how long I wait and my foundation grabs onto it. Fine for evenings, frustrating for mornings. I only use it at night now, which at least makes the bottle last longer.

Waited five full minutes after applying and my skin still felt tacky, every single time. Some people won't care. I couldn't get past it, especially under sunscreen in the morning. Skin did look a bit firmer by the end of the bottle, so three stars instead of two.

Zero fuss. Wash face, two pumps, done in thirty seconds, no smell, nothing shiny on my skin at the office. Six months later the creases by my eyes are softer and I don't look tired even when I am. First skincare product I've ever finished and rebought.

The gel texture surprised me, it sets almost powdery so my sunscreen goes right over it five minutes later. I'm on my second bottle now. The elevens between my brows are still there but they've stopped deepening, and the snake venom peptide thing I rolled my eyes at seems to be doing something after all. You need patience, nothing visible happened for the first month.

Shaving already irritates my skin, so I wanted something low effort. Light gel, invisible finish, no scent lingering at my beard line, and no flare-ups since starting. Tone improved fast, firming came slower. One star off because the opaque bottle ran out without warning on a business trip.

My derm suggested this when I said stronger retinols wreck me. Two pumps at night under moisturizer, and by week six the skin along my jaw looked firmer in photos. The gel dries down in about a minute and has never pilled under sunscreen. Expensive, but I am on my third bottle.

No fireworks, no purge, no drama. Just steadily better skin over three months, firmer through the cheeks, brighter overall, smaller-looking pores beside my nose. The gel is weightless and the airless pump keeps every dose fresh to the last. This is what premium should feel like.

Retinol products usually leave me red and flaky within a week. The low-dose retinol in here, buffered by the growth factors I suppose, has caused zero problems in four months. Fine lines at the corners of my eyes are shallower and my cheeks feel bouncier. It layers cleanly over my hyaluronic serum at night.

Absorbs like water and leaves nothing behind, which my oily T-zone appreciates. The change in fine lines is there but modest after three months. If you want a pleasant, sensible anti-aging serum, this is it. If you want dramatic overnight change, temper expectations.

Skeptical doesn't begin to describe how I felt spending this much on a small pump bottle. But my frown lines are shallower, my skin looks less dull, and I stopped feeling silly about the purchase somewhere around week seven.

r.t: Jawline bumps gone by month two
r.b: Chin and jawline texture cleared by month two, which two years of exfoliating acids never managed. Lightweight for a night cream, no clogged pores, no scent. I keep the travel size in my gym bag and the full pump at home. Do not skip morning sunscreen, it will remind you.

Smoother forehead, smaller-looking pores, and my foundation stopped clinging to dry patches because there are none left. Four months in, applying every other night after cleansing, waiting twenty minutes, then moisturizer. The routine matters with this one but the payoff is real.

Expect the flake phase and plan around it, I peeled around my nose for two weeks straight. After that, smooth sailing and genuinely smoother skin. Wear your SPF, this makes you burn faster if you get lazy.

Honestly shocked. I assumed nothing over the counter would touch my old 0.05% tret, but the finish on my skin is smoother with less irritation. Bisabolol must be doing real work. Also the airless bottle means the last dose is as fresh as the first.

Real results without a fourteen-step routine. Cleanser, this, moisturizer, done. My cheeks stopped looking rough under foundation around week six, and the fine lines under my eyes (I keep it just below the orbital bone) have plumped out. The compact airless bottle travels well too.
Absolute staple now. Everything else on my shelf rotates, this stays. Twelve months of use, two bottles, visibly smoother skin and softer lines in every recent photo.

By week four I caught my reflection in daylight and did an actual double take. The rough patches along my jaw were gone. This is a proper clinical retinol, not a gentle beginner cream, and it behaves like one in the best way.

Not convinced this suits acne-prone skin. I purged for almost five weeks, longer than any product I have used, and while the texture afterward was decent, several purge spots left marks I'm still fading. The cream itself is elegant and the pump is great. Proceed carefully if you break out easily.

Gentler than expected for the strength. I credit the bisabolol because my usually dramatic skin only protested for one week. Tone is more even and the crepiness on my cheeks has eased. Four stars because a bottle this size should last longer than three months of nightly use.

Happy overall. Just know this is a twelve-week product, not a two-week product. My texture change only became obvious when I compared photos from day one. Cream is silky, pump is precise, price is ouch.

Six months in. The etched lines between my brows are softer, my cheeks have a bounce again, and makeup stopped settling into the creases around my mouth. I started every third night and now do five nights a week with no flaking. Worth every dollar of a not-small price.

Post-40 skin drinks this in. The cream feels almost lightweight but works overnight like something much richer. My smile lines are softer, the texture on my chin is gone, and I haven't had a single flake since week three. The pump dispenses a perfect pea every time.

Wish the bottle were bigger for the money, mine lasted about eleven weeks of near-nightly use. Performance isn't in question, my skin texture is the smoothest it has been since my twenties. Just budget for it like a phone bill.

Winter in Edmonton usually means I quit retinol until April. This one, buffered over a hyaluronic serum, made it through minus thirty windchill without cracking me. The lines by my mouth are softer and my skin feels denser somehow. Genuinely impressed.

The airless pump alone puts this above half the retinols I've tried, no air exposure and no digging fingers into a jar. Cream is surprisingly light for 0.5% and my oily skin never felt suffocated. Pores along my nose look tighter after two months.

This replaced my separate peptide serum and my old retinol in one go. The ZCORE peptide and 0.5% retinol combo seems to do the work of both, and my routine went from six steps to four. Skin is smoother, less flaky, and my forehead lines are fading gradually.

Tiny amounts of this go remarkably far, which softens the sticker shock a little. Half a pump covers face and neck. At month five my neck crepe has smoothed and the marionette lines are shallower. It has a faint clean smell that vanishes in seconds.

Good results, slow arrival. Roughly eight weeks before the bumpy texture on my chin cleared up. The cream layers well under my night moisturizer without pilling, and the pump dispenses the same amount every time. Four stars only because the price stings on repurchase.

Two pumps was my mistake on night one, and my forehead glowed red for days. Restarted with a half pump twice a week and it has been fantastic since. Oily skin here and the lightweight cream never clogs. Old chin scarring has faded more in three months than in three years.

Pea-sized amount, seriously, that is all you need. I made the rookie mistake of two pumps the first night and paid for it with a shiny red forehead. Used correctly this has smoothed my texture and faded some old acne marks over four months. Bottle is lasting way longer than expected.

r.t: A decade of retinols, this won
r.b: Been using retinol for a decade, prescription and otherwise, and this is the one I keep returning to. The 0.5% strength hits the sweet spot between results and livability. Texture on my nose and the lines across my forehead have both improved without the constant shedding tret gave me.

Crow's feet are the one thing I stopped photographing around, and after four months of this they are noticeably shallower. I keep it a centimetre away from my lash line and let it migrate. The cream is rich enough that some nights I skip moisturizer entirely.

Combined with my morning vitamin C and daily SPF 50, this has been the backbone of a routine that finally shows in photos. No pilling, no fighting with other products, and desert air has not made it feel drying. Ten weeks for visible line softening on my forehead.

At 58 I figured my texture was permanent. Four months of this three nights a week and the crosshatching on my cheeks has visibly relaxed. I pair it with a ceramide cream and have had zero peeling since the second week. My aesthetician noticed before I told her.

Stopped using it after eight weeks. Constant flaking across my cheeks no matter how slowly I ramped, how much I buffered, or how heavy my night cream was. Some skin just can't do 0.5% and mine is apparently on that list. The pump and texture are lovely, which makes it more frustrating.

Took a full three months before I'd have written five stars, so wait it out. Early on there was tightness and some peeling along my jaw. Now my skin is smoother than it was at 35 and I am 44. One pump lasts two nights if I'm careful.

Every review said start slow and they were right. Twice a week for a month, then three times, now nightly. Mild flaking at the start, nothing since. Around week nine my smile lines looked softer and my skin tone got more even. This is the first retinol I have actually finished a bottle of.

You need patience with this one. Weeks one through three, nothing but a little peeling. Weeks four through eight, hmm, maybe something. Week twelve, my brother asked why I looked less tired. It compounds quietly and then all at once.

Forehead lines I've had since my thirties look shallower after about ten weeks. Nothing dramatic week to week, then one morning the bathroom light was kinder. A small dab, three nights a week, SPF religiously every morning.

Just okay for me after four months. Some smoothing on my forehead, sure, but my drugstore retinal did similar for a third of the price. No irritation at least, and the pump is nice. I expected more at this tier.
No scent, no greasy film, no pilling under anything I layer on top. It just quietly resurfaces your skin while you sleep. Ten weeks in, my wife asked if I had something done.

Skeptical at first because ZO prices feel like a dare. Ten weeks later the orange-peel texture on my cheeks is nearly gone and the little bumps on my forehead cleared. I get why people stay loyal. Small amount at night, thick moisturizer after, sunscreen always.

Purged for ten days along my chin, which I expected from a real retinol, and then my skin settled into the clearest stretch I've had in two years. Texture from old breakouts keeps improving month over month. Minus one star for the purge and the price together.

Decent retinol but I struggle with the value. My insurance covers tretinoin for a fraction of this price and the results feel comparable. The cream itself is nice, lightweight, no pilling under moisturizer. If you can't get a prescription this makes sense, otherwise do the math.
Halfway through my first bottle and already ordered the next. Smoother skin, faded sun damage on my temples, zero pilling under sunscreen the next morning. Ramp up slowly and this thing delivers.

I switched from prescription tretinoin because the constant peeling got old. This 0.5% gives me maybe eighty percent of the result with a tenth of the drama. At 61 my texture is the best it has been in years. The airless pump is also far more sanitary than my old tube that always crusted at the cap.

Almost five stars. Results are excellent, softer lines and glowier skin by month two. But dry skin friends, you will need a serious moisturizer on top, this on its own left me tight by morning. That extra required step is my only gripe.
Works, but pricey enough that I hesitate at every repurchase. Results are real, softer lines and brighter tone by month two. If ZO ever runs a sale, stock up, because full price makes my eye twitch.

Nice texture and a genuinely effective retinol, but Edmonton winter plus 0.5% is a battle. I had to drop to twice weekly with a heavy cream on top from November to February. Summer usage is smooth sailing and my skin looks fresher overall.

Mostly great. Post-acne texture on my cheeks has smoothed out over three months and new breakouts are rarer. One star off because the initial purge brought back memories I didn't need, about three weeks of it.

Started slow, twice a week with a layer of moisturizer underneath, and even then I got a bit pink through week three. Sticking with it because my skin looks more even and the pump keeps everything hygienic. Sensitive types should really pace themselves with this one.

Four stars because the first month tested me. Stinging on application for the initial few uses, brief flake around my mouth. Month two onward it has been smooth, literally. My redness-prone skin now tolerates nightly use, which surprised me. Wish they included clearer ramp-up instructions in the box.

My dermatologist recommended this after I complained tretinoin was wrecking my barrier. The 0.5% retinol with the bisabolol in here is noticeably kinder. Fine lines around my eyes softened by month two and dry Calgary winters have not cracked me yet.

Texture on my cheeks was my white whale, tiny bumps that no acid ever fully cleared. Eight weeks of this at three nights a week and they are basically gone. Absorbs quickly, plays fine under my ceramide moisturizer, and one pump does my whole face with a bit left for my neck.

Middle of the road for me. Texture improved a little by month two but so did it with cheaper retinols I've used. No irritation, no drama, just not the wow everyone promised. The peptide claims did not translate to anything I could see in the mirror.

First proper retinol I have used and probably ruined for anything weaker. Started at 45 with forehead lines and rough cheeks, and both are meaningfully better at the four month mark. The instructions inside the box are actually useful, follow the slow build they describe.

Bought this after microneedling on my medspa's advice, waited the two weeks, then eased in. It has kept the smoothness from my treatments going instead of letting it fade. The cream absorbs in under a minute and has basically no smell, which my migraine-prone self appreciates.

Never thought packaging would sell me on a skincare product, but after my last retinol oxidized to orange in a jar, the airless pump here is the standard I hold everything to. Product performs too, my forehead texture is noticeably tighter after twelve weeks.

Strong stuff. I flaked around my mouth for the first two weeks even at every third night. Once my skin adjusted, the texture on my forehead improved noticeably. Docking a star because there is no smaller intro size to test before committing to the price.

Way too harsh for me even buffered over moisturizer once a week. Red, stinging patches on my cheeks that took a month to calm down after I stopped. The bisabolol wasn't enough for my reactive skin. Beautiful results for my sister though, so it is clearly skin dependent.

Three weeks in and my cheeks feel like they were sanded smooth, in a good way. One small press of the pump covers my whole face. Slight flaking around my nose in week two, so I sandwiched it between moisturizer layers and it settled. No scent, sinks in fast.
Second bottle. That is the whole review, really. Nothing else has earned a repurchase at this price, and my forehead is why.

On my third bottle now. My esthetician swears she can tell when clients use this consistently, and looking at my before photos from last spring, so can I. Lines, texture, and the dull cast are all better. Nightly use, small dose, thick cream on top.

After six weeks the crepey texture on my forehead is honestly hard to find. I use it Sunday, Tuesday, Thursday nights over dry skin, moisturizer fifteen minutes later. My wife started stealing it, which says more than I can.

Solid but the first three weeks were rough, flaking around my nostrils and chin no matter how much I buffered. Once through it, texture and old breakout marks improved a lot. Knock a star for the adjustment period nobody at the counter warned me about.

Decent bump in firmness by week eight and a very noticeable glow almost immediately. The reason for four stars instead of five is purely value, my wallet cries at every repurchase. If it were a quarter cheaper this would be an automatic staple.

Post-microneedling, my clinic recommended this to support collagen while I healed, and my results from the same procedure looked better than the previous year without it. Kept it in the routine ever since. Gentle and silky, no sting even on freshly needled skin.

r.t: Most effective serum in twenty years
r.b: Hands down the most effective serum I've used in twenty years of trying everything. The TNS growth factors plus the peptides do something for sag that my retinol alone never did. One pump, morning, then sunscreen. That is the whole trick.

r.t: Skeptic to believer in six months
r.b: Half a year of daily use. Deep smile lines softened, skin looks visibly thicker (I even bruise less), and the snake-oil skepticism I started with is gone. The lotion itself is featherweight with almost no smell once it dries down.

Wanted to love it unreservedly, but my breakout-prone T-zone went through a two week purge before things settled. Once it calmed down, my tone evened out and the fine lines by my eyes softened. Start slow if you are acne-prone.

r.t: Bought a backup at full price
r.b: Ordered during a points event and figured worst case I would return it. Eight weeks later I ordered a backup at full price. Smile lines softer, skin looks thicker, and it hasn't broken me out once.

Her skin sold me before the ingredient list did. My esthetician has used TNS for years and glows like a lamp. The growth factor blend sounds like science fiction, but the firmness through my cheeks after four months is very much science fact.

Mine dispensed almost entirely from one chamber, so who knows what ratio of growth factors to peptides I was actually getting, and support just told me to keep pumping. It also pilled over my moisturizer no matter the order. Beautiful promises, frustrating execution.

r.t: Slower than advertised, still worth it
r.b: Texture is gorgeous and the glow is immediate, but the deeper structural changes took a full four months to show for me, longer than the two weeks the marketing implies. Set your expectations accordingly and you will end up as happy as I am.

At 58 with thin, dry skin, most anti-aging serums either sting or sit on top doing nothing. This one absorbs in about thirty seconds and my cheeks look plumper by mid-morning. Three bottles in, and my esthetician noticed the change before I told her.

There's a learning curve with the dose. Two full pumps left a tacky film that pilled under sunscreen, while half that amount absorbs clean. Once I figured that out, smooth sailing and smoother skin. Week ten and my forehead lines have faded.

Nothing dramatic to report after twelve weeks, and I used it exactly as directed, one pump each morning on clean skin. Hydrating, pleasant, elegant texture, but for this money I need visible line reduction and I didn't get it. My derm says give it six months. Undecided on a second bottle.

Been on my third bottle since fall and the difference in my progress photos is honestly startling. The sagging along my jaw has tightened up, and the vitamin E in the formula seems to keep my flaky patches away through a Winnipeg winter.

Combined with monthly dermaplaning, this serum gave me the best skin of my forties. It absorbs completely in under a minute, no residue, the faintest sweet scent, and the firmness gains kept building from week six onward.
Worth every penny for me. Dullness lifted, skin bounces back when I press it, and it layers perfectly between my vitamin C and sunscreen without a single pill.

Used it religiously morning and night for sixteen weeks after my dermatologist recommended it for early jowling. The heaviness along my jaw looks lifted and my foundation stopped settling into the lines around my mouth.

r.t: Month three is when it clicks
r.b: It took a full ten weeks to earn five stars from me. The early hydration glow is nice, but the firmness along the jawline is the real payoff, and that arrives slowly. Patience plus one pump nightly.

Late fifties, rosacea-prone, and terrified of actives. This has never once flushed me. Over five months the crepe on my cheeks smoothed out and my flare-ups haven't worsened. I layer it under a bland rich cream at night.

Not going to lie, I gasped at checkout. But a bottle lasts me a solid three months using one pump daily, and the smoothing around my mouth is real. Wish the pump gave a smaller dose option so I could stretch it further.

For the price I wanted fireworks and got a polite golf clap. My skin is smoother and hydrated, sure, but a good peptide moisturizer at a third of the cost did similar things for me. If money is no object, go ahead.

Can't say enough about what this did for my post-menopause skin. The thin, papery texture on my cheeks now looks cushioned. I pair it with a hyaluronic hydrator and the combo carries me through an Edmonton winter.

So the pump intimidated me at first, two chambers, one dose, but it is foolproof in practice. What sold me was week seven, when the vertical lines on my upper lip looked visibly shallower. Nothing else has ever touched those.

You mix the two chambers as you pump, which felt gimmicky until I read about keeping the growth factors and the Progeline peptides stable separately. Whatever the science, my skin is firmer at 62 than it was at 58. AM and PM, one pump each.

Repurchased four times now, which for me is unheard of. It plays nicely with my retinol at night, never stings, never clogs my pores, and the airless-style pump keeps everything fresh nearly to the end.

Six weeks in and the crepiness on my neck has softened enough that I stopped wearing scarves on Zoom calls. I pat it on after cleansing, PM only, then seal it with a rich moisturizer. No irritation, no pilling.

Was gifted a bottle for my 60th and it has ruined me for anything cheaper. The dual-chamber pump mixes a fresh dose each time, and the resulting lotion absorbs fast and has made my skin visibly denser and springier over four months.

Just finished bottle number one. Verdict: real smoothing on my forehead and crow's feet, a subtle lift by the jaw, and a texture I look forward to using. Minus one star because the final week of product required unscrewing the top and scraping. At this price, every drop matters.

If you're on the fence, track your progress with photos. I saw nothing in the mirror day to day, but the side-by-side at week eight shocked me. Nasolabial folds are shallower and my tone is more even.

Honestly the results crept up on me. Nothing at week two, a little at week six, then at three months I caught my reflection and my cheeks looked lifted. Four stars only because the last quarter of the bottle is a struggle to pump out.

Underwhelmed after all the hype. Three months of consistent morning use and I can't point to a single change beyond basic hydration. The sour smell on application never stopped bothering me either. Returned my second bottle unopened.

Between this and my sunscreen, people guess I'm ten years younger. I am 63. The serum feels like a light silky lotion, sinks in fast, and the firmness through my cheeks built gradually over about three months.

r.t: Glad my medspa had a promo
r.b: Okay, confession, I only bought it because my medspa ran a promo. Two months later my pores look tighter and my cheeks have that bounce back when I poke them. The dispenser wastes product if you pump too fast, so press slowly.

Bought this after my sister wouldn't shut up about it. Fine, she was right. Forehead lines noticeably shallower by the second month, and the texture is lovely, like a cushiony gel-cream hybrid once the two sides mix out of the pump.

Something about this serum makes my whole face look rested even on four hours of sleep. I assume that is the peptide side, because the effect shows within an hour of applying. The long-term firmness gains are slower but very real.

On my second bottle and fully converted from a much cheaper peptide serum. The difference is in the bounce, my skin springs back now instead of creasing. Apply to clean dry skin, wait a minute, then moisturizer. Don't skip the wait.

The smell is my main issue. I know the growth factors are the culprit and it does dissipate, but every application starts with a whiff of something sour. Results were decent, mild smoothing at two months, just not enough to overlook the sensory experience at this price.

Fine lines around my mouth were my white whale. Retinol helped a little, lasers helped more, but this serum kept the improvement going between treatments. Three months in, the lines are soft enough that I'm skipping filler this round.

r.t: Subtle at best for the money
r.b: Gave this an honest five months and the improvement was subtle at best. Slightly smoother forehead, maybe. For nearly four hundred dollars Canadian I expected more than maybe. The texture and pump are lovely, which is why it gets three stars and not two.
Wish the bottle were bigger, that is my only real gripe. Performance-wise it firmed my neck and blurred the horizontal lines there in about nine weeks. I ration pumps like a dragon hoarding gold.

Pricey, yes, but I have chased firmness for a decade and this is the first thing that visibly lifted my lower face. One pump every morning under moisturizer, and the results showed up around week five and kept building.

Every morning, one pump, over a year now. My before and after photos convinced two coworkers to buy it. Deep forehead lines are maybe forty percent softer and the skin under my eyes stopped crinkling when I smile. Zero irritation the entire time.
After my facelift consult I decided to try this first. Eight months later I cancelled the consult. Not kidding.
Keeping this short. Fifty-four years old, combination skin, twelve weeks of daily use, and the marionette lines are visibly softer in photos. Nothing else changed in my routine.

Third week update that turned into a permanent review: the glow arrived early and stayed. On dry Calgary mornings I press a drop of HA serum over it and everything sits perfectly under mineral SPF, zero pilling.
A splurge I don't regret, mostly. Firmer neck and brighter cheeks by week ten. The nozzle clogs if I go more than a day between uses, which is a silly flaw on a serum this expensive.

r.t: One pump covers face and neck
r.b: Two pumps sounds like a lot but honestly one is plenty for face and neck. Goes on like a light lotion, no pilling under my mineral sunscreen. My 11s are softer after two months and my mom asked what I changed.

Brightness came in about two weeks, firmness closer to two months. The dual chamber pump is oddly satisfying and the mixed serum feels like silk going on. Morning after washing, then SPF over top, that is my whole routine now.

r.t: Helped the sag under my chin
r.b: Never thought a topical would touch the loose skin under my chin, but here we are. Ten weeks of one pump nightly and the sag is measurably better in my progress pics. It even calmed the redness I usually get from actives.
Love how it functions as a primer, my foundation glides over it. The actual skincare results took about six weeks, softer 11s and a tighter look through the mid-face. AM use for me, retinol at night.

I was skeptical about growth factors in a bottle, but the crepey texture on my cheeks has genuinely smoothed out since March. Docking one star because the pump started dispensing unevenly around week six, noticeably more from one chamber than the other.

Started using it post-Botox to stretch the time between appointments and it genuinely helps, I have gone from every three months to every four and a half. Knocked a star off for the scent, which is faint but odd, a bit like bread dough.

My derm put me on this after a series of microneedling sessions and I understand the hype now. The two chambers blend into a silky peach-toned lotion that sinks in before I finish brushing my teeth. Jawline looks less droopy at month three. Yes it costs a fortune. I budget for it anyway.

First growth factor serum I've tried and now I get why derms recommend the category. My skin looked rested within days and genuinely firmer within two months. The pump gives a perfect dose and the blended lotion never separates or feels greasy.

This replaced three separate serums in my routine, which almost justifies the price. Almost. Skin feels denser and my makeup sits better. The first few applications had a faintly yeasty smell that threw me, though it fades within seconds of applying.

Silky, fast-absorbing, and genuinely effective on my crepey under-eye and cheek area within about seven weeks. Four stars because the pump jams if any product dries in the nozzle. I keep a toothpick nearby, which feels absurd for a serum at this price.

r.t: Looks like eight hours of sleep
r.b: Five months of consistent use and my skin looks like I sleep eight hours, which I don't. Texture smoothed first, around week four, tone caught up by month three. A pea-sized dot spreads well. Just wish they sold a bigger tube.

Ok so I have rosacea-prone skin and had accepted that retinoids were off the table for me. My derm suggested this because of the built-in niacinamide. Four months in, no flare-ups, and the bumpy texture on my chin is finally smooth.

Nothing dramatic to report after four months. Skin feels a touch smoother and my chin bumps are fewer, but the forehead lines I bought it for have not budged. It is a nice, gentle night cream. At this price I wanted more than nice.

Layered under a plain ceramide cream this has been perfection for my dry, reactive skin. I gave the first tube six months before judging and the verdict is smoother cheeks, softer eye-area lines, and a calmer face overall. Repurchased without hesitation.

Pricey, but it does what my dermatologist promised. I alternate nights with a peptide cream and my skin has stayed calm through the whole Ontario winter. If the tube were bigger I would give five stars, I run through one in about ten weeks.

Retinol newbie here and this was a painless introduction. Started twice weekly like the insert says, nightly by month two. My skin never once flaked, which my friends on tretinoin cannot believe. Pores look smaller and makeup sits better.

For mature skin this is the sweet spot between prescription strength and doing nothing. My crepey cheeks have firmed up over five months and the sun damage from years of sailing has faded. I won't be without it now.

Nightly use since November and my before and after photos convinced my sister to buy one too. The improvement in my acne scarring is what shocked me, old marks on my jaw faded more in four months than in two years of vitamin C.

Twice the price of my old retinol and about twice as good, so the math works, barely. Glow is immediate from the glycolic, line-softening took until month three. The tube cap cracked at the hinge halfway through, which was annoying.

Decent, but slow. I saw more from a cheap adapalene gel in the same window. Nice cream texture and no dryness, credit where due, and my tone did brighten a bit by month three. Not sure I'll repurchase at this price.

At 54 my skin was dull and rough no matter what I exfoliated with. Eight weeks of this at night and the difference is obvious in photos. It feels like a plain moisturizer going on, no sting, a faint neutral smell that disappears instantly.

Slight tingle the first week and some dryness at the corners of my mouth, so I buffered it over moisturizer for a while. Settled down by week three. Results are real but gradual, softer lines around month three. Good, just be patient with it.

Menopause skin is tricky, suddenly dry, suddenly bumpy, lines showing up fast. This has been the single most useful thing in my routine for a year now. Gentle enough to use nightly, strong enough that skipping a week shows.

No purge, no flaking, no drama. Just slow, steady smoothing. I noticed my blush applying more evenly around week four, and by month three the vertical lip lines had softened. The tube means no scooping and the cream stays fresh to the end.

Hands down the easiest retinoid I've used, and I've used most of them. A retinoid bonded to an acid sounds like marketing until you realize you have been on it two months with better texture and not one flaky patch. The tube is travel-proof too.

Winter in Calgary destroys my skin and every previous retinol made it worse. This one I used straight through January with no flaking, I think the niacinamide is doing quiet work in the background. My texture is the best it has been in years.

Came highly recommended by my esthetician after a series of light peels, and it has kept those results going. I use a small dot straight on clean skin, nothing mixed in. Five months later the dark patch on my cheekbone is the lightest it has been.

This replaced my prescription retinoid and my barrier has never been happier. I use it after cleansing, nothing underneath, ceramide cream on top. The glycolic gives a gentle glow by morning and I've had zero flaking since I started in the fall.
Cheek texture improved a lot, and no irritation, which for me is rare. Two complaints, the cream can pill if I apply too much or rush my moisturizer on top, and the price stings. Still repurchasing.

Broke me out for the first three weeks, small clusters along my jaw. Things did calm down and my texture is better now at month four, but the purge was rougher than the gentle marketing suggests. Start slow, two nights a week.

r.t: A little goes a long way
r.b: Pea-sized amount is genuinely enough, which makes the small tube less painful. I'm on my third one now. My deep frown line is still there, no cream fixes that, but the fine crosshatching on my cheeks is basically gone and my tone is brighter.

r.t: Skipped a week, saw the difference
r.b: You know a product works when you skip it for a week of travel and notice. My skin went dull and rough again fast. Back on it, smooth within days. The tube also survived being squashed flat in my carry-on.

r.t: Two tubes, one faint frown line
r.b: Hard to review without gushing, but here goes. Nine months, two tubes, and the line between my brows has gone from obvious to faint. My husband started stealing squeezes from my tube, which is its own five-star review. Buying him his own.

After two decades of avoiding retinol because of my touchy skin, this converted me. The cream is silky, fragrance free, and spreads easily so the tube lasts. Around month two people started asking if I had changed my foundation. I hadn't.

Love that it combines the exfoliating acid and the retinoid in one step, my night routine went from five products to three and my skin feels like it drank something overnight. The niacinamide keeps my cheeks from going pink.

r.t: The compliments started at month four
r.b: Smooth, no scent, sinks in fast, and never fights with the rest of my routine. I keep it simple, cleanser, this, an occlusive on top. Four months later my skin texture is the thing people compliment. Never thought I would say that at 58.

Skeptical at first because gentle usually means weak. This is not weak. My skin got smoother by week five and the old acne marks on my cheeks faded a shade. Four stars because the last quarter of the tube is a fight to squeeze out.
Halfway through my first tube and I have already ordered a backup, softer smile lines and a clearer forehead with zero drama along the way.

Bought this on a whim after my wife raved about hers. Ten weeks in, the rough patches on my cheeks are gone and the sun damage on my temples looks lighter. Docking a star because the tube is small for the price and I go through it faster with a beard to work around.

r.t: Suits both halves of my face
r.b: Combination skin here, oily t-zone, dry cheeks, and this somehow suits both. Light enough not to clog, rich enough that my cheeks do not feel tight. Twelve weeks in, the orange-peel texture on my nose has smoothed right out.

r.t: Should have bought this years ago
r.b: Wish I'd found this sooner instead of cycling through five drugstore retinols that all burned. The retinoid plus glycolic combo sounds harsh on paper but my sensitive skin took to it immediately. Pores along my nose look tighter and my chin texture is smooth.

Expensive for 30 ml and I saw very little after five months of consistent nightly use. No irritation, but also no real change in my lines or tone. My skin may just be too used to stronger prescriptions. Going back to tretinoin.

r.t: Pilled no matter what I tried
r.b: It pilled under everything I tried, moisturizer, sunscreen the next morning, even on bare skin if I used more than a pea. Little rubbery bits all over my face. My sister loves hers so maybe my other products clash with it, but I gave up after six weeks.

Three months in and the crepey texture under my eyes and along my jaw has softened a lot. I apply it as the last step at night over a hyaluronic serum, wait a few minutes, done. No pilling as long as I let it sink in. The niacinamide seems to keep the redness away too.

r.t: Works for me and my mother
r.b: Picked up a second tube for my mother after she kept commenting on my skin. She is 68 with thin, dry skin and tolerates it fine at three nights a week. We are both seeing softer lines. Rare that one product works for both of us.

Every other night worked best for me in this desert climate, nightly use left my chin a bit tight. On that schedule it is excellent. Sun spots faded around week nine and my skin feels thicker in a good way.

Really wanted to love this after all the hype. Three months of nightly use, my texture is a little smoother but the lines on my forehead look the same. It is pleasant and gentle, no irritation at all, but for this money I expected more visible change.

The texture of this cream surprised me, lighter than I expected for something this potent, almost a thick lotion. Sinks in within a minute so I can go straight to my pillow. Forehead lines are shallower after about ten weeks.

First retinoid I've tolerated in my forties. I have eczema-prone patches near my nose and this never set them off. Small tingle the first three nights, then nothing. Texture win by week five, tone win by week ten.

r.t: Better at day ten, not worse
r.b: Used to think all retinoids meant peeling through week three. Not this one. The glycolic in it smooths while the retinoid does its slower work, so I never hit an ugly phase. My skin looked better at day ten, not worse.

So the niacinamide in here matters more than I expected. My usual retinol redness never showed up. Applied to dry skin after cleansing, moisturizer after ten minutes, and by week seven my skin looked polished in daylight. Not one negative to report.

Was using a drugstore retinol before and this is smoother and stronger at the same time. Better glow, faster texture change, zero irritation. Four stars only because the 30 ml tube empties fast when you use it on your neck too.

I was nervous about retinoids after a bad reaction years ago, but this one gave me smoother skin with zero flaking. Started twice a week, nightly by week four, and the little bumps on my chin are gone.

Almost returned it in week two when my cheeks felt tight, but I dropped to every third night and it turned around completely. Now nightly with no issues and softer lines by month three. The learning curve cost it a star.

Honestly didn't expect much from another retinol alternative, but it won me over slowly. Took a solid three months before my smile lines softened, so patience is required. Nice that it never made me peel, though I wish results came faster for the price.

Not an overnight miracle despite the name. Took me close to three months to see real change on my forehead. Once it kicked in though, it kicked in. Smoother shave, fewer clogged pores, less shine. Wish it cost less.

Switched from tretinoin 0.05 after fifteen years because winter here made the flaking unbearable. Honestly didn't expect a cosmetic retinoid to hold up, but four months in my lines look the same as they did on the prescription and my cheeks aren't raw anymore. Worth the tube price for me.

Melasma plus fine lines at 47 and this has helped both, slowly but genuinely. Cheeks look more even in bare-face photos taken three months apart. I pair it with a mineral SPF every morning, no exceptions, and the combination is working.

Big fan of the glycolic and retinoid pairing, it gives the morning glow of an acid with the long game of a retinoid. Dark spots from old breakouts faded noticeably by week eight. No scent, elegant texture, absorbs in under a minute.

r.t: Softer mouth lines in ten weeks
r.b: Fine lines around my mouth were my main concern and they are visibly softer after about ten weeks. I layer it over a hydrating cream on dry winter nights and it never pills that way. My skin drinks it up.

r.t: Good so far, jury still out
r.b: Six weeks in and I like it, don't love it yet. Texture and glow improved, lines not so much. My esthetician says give it six months. Taking off a star for now because at this price I expected quicker movement on the forehead lines.

r.t: Finally a retinoid I can handle
r.b: My derm recommended this after tretinoin left me flaky for months. The AlphaRet pairs the retinoid with glycolic acid but somehow my skin never peeled. By week six the texture on my forehead was noticeably smoother and my makeup stopped settling into the lines around my eyes. A pea-sized amount from the tube covers my whole face. Zero scent, zero sting.

Started this four weeks after microneedling on my provider's advice and the combination has been excellent. Smoother, brighter, and the pigment from an old acne scar is nearly gone. The cream itself is unscented and sinks in cleanly.

Gentle is the right word. I have reactive, redness-prone skin and every retinol before this one lit my face up. This one has a slight tingle for the first minute and then nothing. Eight weeks in, my texture is smoother and my flushing hasn't gotten worse.

Two tubes in and mostly thrilled. The lines at the corners of my eyes look softer and my tone is more even. My only gripe is a mild purge in weeks two and three, a scatter of small whiteheads on my chin before things cleared.
It is a lovely lightweight serum and my post-laser recovery was smooth. At this price I was hoping the firming would be more pronounced by now. Still a four because the recovery benefit is real.

My surgeon recommended the Skin Nectar to support recovery after a mini lift and I could not be happier. The skin bounced back beautifully and the firming feels like it complemented the results. Zero irritation on healing skin.
Started two weeks before my resurfacing as instructed and I did heal quickly. For daily firming I find it subtle, so I mainly reach for it around appointments. Light and non-irritating.

I started this for general anti-aging after my sister raved about it. By week six my skin looked plumper and my cheeks felt firmer to the touch. It disappears into the skin and layers under everything without a fuss. Not cheap, but it lasts me nearly four months.
Absorbs in seconds and layers well under my moisturizer and SPF. My skin does look a little firmer and healthier after ten weeks, just not night-and-day. Good product, premium price.
RF microneedling usually leaves me red and swollen for a week. Applied this right after and for the days following, and I was presentable in three days. Impressed.
Used it on my decolletage where sun damage left things crepey. After about two months it looks smoother and a bit firmer. Wish the improvement were faster given the price, but I am sticking with it.

After a rough winter of dryness and a couple of peels, my barrier felt shot. Two months on this and my skin bounces back faster and looks less thin. The peptides seem to be rebuilding something. I use one pump AM and PM under moisturizer.

Sixty-one and I have tried a lot. After a full four months on the Nectar twice daily, the sagging around my mouth is genuinely lifted and my skin looks less thin. It layers beautifully under my SPF in the morning. Pricey, worth it for me.
Deeper skin tone here and a lot of recovery serums leave an ashy film. This one just melts in with nothing left behind. My post-procedure marks faded faster than expected too.

Effective enough around my microneedling, but the faint herbal smell that others say fades stuck around longer than I liked. Firming was subtle over six weeks. It is a fine product, just didn't wow me for what it costs.

If you want a gentle serum that helps skin recover and slowly firms, this fits. If you want dramatic overnight lifting, look elsewhere. I like it enough to keep it in rotation. Weightless texture, no clogging.

My clinic has me start the Nectar two weeks before any resurfacing and keep going after. My downtime has genuinely shortened compared to the days before I used it. Light, fast, and gentle on healing skin.
Used it for weeks after a mole excision to help the surrounding skin. Healed cleanly and the texture around the site is smooth. Light and gentle.

My dermatologist added this before and after my Fraxel package. Not only did I heal faster, my overall firmness has improved between sessions. The airless pump feels premium and keeps everything sterile.

I didn't expect the fine lines around my mouth to improve, but after three months twice a day they are softer. The firming is real. The bottle is small for the money but the airless pump means nothing is wasted.
Ran this for six weeks leading up to my daughter's wedding and my skin looked plumper and more even in the photos than it has in years. Barely any scent, layers perfectly under makeup.
Have repurchased twice for use around my treatments. It calms redness and speeds healing consistently. Firmness improvement is modest but present. The pump can be a touch stiff at first.
Bought it for firmness but the surprise win was texture. My skin feels smoother and more even after about eight weeks of nightly use. Absorbs in seconds, no scent I can detect.
My skin felt soothed and looked less blotchy after peels. It hydrates nicely without any heaviness. The firming is a slow burn but the calming payoff was immediate.

Used this after a minor facial surgery on my dermatologist's advice to support healing around the incision. The area recovered smoothly and the fine lines nearby actually look better. Airless pump, no mess, absorbs in seconds.
Aggressive microneedling used to sideline me for a week. With the Nectar going on right after and for the days following, I was back to normal in three or four days. Genuinely impressed.

Used it before and after a laser on my clinic's advice. Recovery was fine but I honestly cannot say it was better than a plain gentle serum would have been. For what a bottle costs, I expected far more.

I turned 50 this year and wanted something legit for firmness. After roughly ten weeks of morning and night use, the skin along my jaw looks tighter and my pores seem smaller. The serum is milky white and vanishes into the skin. Not cheap, but a little does the job.

r.t: Recovery serum that earns its price
r.b: I was hesitant at the price point, but after using it around two rounds of microneedling I am a convert. The bruising and redness clear so much faster, and in between procedures my skin just looks healthier and firmer. One pump covers the whole face.
The arnica angle is legit, my post-filler bruising was much lighter. I was hoping for more obvious firming and that part has been slow. Absorbs beautifully and never pills.
After a laser plus Ottawa winter, my skin was raw and reactive. This calmed it right down and rebuilt the barrier within a couple of weeks. No stinging at all.
Lightweight, sinks in fast, and my skin looked calmer after my last laser. The one ounce bottle goes quicker than I'd like if you use it twice a day on face and neck. Still, results are real.
Had a big under-eye bruise from filler and my nurse told me to smooth this over the area twice a day. It faded far faster than I expected. The arnica must be doing the heavy lifting.

r.t: My skin looks lit from within
r.b: The phytoene and phytofluene must be why my complexion looks so much more radiant. Combined with the firming from the peptides, my skin honestly glows after a couple of months. Sinks in fast, no residue.

I use the Nectar on my neck and the backs of my hands because those give my age away. After about ten weeks the crepey texture on both has smoothed out and my hands look plumper. The milky serum absorbs without any greasy film.

r.t: Does what it claims, at a cost
r.b: My med spa recommended it around my microneedling series and it delivered on faster healing and less bruising. The firming is there but gradual. It is expensive enough that I only use it around procedures rather than daily.

Decent recovery serum that calmed my skin after IPL. My frustration is the airless pump stopped drawing product with a good centimeter left in the bottle, so I felt I paid for serum I couldn't access. Results were okay, nothing remarkable.

I am rosacea-prone and terrified of new serums, but this one never flushed me or stung. I started it after a gentle laser and the calming was noticeable within days. No fragrance that bothered me, and the pump is hygienic which matters for reactive skin.

r.t: Even my oily skin loves it
r.b: Most firming serums feel heavy on my oily skin, but this sinks in matte and never clogs me. Used it after a series of peels and my pores look tighter. No breakouts at all.
Kind to my sensitive, post-peel skin and I did see improvement in firmness over a couple of months. The light herbal scent is not my favorite but it fades fast. Would repurchase.

Bought a bottle after a chemical peel and my wife liked the results on me so much she now uses it too. The peptides really do seem to firm things up over time. We are on our third bottle between us. Absorbs quickly and sits nicely under everything.
My injector told me to start this a few days before Botox and I hardly had a mark afterward. It is now part of my pre-appointment ritual. Light, quick, and no fragrance to fuss over.

r.t: Broke my budget, not my wrinkles
r.b: I wanted to love this given the reviews, but after nearly three months I saw very little firming and no real change in my fine lines. It did absorb nicely and never irritated me. Two stars because at this price I needed to see something, and I did not.
Used this the whole week following IPL and my face was not nearly as blotchy as usual. Goes on almost like water.

Started two weeks before CO2 laser and continued after. The peeling and redness resolved days sooner than my previous treatment without it, and my skin has stayed firmer since. A little goes a long way from the pump.
I use it before laser and it does seem to reduce my downtime. Cannot say I notice much for firmness on its own, but the recovery benefit alone keeps me buying it. Absorbs quickly with no residue.

I used a full bottle over two and a half months, morning and night, and honestly the firming was minimal. It did help my skin recover after a peel, so it isn't useless, but for the price I expected more visible change. Texture and absorption are excellent at least.

My injector recommends the Skin Nectar before and after filler and now I understand why. I ran it for a week ahead of my last appointment and the swelling and bruising were minimal. Lightweight, barely any scent, and it never pills under my sunscreen.

I am 47 and skeptical of most serums, but the pinch test on the back of my hand and on my cheeks is noticeably springier after three months. The phytoene antioxidants are a nice bonus on top of the firming. It absorbs cleanly and plays well with my retinol at night.

r.t: Kept using it after my peel
r.b: I only bought it to recover from a peel, but the way it plumped and firmed my skin convinced me to keep going. Now it is my daily anti-aging serum. Milky, weightless, faintly herbal.
Used it after a TCA peel and the flaking phase was far more comfortable than usual. No sting, sinks in fast, faint plant scent.
Helped my skin settle after IPL faster than usual and I do think my skin is firmer. My only real gripe is the cost for the size of the bottle. Nice light texture with a faint herbal smell.

Started this two weeks before a microneedling package and my esthetician was shocked at how little I bruised afterward. The arnica clearly does something. Texture is like a light lotion, absorbs in seconds, and I layer my moisturizer right over top with no pilling.

At 58 my neck had that crepey look creeping in. I've been smoothing the Nectar over my neck and chest every night for about four months and the crepiness has visibly softened. It absorbs clean and the airless bottle keeps the actives from going off.
My nurse injector recommends starting this a week out from filler. My last round I had zero visible bruising, which never happens for me. The formula is so light it disappears.

My esthetician put me on the Skin Nectar to support collagen between treatments and I trust her completely. Over four months my skin looks visibly more refined and firm. The formula is weightless and never breaks me out. Yes it costs a lot, but the airless bottle stretches surprisingly far.

My dermatologist sent me home with the Nectar after a Fraxel session and told me to start it that same night. The milky serum sank in fast with no sting even on raw, peeling skin, and my redness calmed a couple of days quicker than after my last laser. I'm 54 with dry, mature skin and I have stayed on it morning and night since. The airless pump doses out exactly the right amount.

No complaints about how it feels going on, it absorbs instantly and never irritates. The firming took me a solid three months to notice though, so patience is required. Docking a star because the results were subtle rather than dramatic for the price.

I bought this purely for the TriHex peptides after reading about the elastin support, no procedures involved. Three months in and my cheeks genuinely feel firmer and my foundation sits better on them. There is a faint herbal smell that fades within a minute. It is pricey, but one pump goes a long way so the bottle lasts.

Real talk: nothing happened for a month and I felt like a fool. Then week five arrived and my skin started looking rested, then smoother, then brighter. Now at week fourteen the fine lines around my mouth are visibly softer. Charge it, strap it, breathe for ten minutes. The routine is the product.

For my tired postpartum skin this has been the one thing I can keep up. Baby naps, mask goes on, ten minutes of lying still. Twelve weeks in, the dullness has lifted and the creases from sleeping on my face bounce back the way they did in my twenties. Can't overstate how easy it is.

Since February I have logged every session in a spreadsheet, 78 total, average 4.6 per week. Compared my January photos to end of May: the nasolabial creases are visibly softer under the same bathroom lighting. Placebo doesn't survive a controlled photo setup. Battery lasts me about three sessions per charge, for the record.

So much of skincare is faith, but this one gave me receipts. My aesthetician measured my skin before and after twelve weeks and the hydration and firmness scores both improved. I do ten minutes in the evening, mask on bare skin, serums after. The velcro straps have held up through daily use since January.

Full disclosure, I have a small face and the mask overhangs my jaw a little, so I fold a towel under the edge. Even with imperfect contact the results at week eight are real: brighter, smoother, fine lines softened around my eyes. If Omnilux made a petite size I'd trade up instantly.
