Fifty-eight years old, twelve weeks in, and my skin looks better than it did at fifty. The crepe on my cheeks has smoothed, the deep frown line is softer, and I have stopped wearing foundation most days. I do my session with my morning stretches. The mask flexes when I move, never slides off.

You have to be boring about it, ten minutes almost every day, and then it works. I tracked with weekly photos: visible change at week six, obvious at week ten. Forehead lines softer, skin bouncier. It is comfortable enough that I do the dishes wearing it, which is a look, but it means I never skip.

r.t: Pleasantly boring in the best way
r.b: Pleasantly surprised by how unremarkable using it is. No tingling, no heat beyond gentle warmth, no drama, just a beep after ten minutes. The results crept up on me: around week six my skin started looking like I sleep eight hours. I don't. Flexible enough to wear reading in bed. Highly recommend.

r.t: Wish I had bought it sooner
r.b: Wish someone had told me the results are cumulative and slow, because I nearly quit at week three when nothing had changed. Week seven was the turning point: smoother texture, brighter tone, and the little lines under my eyes softened. Four stars because the nose bridge doesn't sit flush on my face and I suspect that area gets less light.

r.t: My whole family owns one now
r.b: Nobody in my family believed a mask of little red lights would do anything, and now my mother and my aunt both own one. Three months of use most weeknights smoothed my texture and faded the red marks my breakouts leave behind. It fits under my chin properly, which cheaper masks never did. One star off for how bright it is around the eyes.

Never thought I'd own a glowing face mask at 67, but my dermatologist suggested red light for overall skin quality. She was right. The deep creases are still there, I'm realistic, but the fine crosshatching on my cheeks has smoothed out and the skin feels thicker. Simple to use, shuts off by itself.

Using it since Boxing Day, mostly four nights a week. Results are legit: smoother texture by week five, and the sun damage on my cheekbones looks lighter. My gripe is fit. I have a wide face and the velcro straps are at their limit, leaving a strap line across my ears for a half hour after. Would still buy again.

Hard pass for me unfortunately. The mask never sat flush on my low nose bridge and high cheekbones, so light bled into my eyes to the point of watering, and I got a pressure headache from tightening the straps to compensate. Returned it within the window. Beautifully made device, just not a universal fit.

Okay so here is my honest take at the three month mark. Tone: brighter, yes. Texture: smoother, yes. The firmness and lifting I bought it for: minimal. My jowls don't care about red light apparently. If your goal is glow and fine lines, go for it. For sagging, manage your expectations.

Not my first LED rodeo. I owned a rigid mask that pressed on my nose and hovered an inch off my cheeks. The Contour actually touches my whole face, which apparently matters for the light dose. Results came faster than with the old one, smoother cheeks by week five. Strap marks fade in twenty minutes, fair trade.

This gets used more than anything else I've ever bought for my skin. I was paying for in-office LED after peels; the math made the mask cheaper within four months. Flexible, comfortable enough to walk around in, and my post-peel flaking calms noticeably faster. FDA cleared mattered to me and it shows in the results.

Verdict: worth it, with honest caveats. The improvement is real but gradual, my six month photos show softer lines and better tone than any cream achieved. The velcro strap fuzzed up around month four and grips slightly less. Battery needs charging every two or three sessions. I would still repurchase tomorrow.

Mixed results here. My skin tone is brighter and my husband swears my skin looks smoother, but my main target, the deep line between my brows, has barely budged in four months. It is relaxing at least, my ten minutes of enforced stillness. If you want glow, yes. Deep expression lines, temper expectations.

Didn't expect a light to do what my shelf of creams could not. Menopause left my skin thin and dull; after ten weeks of near-daily sessions it looks denser and the colour has come back to my cheeks. My only note is to buy it on sale if you can. Worth it regardless.

Purchased with my retirement gift money and no regrets. The mask is soft, bends with my face, and the controller is one button, which suits me fine. After about two months people started asking if I changed my makeup. I hadn't. Fine lines are softer and my skin has a low-key glow.

Love that this fits into a real life. I wear it while my tea steeps. In three months the fine lines on my forehead went from obvious in photos to something I have to hunt for. No serums needed with it, no mess, and the silicone hasn't yellowed or stiffened with daily use.

Halfway through my third month and I'm still on the fence. There is a glow, my partner sees it too, but the wrinkle change is smaller than the marketing photos implied. It is pleasant to use and well made, I just expected more for over five hundred dollars Canadian. Trying two more months before final judgment.

r.t: Lying down never felt so productive
r.b: Lying flat with a warm glowing mask for ten minutes turns out to be the most consistent skincare habit I've ever kept. Ninety-plus sessions since spring. My before photo shows forehead lines I no longer see in the mirror, and my skin tolerates retinol better on mask days somehow. Genuinely earned its price.

Got it for my wife, borrowed it, and now we fight over the charger. My before and after photos at week seven show the creases on my forehead genuinely shallower. Ten minutes with a podcast and done. Only tip: charge it after every second session because the battery pack doesn't hold a ton.

Confession time, I mocked my sister for buying one, then borrowed it for a month and quietly ordered my own. The difference in my skin's bounce was undeniable by week four. Mine lives on my nightstand and gets used while I do my gratitude journal. The battery pack clips to my pyjama collar. We are inseparable.

Bit the bullet after a year of deliberating. The good: visibly smoother forehead by week six, and it is comfortable lying down, which flat panels aren't. The caveats: the near-infrared LEDs look unlit so half the mask seems broken the first time (it isn't, read the manual), and you will want to charge it more often than you expect.

r.t: Ten quiet minutes that pay off
r.b: Ten minutes lying on the couch while it does its thing has become my favourite part of the evening. Twelve weeks in: brighter overall tone, the vertical line between my brows is softer, and breakouts heal faster without leaving marks. It wipes clean with a damp cloth, which matters more than people think with a silicone mask.

Was loving it until the controller stopped holding a charge in month three. It would beep and die five minutes into a session. Customer service did honour the warranty but I was without it for weeks and the replacement process was slow. Skin-wise I saw modest smoothing, but for this price the hardware should be bulletproof.

Photos don't lie. My daughter compared my March and September pictures and immediately asked to borrow the mask. The texture on my cheeks is smoother and the frown line is noticeably softer. I'm 63. I pair it with my usual moisturizer after each session and that is the whole routine.

Six weeks of five sessions a week and the marionette lines beside my mouth have visibly softened. I'm 61 and was fully prepared for this to be a gimmick. It isn't. The mask molds to my face, the eye openings line up properly, and a session is easy to keep up with morning coffee.

Started this hoping to fade post-acne marks faster and it delivered inside six weeks. Kept going and the bonus effects piled up: calmer skin overall, fewer new breakouts, and a smoothness that makeup loves. It sits comfortably even over my cheekbones and the mouth opening means I can talk on calls. Ten minutes, no thoughts.

Red light was the one thing my esthetician, my sister, and my group chat agreed on, so I caved. The Contour flexes flat against my cheeks unlike the hard shell mask I returned last year, and coverage feels edge to edge. Six weeks of evening sessions and the glow is honestly a little addictive.

r.t: Subtle, and you must be consistent
r.b: The results are real but subtle, and nobody warns you how much discipline this takes. I managed maybe three sessions a week and after two months I see slightly smoother texture, nothing dramatic. If you skip weeks like I did over vacation, you are basically starting over. Lovely build quality, though, and the carry bag is handy.

Big skeptic energy going in, I work in healthcare and hate wellness gadgets. But the wavelengths here, 633nm red and 830nm near-infrared, are the same ones in the studies I went and read. Ten weeks of consistent use: finer texture, less redness, softer smile lines. The evidence and my mirror finally agree on something.

Nightly use since spring, and my quarterly facial turned into my esthetician interrogating me about what changed. Texture smoother, pores look tighter, the etched lines on my forehead softer. It replaced a serum and a mask in my routine, which offsets some of the cost. Wipes down in seconds, charges overnight, zero fuss.

Genuinely didn't expect much. My wife bought it, I used it on a lark for my razor irritation and general weathered fisherman situation. Two months of most-evenings use and the redness along my jaw is way down and the skin feels less leathery. Wish the straps adjusted a little finer for bigger heads, but otherwise easy. Beeps when done, wipe it, hang it on the hook.

Honestly the brightness surprised me the first time, I keep my eyes closed the whole session now. Past that adjustment it has been simple: ten minutes, three or four nights a week, on bare skin before serums. Two months in, my jawline looks a touch firmer and the redness in my cheeks has calmed down.

Consistency was my worry and this mask solved it by being genuinely easy. No goop, no downtime, just strap it on after cleansing. My sensitive skin tolerates it perfectly, no heat rash, no redness after. Three months in, the crepey texture under my eyes has smoothed out more than any eye cream ever managed.

Treated myself after my 50th and it has outperformed every cream on my counter. I use it four mornings a week before sunscreen. By week seven my skin looked firmer at the cheekbone and the vertical lip lines catch less lipstick. The eye openings are generous enough that I can actually see my book.

My esthetician uses Omnilux panels in clinic, so I trusted the brand. The mask straps on with velcro at the back and the little battery pack clips to my collar. Four sessions a week, six weeks in, and the lines across my forehead are shallower. Not erased, shallower. That is exactly what I hoped for.

Fits my routine like nothing else has. Cleansed skin, mask on, ten minutes while I read on my phone through the eye holes, done. At 52 my jawline was getting soft and after three months it looks noticeably firmer in profile photos. My husband, who notices nothing, noticed. Money well spent.

r.t: Everyone asks about my skin now
r.b: Everyone in my office has now tried on my mask because they keep asking why I look less tired. Eight weeks in, mostly five sessions a week, sometimes while walking on my treadmill pad. Fine lines softer, dark marks from old breakouts fading quicker. Only knock is charging it every couple of sessions gets old. It survived a drop onto tile, though.

r.t: Works, but plan for the cord
r.b: Skeptical was an understatement, my husband teased me for weeks. The 633nm red plus the near-infrared you can't even see felt like an expensive gamble, but around week four my skin tone got noticeably more even and makeup sat better. Knocking a star off because the cord to the controller always ends up in an awkward spot when I lie down.

r.t: Fine lines fading week by week
r.b: Fine print for future buyers: take a photo before you start. I nearly returned mine at week three until I compared photos and saw my crow's feet had already softened. Now at week eleven the change is obvious in person. Bare skin, five nights a week, and the phone timer is redundant since it shuts itself off.

At first I bought it purely for anti-aging, but the surprise win was my rosacea. Flares are shorter and less angry since I started four sessions a week. The 633nm red light is apparently well studied for this and I believe it now. Zero sting, zero irritation, no product needed, which my reactive skin appreciates.

Week one I felt like I lit my face up for nothing, just pleasant warmth and red glow. Week eight, the smile lines are less carved in and my skin looks rested even when I am not. Four stars only because the price stings and the battery indicator is vague about how much charge is left.

r.t: Once a skeptic, now on autopilot
r.b: Once I stopped treating it like a miracle and started treating it like brushing my teeth, it delivered. Ninety days of short evening sessions: firmer cheeks, softer elevens, brighter tone. I'm 49 with combination skin and nothing else changed in my routine, so I'm confident the mask gets the credit.

Two things happened after four months with this mask: my injector said my skin quality looked better, and I pushed my Botox appointment out by six weeks because the lines weren't bothering me yet. It has paid for a chunk of itself already. Ten minutes, five days a week, no excuses.

Bought this after my facialist kept raving about red light. Ten minutes on clean skin most evenings, usually while I answer emails. By week five the crow's feet at the corners of my eyes looked less etched in and my cheeks had a bounce I hadn't seen in a while. The silicone actually flexes to my face, unlike the rigid masks I tried before.

r.t: Ten minutes I actually keep up with
r.b: The mask molds to my face better than the rigid one I returned last year, and the ten minute auto shutoff means I can do it while emptying the dishwasher. Around week six the lines across my forehead started looking shallower in bathroom light. The controller cord is shorter than I'd like, that's my only real gripe.

Compared to the rigid panel I used for a year, this actually contours to my face and I can move around the house. Results showed faster too, about five weeks for softer eye lines versus never with the panel. Docked a star for the price and because the carry bag zipper already feels flimsy.

Between weeks four and eight something shifted. My esthetician, who did not know I bought it, asked what I was doing differently because my skin looked plumper. That is the review, honestly. Ten minutes most nights, red and near-infrared doing their invisible thing, and a compliment from the person who knows my face best.

Splurged on this for my 45th and mostly thrilled. Skin looks plumper and the forehead lines have relaxed after nine weeks. Two practical notes: it is bright even with eyes shut, I fold a thin cloth over the eye area, and the cord placement means sleeping in it isn't an option. Otherwise excellent.

After microneedling appointments my redness used to hang around for days. Now I do ten minutes under this mask that evening and I'm presentable by morning. My nurse confirmed red light at these wavelengths is the real deal. It beeps and shuts itself off, which I appreciate because I always fall asleep in it.

Three dermatologists cleared me to use this alongside my melasma routine since there is no meaningful heat buildup like some devices. It hasn't triggered my pigment, and the overall brightness after eight weeks makes my tone look more even. I use it in the morning before sunscreen. Feels sturdy, folds flat for travel.

Works, but slowly, and you must wear sunscreen or you are wasting your money. My age spots took a full three months to visibly lighten. The pump is smooth, the lotion is elegant, and the price is the only real ouch.
Returned to this after a month of trialing trendier serums, and nothing else kept my tone as even. Lesson learned. The pump lives on my counter now and the trendy stuff went to my sister.
Been on it a year, morning and night, and my esthetician now asks what I changed at every single facial.

Two pumps at night, moisturizer over top, and the constellation of age spots on my cheekbones has softened dramatically since Christmas. At 61 I did not expect much. My daughter now borrows it, which is its own five-star review.

Was hoping it would hydrate a bit more on its own, but on my dry skin it definitely needs a cream over top in winter. That said, the brightening is real. My overall tone looks like I sleep eight hours, which I do not.

r.t: Texture sells it, results keep it
r.b: Silky lotion texture won me over the first morning, absorbed before I finished brushing my teeth. The results took longer, around nine weeks, but the sallow dullness I've had since my twenties finally lifted. My cheeks look lit from within, and I am not usually a lit-from-within person.

Every morning after cleansing, one pump, then SPF, and that's the whole trick. Eight months in, the mottled tone across my cheeks reads even in daylight, and I've stopped wearing foundation to the grocery store.
It layers under my morning SPF and over my exfoliating toner with no pilling, and ten weeks in the city-living dullness I complained about all year has quietly lifted.

Slow burn of a product. I nearly returned it at week five, then week eight arrived and suddenly my face was one colour instead of three. Now on bottle two and the maintenance seems easier than the initial fade.

Six weeks before I noticed anything, then it kind of snowballed. Overall tone is brighter and the freckle cluster on my left cheek is softer. Wish the bottle were bigger, I go through one in about seven weeks using it twice a day.
A little goes a long way here. One pump covers face and neck, so the bottle lasted me almost three months. Acne marks on my cheeks lightened noticeably by week nine and my T-zone never got congested.

Surprised by how gentle it is for something that actually fades pigment. No sting even right after cleansing. My only gripe is the pump refuses to surrender the last week's worth of product no matter how I shake or tap it.

Mixed feelings, but leaning good. Weightless feel, never broke me out, and my newer marks faded within a couple months. The older post-acne spots needed reinforcement, so my esthetician has me pairing it with an exfoliant now. Together they're working.

Since retinol wrecks me every single time, this was my compromise, and honestly the tone improvement rivals what my friends get from their tretinoin. Fine lines, no. Brightness and evenness, absolutely yes. Cheeks look polished instead of patchy.

Halfway through the bottle and my verdict is mostly positive. General brightness, definitely. The two stubborn sun spots I bought it for are only starting to budge. It applies beautifully and never irritates, so it earns four stars while I wait on the rest.

Didn't expect a brightener to fix my January complexion, but here we are. The grey, tired cast melted off over about seven weeks. I layer it under a heavy cream at night and there's no pilling, no sting, no scent worth mentioning.

After my second pregnancy my forehead was a patchwork of brown. Six months of this, morning and night, and it is honestly close to even again. No retinol meant I could use it while nursing, which was the whole reason I picked it.

Used it strictly at night for three months against the brown marks a bad winter breakout left behind. Most are gone, two linger. No purging, no clogged pores. Would be five stars at a friendlier price.

Pleasant surprise after years of disappointing brighteners. The tone shift crept up on me until a coworker asked if I'd been on vacation. Two pumps each morning before sunscreen. Nothing pilled, nothing stung, nothing broke me out.

Melasma has bullied me since my thirties and this is the first non-hydroquinone thing that made a visible dent. The mustache shadow is maybe half as dark after four months. I use two pumps at night after my toner. It has a faint clean scent that vanishes in seconds.

Fine for the first week, then it started pilling under both my sunscreen and moisturizer no matter how long I waited between layers. Tried applying less, tried more, gave up around week five with zero change in my spots. Expensive experiment.

Repurchased twice now. At 58 my sun damage is decades deep, and this hasn't erased it, but my face looks brighter and the age spots at my temples have blurred at the edges. Two pumps nightly, then a rich cream over top.

For sensitive-leaning skin that still wants results, this hits the mark. I doubted a brightener without acids or retinol could do anything, and twelve weeks later my before photo looks like a different, tireder person.

This replaced my vitamin C serum since it has brightening covered without any greasiness. Sits well under gel moisturizer and sunscreen, no pilling. Marks from old breakouts faded around the two month mark. Four stars only because the pump sputters when the bottle gets low and you lose product.

Can't say it did much for my melasma, which is why I bought it. General glow, sure, but the patches on my forehead look the same in every light. Absorbs nicely at least, and it never pilled under my SPF.

One pump wasn't quite covering my face and neck so I use two, which means a bottle lasts me about six weeks. Results are legit, my tan-related patchiness resolved by the end of month two, but the burn rate keeps it at four stars.

Love that there is no retinol or hydroquinone in this, because my reactive skin tolerates neither. The glucosamine and papain do the exfoliating work invisibly. Redness never flared once in five months, and the brown marks left over from a bad flare are basically gone.

Got this after IPL to keep the pigment from marching back, and one year on, it hasn't. My technician credits the hexylresorcinol. Whatever it is, I stopped needing touch-up sessions, which means the bottle basically pays for itself.

The pump on mine jammed within three weeks and I had to unscrew the top to scoop product out, which surely wasn't great for the vitamin C. Beyond that, two months of consistent use did basically nothing for my sun spots. Frustrating at this price.

r.t: Great on oil, minus one quibble
r.b: Wish it came in a bigger size because I fly through it. Otherwise, for oily skin this is ideal: lotion-light, matte-ish finish, no clogging, and my summer tan lines and spots evened out by early fall.
Years of hormonal spots along my jaw have visibly lightened since spring, and all it asks of me is one pump of light, barely scented lotion before bed.

Post-summer sun damage sent me here, and by Halloween the new freckling across my nose had mostly faded back out. Kept using it through winter and my skin tone stayed the most even it's been in years.

Three months in and the melasma patch on my upper lip is noticeably lighter, which nothing over the counter ever managed. I press one pump in after cleansing at night and follow with moisturizer. The lotion is silky and sinks in fast. Wearing sunscreen religiously alongside it, which I'm sure helps.

Nothing dramatic to report after nine weeks. Maybe a slight overall brightening, though I wonder if that's the sunscreen habit I started at the same time. Pump works fine, texture is fine, everything is fine. Just fine.

Picked this up at my clinic after laser alone didn't hold my pigment back. Six months later the spots have not returned and my jawline discoloration is smoother. It became the boring reliable step in my routine, and I mean that as praise.

On my third bottle. Nothing about this is exciting: white lotion, pump bottle, faint scent, sinks in fast. But my formerly blotchy forehead is uniform for the first time in a decade, so exciting is overrated.

Hands down the lowest-effort win in my routine. Cleanser, this, sunscreen. That's everything I do, and colleagues have started asking if I got work done. The pump dispenses the exact right amount, which my clumsy morning self appreciates.
Texture is lovely and it never irritated me, but after a full bottle my acne marks look maybe twenty percent better. For this price I wanted more. Might work better stacked with an exfoliant.

Dark spots from cystic acne have haunted my chin for years. This didn't work overnight, more like a slow dimming over three months, but they went from the first thing I saw in the mirror to something I have to look for.
Not a miracle. My dark spots from picking are marginally lighter after ten weeks and the lotion feels nice enough, but drugstore niacinamide got me similar results for a quarter of the cost.

So I bought one bottle, then my mom noticed my skin, then my sister, and now three of us are on it. Different ages, different spot types, all seeing fading somewhere between week six and week twelve. The pump makes sharing hygienic at least.

Pricey but performing. The freckles I wanted to keep stayed put while the blotchy patches faded, which felt oddly selective and I am not complaining. Four stars because the cost per bottle stings more than the serum ever did.

You need eight to twelve weeks, full stop. I almost quit at week six, then my post-inflammatory marks from a beard breakout faded fast. The lotion is light, unscented to my nose, and one pump does my whole face and neck.

Zero irritation in six months of daily use, which for my rosacea-prone skin is a small miracle. The brown staining left behind by old flares has faded to almost nothing. I apply it before my moisturizer at night and that's it.

My derm suggested this because I can't tolerate hydroquinone. Took a solid ten weeks before my post-shaving marks lightened, which tested my patience, but they did lighten. Docking a star for the price per mL.

Honestly the only reason my skin looked airbrushed in my wedding photos. Started it five months out on my esthetician's advice, one pump every morning, and the blotchy unevenness across my cheeks just quietly disappeared. Zero flaking, zero drama.

Genuinely the first pigment product my reactive skin has accepted. No burning, no rebound redness, and the marks from an eczema patch on my cheek faded within about ten weeks. I keep the pump on my sink and use it like clockwork.

Okay so it took nearly three months, but the red-brown leftovers from a year of maskne are finally faint. It never clogged me, which brighteners often do. Knocking a star off because the scent, while light, reads a bit chemical for the first minute.

If you're expecting two-week results, walk away now. Mine took until week ten to show, and then improved steadily through month four. The uneven olive-toned patches on my cheeks are largely gone. Just budget for the long game.

Started using this after a chemical peel to keep pigment from creeping back, per my nurse's plan. Spots stayed away and the rest of my face got brighter as a bonus. Absorbs in about thirty seconds and plays fine under makeup.

Bought this in early January for the freckly sun damage across my cheekbones, and by week eight the biggest spot had gone from obvious to faint. It's a creamy lotion texture, not a watery serum, and one pump covers my whole face. I use it every morning under SPF. No sting, no purge, just gradual evening out.

Decade of Arizona sun on this face, and it still made a visible dent. The scattered small spots faded first and the big one on my temple finally followed around month four. Feels like a light lotion and never balls up under my mineral sunscreen.

At 52 I assumed my sun spots were permanent residents. My clinic recommended this over another round of laser, and I'll admit I rolled my eyes at a pump bottle of lotion. Four months of two pumps twice daily and two of the five spots are gone entirely, the rest faded to background noise. It never stung, never pilled under my day cream, and the light scent disappears fast. Wish I had taken photos on day one because the change snuck up on me.

I was braced for stinging because most brighteners set my face on fire, and this one just... didn't. The papain and hexylresorcinol combo apparently works gently. Four months in, the dull grey cast I had all winter is gone and my foundation shade is one step lighter.

First brightener out of maybe six I've tried that produced results I could photograph. Side-by-sides at week zero and week twelve genuinely surprised me. The papain enzyme approach seems to suit my easily-annoyed skin better than acid-based options ever did.

Booked my wedding for July and started this in January in a mild panic about the uneven patches on my cheeks. Six months later my makeup artist asked what I had done because my base went on like glass. Consistent, twice a day, always under SPF 50. It worked.

r.t: My cheeks match my forehead now
r.b: One year update: still using it, still clear. My melasma used to darken every single summer no matter how careful I was with hats and SPF. Last summer was the first in a decade it stayed quiet. I credit the tranexamic acid, my derm credits my consistency. Either way, repurchasing.

For weeks I saw nothing and complained to anyone who would listen. Then around day fifty the patch beside my nose started breaking apart, and by month four it was gone. Pigment correction is not linear, apparently. Light milky texture, absorbs fast, worth the wait and the money.

Side by side photos three months apart finally convinced my skeptical husband this was worth the money. The brown patch on my forehead is visibly smaller and lighter. Texture is like a silky thin lotion, absorbs in about thirty seconds, and never balls up under sunscreen.

After my second baby the pigment across my forehead wouldn't budge for anything. This did it. Not fast, I want to be clear, it took a solid three months of morning and night application, but the mask has lifted about eighty percent. I pair it with a bland moisturizer and mineral SPF and nothing else.

Bottle number three just arrived. My melasma journey started in 2024 with lasers that made things worse, and this humble pump bottle has done more than any of them, slowly and without drama. I use it with a bland ceramide cream and a hat the size of a satellite dish.

Third trimester left me with a proper pregnancy mask and my OB cleared this once I finished breastfeeding. Fourteen weeks of use, morning and evening, and my cheeks match my neck again. The pump measures out the perfect amount and the lotion dries down so fast I never wait to apply sunscreen.

Frustrating experience with the packaging. The pump stopped drawing product with what felt like a fifth of the bottle left, and I ended up unscrewing it and scraping. Results on my discoloration were okay, gradual lightening over three months. Would consider repurchasing if they fix the pump.

Committed to this all winter on my derm's advice while UV was low, and by spring my melasma was the faintest it has been in years. Smart timing if you can manage it. The airless pump kept every last drop usable, unlike dropper serums that oxidize halfway through.

Nothing touched my melasma before this, and I tried vitamin C, azelaic acid, and two rounds of peels. My dermatologist called it stubborn hormonal pigment and suggested Lytera because it skips hydroquinone. By month three the big patch on my forehead had broken up into faint islands. Still going.

Insurance is how my derm described it after my IPL series, something to keep the pigment from creeping back. Ten months later I remain spot free through a full summer. One pump AM, one PM, sandwiched between toner and moisturizer. It has earned permanent shelf space.

Truce is the right word, because melasma never fully surrenders. But this keeps mine so faint that tinted moisturizer covers it completely, when I used to need full coverage foundation plus concealer. Light lotion texture, mild scent, zero irritation alongside my weekly lactic acid.

As someone with medium-deep skin, I avoided hydroquinone after a bad rebound experience left me worse off. My derm specifically recommended Lytera because the phenylethyl resorcinol and tranexamic acid approach is gentler for tones like mine. Five months in, the post-inflammatory marks on my cheeks have faded evenly with no halo effect around them.

Costs add up since you really need two bottles a year minimum to see and keep results. That said, it earns the spend. My melasma is roughly half as visible as it was a year ago and my overall tone looks brighter. The light lotion format is foolproof to apply.

Two months in, my post-summer freckling has evened out nicely and my skin looks brighter overall. A pump bottle this small going this fast is my only gripe. Twice daily use killed mine in about eleven weeks, so budget for refills if you commit.

Slow. That is my whole review, basically. There is improvement in my discoloration but it took five months to say so with confidence, and I nearly quit at month three. If you have the patience and the budget it does eventually deliver. I'm just not sure I'll repurchase.

Twelve weeks in and the shadow on my upper lip that made me look like I had a mustache in photos has faded to almost nothing. I pat it on after cleansing, wait a minute, then layer moisturizer. No sting, no purge, no drama.

At sixty-three I assumed my age spots were permanent residents. Wrong. The cluster on my right cheek has faded to where I can skip foundation for errands. It took a full four months and I have used it every morning and night without fail. Delighted, honestly.

r.t: Kept pigment away after my peel
r.b: Post-peel maintenance was the assignment and it has delivered. My esthetician warned that pigment loves to return after a chemical peel, especially with my melasma history. Six months of Lytera morning and night and nothing has resurfaced. It feels weightless, more like a hydrating lotion than a treatment.

Brightening overall happened faster than spot correction for me. Within a month my whole face looked more even and awake, but the two dark sun spots on my left cheek needed closer to four months to visibly lighten. The lotion has a light botanical smell that fades in seconds.

Reactive skin plus a deeper tone made me nervous about brighteners, since irritation itself leaves marks on me. This never caused a single flush or sting. Over five months my acne scars and the darker patches around my mouth have evened out beautifully. Patience and daily sunscreen are non-negotiable partners.

No fireworks, just steady progress. Each month my skin tone looked a bit more uniform until around month four when a coworker asked if I had changed my makeup. I hadn't. Four stars only because the price stings on reorder day.

I cycled hydroquinone on and off for years and hated the rebound. This has been gentler and, honestly, more durable. The tranexamic acid and niacinamide combo seems to keep new pigment from forming rather than just bleaching what is there. Six months in, my melasma is the lightest it has been since my thirties.

Tempering expectations is key. This lightened my sun spots by maybe sixty percent over four months, which is honestly excellent for a non-hydroquinone product, but the marketing photos suggest more. Texture, pump, and gentleness are all top notch. Just know it is a marathon.

Really solid pigment corrector, just shy of perfect. It faded my sun spots meaningfully by month three and never once stung, but it leaves a slightly tacky finish that I notice on humid days. Under moisturizer it is fine. On its own in July, less fine.

Glycolic peels lightened my sun damage partway and this finished the job over the following three months. The morning pump goes under sunscreen, the evening pump over my toner, and it absorbs before I finish brushing my teeth. Faint pleasant smell. Nothing has crept back so far.

Skeptical was an understatement when my aesthetician handed me a two hundred dollar pump bottle. Ten weeks later I owe her an apology. The patches on both cheeks have gone from obvious to only visible in harsh bathroom lighting. It layers cleanly under my SPF 50 with no pilling.

Do a patch test if you are sensitive. My cheeks tingled for the first week before settling down completely. Once my skin adjusted it was smooth sailing and the acne marks along my chin faded by autumn. The pump dispenses a perfect face-sized dose.

Started this in June for the melasma above my lip and by September it had faded enough that I stopped wearing concealer there. Two pumps a day, always followed by mineral sunscreen. The light floral scent vanishes in under a minute. My only regret isn't starting years earlier.

Living in Phoenix means pigment is a constant battle. This has been my defense for a year now, one pump every morning under SPF and one at night after my retinol. New spots simply aren't forming the way they used to, and the old ones keep getting fainter.

Concealer usage has dropped by half since spring. That is the most honest metric I can give. The hyperpigmentation along my jawline from hormonal breakouts has faded steadily, and the niacinamide seems to have calmed the new breakouts too. Absorbs quickly, plays well with everything I layer over it.

Years of a darker forehead band ended this summer. I applied it every morning before SPF and every night after cleansing, no exceptions, and by week eleven the band had blended into the rest of my skin. My aesthetician noticed before I did. The bottle lasted just over three months.

My medspa put me on this after a round of IPL to keep the pigment from bouncing back. Eight months later my cheeks are still clear, even after a beach vacation where I was religious about reapplying SPF. One pump covers my whole face and the bottle lasted me close to four months.

Sun spots from twenty years of prairie summers started fading around the two month mark. It goes on like a light lotion, no tackiness, and my makeup applies fine right over it. I keep it next to my toothbrush so I never skip a night.

Miami humidity makes heavy serums unbearable and this one is genuinely weightless. My post-acne marks faded in about nine weeks and it never once pilled under sunscreen, even when I layer it damp. The scent is light and gone fast. Already on bottle number two.

r.t: Vineyard sun spots half as dark
r.b: Genuinely impressed, the sun spots on my cheekbones from years of vineyard work went from obvious to faint over one bottle, and it never once pilled under my fussy mineral sunscreen.

Overall tone improvement showed up within six weeks and my skin genuinely glows more. The one deep spot I bought it for has been more stubborn, maybe thirty percent lighter after five months. My derm says dermal pigment is slower. Keeping at it, but adjust your expectations for deep spots.

Four months of faithful twice daily use and my dermal melasma looks exactly the same. The floral scent also bothered me at every application. To be fair the lotion is light and never irritated my reactive skin, but at this price I needed to see something. My derm thinks my pigment sits too deep for topicals.

Where has this been all my life. I retired my vitamin C, my alpha arbutin, and my niacinamide serum because this one pump covers the same ground with better results. Four months in, the dime-sized spot on my left cheekbone is more of a memory than a mark.

Melasma from two pregnancies sat across my cheekbones for six years. My derm suggested this since I did not want hydroquinone again, and by week ten the patches had softened from brown to a faint tan. I use two pumps morning and night under moisturizer, and it sinks in within a minute. Strict SPF alongside, obviously. Expensive, but the first thing that has actually moved the needle.

Such a lovely silky texture, and it wears beautifully under makeup with no pilling. My pigmentation from an old sunburn has faded nicely since February. The two ounce bottle disappears fast at two pumps twice a day though, so the cost per month is real.

Decades of surfing left my cheekbones speckled. My derm put me on this with a zinc sunscreen and after one full bottle the speckling has genuinely blurred. It absorbs fast enough that I can wax a board ten minutes later without my hands sliding around my face. Weird criteria, I know.

Fragrance is my only complaint, a floral hit every application that I never learned to love. Results wise, no complaints at all. The sun damage on my cheeks faded steadily from March through May and my skin looks brighter overall. If they made this unscented it would be perfect.

Dark marks from ingrown hairs along my jaw cleared up faster than anything else I tried, maybe eight weeks to near invisible. The lotion is light, the faint scent doesn't bother me, and one pump does my whole beard area. Nobody markets this stuff to men and that is a mistake.
Understated but effective, a thin lotion twice a day that quietly lightened my patches by week nine with no tingle, no purge, and no drama.

Honestly torn on this one. My post-acne marks lightened maybe twenty percent after four months of twice daily use, which is something, but two hundred dollars something? The pump is nice and the lotion never irritated me, I just wanted more correction for the commitment.

Between cleanser and moisturizer, morning and night, that is all this asks. It plays well with my prescription tretinoin without extra irritation, which surprised me. The sun spot on my right temple that I have had since 2019 is now a faint smudge. Can't argue with that.

Works, but slowly. Nothing visible for the first six weeks, then somewhere around week nine my wife asked if I had been using something on the sun damage along my hairline. Four stars because the opaque pump gives zero warning before it starts sputtering empty.

Tranexamic acid was the ingredient my derm kept circling back to for my stubborn cheek pigment, and this delivers it without a prescription. Visible fading by week eight, significant by week fourteen. It feels like a light lotion and layers cleanly under my daily mineral SPF.

Middling results here. My hormonal pigment lightened a little around month three but plateaued after that, and the last quarter of the bottle sputtered out in messy spurts. It never irritated my dry skin, which counts for something. I switched to a prescription and kept this as a maintenance step.

The texture is a thin milky lotion rather than a true serum, which I like because it layers under sunscreen without pilling. Sun spots on my temples are noticeably lighter after three months. Docking a star for the floral fragrance, which feels out of place in a medical grade product.

You can't see how much product is left, which drives me nuts for something this expensive. That aside, the serum itself earns its keep. My acne marks from last winter faded in about ten weeks and my skin tone reads noticeably more uniform in photos.

Halfway through my second bottle and I'd call the improvement modest. Freckle-adjacent sun spots lightened, the actual melasma patch barely changed. It is pleasant to use, lightweight, no breakouts on my combination skin. I just expected more correction at this price after seven months.

Redness prone skin usually rejects brighteners, so I patch tested this for a week before going all in. Zero flushing, zero sting. The niacinamide might even be calming things down. The discoloration on my jaw from an old cooking burn has faded noticeably since December.

Recommended by my dermatologist over hydroquinone since I would be using it long term. Eight weeks brought subtle change, sixteen weeks brought obvious change. Knocking off a star because the lotion can feel slightly tacky for a few minutes in dry winter air before it settles.

Second summer with it and the routine survives everything from subway heat to rooftop happy hours. I appreciate that the scent is basically nothing, my office is fragrance-free and nobody has complained.
Zinc oxide at 12 percent usually means a mask-like film, but this spreads thin, sets in about a minute, and leaves a low-key glow. I keep one at home and one in my gym bag.
Surf checks, school runs, patio lunches, this covers all of it. Light tint evens me out enough that nobody knows I'm wearing anything. My only routine change in years that actually stuck.

Since going mineral-only during pregnancy I have tested plenty, and this is the one that stayed. No sting, no smell strong enough to trigger nausea, and the tint helped when my skin went blotchy in the second trimester.
Eye-rolled at the EnviroScreen blue light claims, but the basics are undeniable. Twelve percent zinc oxide, a believable tint, no sting around the eyes, and my skin has looked more even since March.

No graveyard of half-used sunscreen tubes in my drawer anymore. This one gets used down to the crimp because it doubles as my light coverage base. Reapplying over makeup is the only awkward part, I use a damp sponge.

Quick summary: elegant texture, believable tint, too much shine for my oily skin, and the tube separated constantly no matter how much I kneaded it. My daughter loves the same tube on her dry skin. Depends entirely on your skin type.

Got serious about sun protection after a basal cell removal, and my dermatologist specifically recommended this. It smooths over my 62-year-old skin without settling into lines, and the tint means I skip concealer most days.
Repurchased for the third time, which I've never done with sunscreen. Dewy enough for prairie winters, fine with a dusting of powder in July. It just works with my combination skin year round.
Having razor-sensitive skin means most sunscreens burn on application. This one goes on quiet, no sting, no scent bomb, and the tint is subtle enough that no one at the firehouse has noticed.

Solid pick for someone like me who refused sunscreen for 40 years. It doesn't feel like sunblock, doesn't smell like a beach, and my perpetually pink nose is less pink since the niacinamide got involved.

Mixed feelings on the packaging. The formula flatters my 55-year-old skin and never creases, but the tube split at the seam in my carry-on and sacrificed a third of the product to a ziploc bag. Formula five, tube three, so four.
Wore it for a full day at Whistler and my face was the only unwindburned part of me. Goes on thick enough for altitude without caking, and the flip cap works with gloves on.
Decent glow for dry winter months but by June I need powder on top by mid-morning. Never irritated my skin and the tint is genuinely flattering, so it stays in rotation from October through April.

r.t: Four days in Mexico, zero new spots
r.b: Picked it up at my med spa before a beach trip. Reapplied every two hours for four days and came home with no new freckles on my cheekbones, which has never happened. It photographs a little shiny, plan accordingly.

r.t: Runs out faster than it should
r.b: Ran the math and this is my most expensive per-gram skincare item. It earns its keep as both sunscreen and a light base, but I'd trade the pretty carton for 30 percent more product.
Doubted it could survive Miami, but it wears eight solid hours before I feel the need to refresh. The glow finish actually suits the climate, I skip highlighter entirely.
Good sunscreens exist everywhere, but the sheer wash of warmth this leaves is what keeps me paying for it. Bare-faced school drop-offs no longer scare me.

Pricey is an understatement for 55 ml, and the crimped end of the tube always traps product I paid for. Still four stars because nothing wears under makeup this well, and my winter redness looks calmer since I started it, which I credit to the niacinamide.

One universal tint is a stretch. On my olive skin it pulls slightly peach and I can see it in daylight photos. Comfortable and non-irritating, so I finished the tube at my desk where nobody photographs me.
Honestly I only bought it to stop my esthetician from bringing it up, and now I owe her an apology. Feels like a tinted moisturizer, wears like one too, and my skin tone looks more even by evening.

Ordered on a friend's insistence and it turned out kinder to my flaky cheeks than half my moisturizers. There is enough slip that it never drags, and the tint hides the pink patches my dryness leaves behind.

Rolled into tinted crumbs over three different moisturizers and my vitamin C serum, no matter how long I waited between layers. Gave it three weeks and half a tube before giving up. Texture lottery, and I lost.
If you hate how sunscreen feels, start here. Sinks in within a minute, never migrates into my eyes on long runs, and the tube lives in my jacket pocket.

Halfway through my second tube. Excellent wear, invisible finish on my brown skin, and no stinging on mornings after I use glycolic pads the night before. Withholding the fifth star for the price per millilitre, which is objectively silly.

The separation thing is real. Skip the knead and the first squeeze comes out as thin orange liquid. Mixed properly it is a lovely light tint that has never once broken me out, which is rare for me. Four stars for the daily arm workout.

As a melasma person I'm fanatical about SPF and this became my weekday default fast. Sheer coverage blurs my spots and nothing darkened all summer. One star off because I empty a tube a month between face, neck, and hands.
Outdoor wedding, 88 degrees and humid, and my face did not slide off. My makeup artist put it under my base in the morning and everything was still in place at the last dance.
Rosacea and a convertible are a bad combination, and this is the first SPF that manages both. No flare-ups since April, and the slight tint knocks back the redness that does show.

Golf four mornings a week, and for the first August in years I didn't finish the season with a raccoon line from my sunglasses. Stays put through sweat better than anything from the drugstore ever did.
Derm office sold it to me post microneedling and now I get the hype. Zero sting on freshly treated skin, and the tint covered enough of the redness that I went back to work the next day.
Every tinted SPF I owned before this either pilled under concealer or turned my chin grey. This one does neither. I press it in, wait sixty seconds, then apply blush and go.

Not made for very fair skin. Within an hour the tint turned distinctly orange on me and left a line at my jaw. The texture is genuinely beautiful, which makes the shade miss more frustrating. Returned it.
Lightweight enough for long hikes and it never drips with sweat, but the small tube doesn't love my two-application mountain days. Buying two at a time now and grumbling about it.

My dermatologist handed me this after an IPL series and it never stung, even on week-one skin. The 2 percent niacinamide seems to keep my redness calmer than my old sunscreen ever did. Only complaint is how fast the tube goes.
This runs glowy. My forehead looks polished at 9 am and greasy by noon, even set with powder. No breakouts and I trust the protection, I just need something more matte from May to September.
Nothing about my 40 minute bike commute defeats it, sweat, helmet straps, sunglasses pressure marks, nothing. I do blot once at lunch because the finish is more glow than matte.

Bought this for a Phoenix trip and it stayed put through 41 degree afternoons without stinging my eyes. Docking a star because using it on face and neck daily, the 55 ml tube was done in five weeks. That adds up.

On my deep-medium skin this vanishes, no grey, no purple cast, just a soft glow. That alone puts it ahead of every mineral sunscreen I have owned. I use a nickel-sized amount and buff it in with fingers.

r.t: My rosacea finally has an SPF
r.b: Finally, a sunscreen that doesn't set my face on fire. No flushing, no burn, and the tint takes the edge off my cheek redness. Third tube and counting.

Living on the coast I golf nearly year round, and this holds through a full round with one reapplication at the turn. Wish the water resistance ran longer than 40 minutes for sweaty days, hence four stars.

Three summers of sun anxiety and this is the first SPF that kept my melasma patches from darkening. The tint is sheer but warm enough to skip foundation on weekends, and it layers over my vitamin C serum without pilling. A tube lasts me about ten weeks.
It takes real desert sun to test an SPF and this passes. I garden before 8 am, reapply at noon with the brush powder, and my derm noted zero new sun damage at my annual check.

After years of chalky zinc formulas this one just disappears into my medium-tan skin. The universal tint reads warm, so very fair people should swatch first, but on me it looks like skin, only better.
Used my sister's on vacation, ordered my own before we even flew home. It sits beautifully over the hyaluronic serum I use in the morning and my skin looks finished, not coated.

Nice weight on skin, invisible at the hairline where liquid sunscreens usually collect, and no scent worth mentioning. Between my wife and me a tube disappears in a month, so the size is my only complaint.
Two months in and the clogged bumps I always got along my hairline from chemical sunscreens are gone, plus zero eye sting at spin class.

Tried it on a tester arm at the clinic, bought it on the spot. Six months later my watery-eye problem with sunscreens is fully solved. I get a small tug of dryness at the corners of my mouth in winter, moisturizer fixes it.

I must have tried a dozen mineral sunscreens and this is the only one that leaves no grey film on me. It spreads like a light tinted lotion, dries to a healthy satin, and my foundation goes over it clean.

r.t: Lovely formula, wrong shade for me
r.b: Started out hopeful because the texture is gorgeous and it never stung my reactive skin, but the tint is simply too warm for my neutral fair tone. I only reach for it on self-tanner weeks now.

Between the tint and the satin finish, my skin looks livelier than with any powder foundation I have tried at 67. It does cling a touch to the driest spots on my cheeks unless I moisturize first, and the price makes me wince.

Been wearing this under foundation every workday since February and my base applies smoother than it did over plain moisturizer. Faint earthy scent, gone within a minute. No pilling even over hyaluronic serum.
Love is a strong word for sunscreen but here we are. It replaced a tinted moisturizer, a primer, and my old SPF in one move, and my combination skin has stayed clear since the switch.
Prairie winter is brutal and this pulled double duty, SPF plus a bit of glow on grey days. Never flaked over my dry patches the way my old mineral stick did.
When it goes on sale I buy three. At full price I hesitate every time, then buy it anyway because my makeup looks better over it and my skin stays calm. Make of that what you will.

Used it religiously twice a day for eight weeks before writing this. Fine lines on my forehead are softer, skin feels sturdier, and my usual dryness never showed up despite constant air conditioning. Zero fragrance, which my reactive skin appreciates.

Even in Miami humidity this doesn't feel heavy or greasy, which is rare for something this hydrating. Took a month to notice the calming effect on my post-waxing redness. Four stars because the pump dispensed inconsistently from about the halfway mark.

You can actually see the difference in photos. By week three the crepey texture on my cheeks looked smoother and my foundation stopped settling into fine lines. I apply it on slightly damp skin, then a cream on top. Simple and it works.

Redness around my nose and chin that nothing touched for years faded within the first week. I honestly bought it for hydration and the calming was the bonus. Two pumps at night, one in the morning. No scent, no sting, sits perfectly under sunscreen.

r.t: Helped my healing, mind the cost
r.b: Great post-procedure, my CO2 laser recovery was visibly smoother than my first round without it. For everyday use though, the cost per bottle adds up fast if you apply the recommended amount. I now save it for treatment weeks and flare-ups.

Living in Phoenix, hydrating serums are a survival tool. This is the first one that keeps up. Light, fast absorbing, no pilling under mineral sunscreen, and my skin looks plumper by mid afternoon instead of parched. The bottle lasted me about ten weeks with twice daily use.

Returned mine after five weeks. No irritation, but also no change I could see or feel beyond what a basic hyaluronic serum gives me, and the pump started spitting air by week four. My clinic loves it so maybe post-procedure is the real use case. Not for me as a daily serum.

Third bottle in and it still pulls its weight. My skin is reactive to almost everything, including most HA serums weirdly, but this one has never once made me itch or flush. I use it AM and PM and my makeup sits better over it than over my old primer.

Hands down the most effective hydrator I have tried, and I have a drawer of failed serums. High altitude dryness plus a daily retinoid is brutal, and this holds the line. Absorbs fast, no film, no smell. I go through a bottle about every nine weeks.

Almost perfect. Calms my rosacea-prone skin, layers cleanly, fragrance free as promised. In deep winter I need two pumps plus a heavy cream or I still get tight by evening, so it isn't quite a one product solution for serious dryness. Still repurchasing.

Absolute staple. My skin is the calmest and most evenly hydrated it has been in a decade and this is the only new thing in my routine since October. It even took the itch out of my cheeks during ski season.

Four solid stars. My skin tolerated a retinal upgrade only because this was underneath. Hydrating, calming, invisible under makeup. The missing star is because a friend gets the same buffering effect from a serum that costs half as much. Quality tax, I suppose.

Skin barrier was wrecked from overdoing acids last fall. This was the only thing that didn't sting. Used it alone at night for two weeks, then slowly added everything back. My face felt normal again around day ten. Texture is almost like a light gel water, absorbs clean, no residue.

Got a sample from my clinic while doing pigment treatments and bought the full size before the sample ran out. It keeps my skin from freaking out at the tranexamic acid and retinoid I use around it. One pump covers face and neck easily.

Every February my face falls apart in the Winnipeg cold. Not this year. One pump twice a day, sandwiched between toner and cream, and I made it through without a single cracked patch. That alone justified the price for me.

Good hydrator and my post-microneedling redness settles noticeably faster with it. The pump is my gripe, it sputters once the bottle gets low and I am certain there is product trapped in there I can't reach. Contents five stars, packaging three.

Expected more given the reviews and the cost. It is a pleasant, light serum that never irritated my sensitive skin, and that is worth something. But hydration-wise I still needed my usual cream sandwich in Calgary winter, so what exactly was I paying for?

Menopause turned my skin into parchment almost overnight. This serum is the first thing that made it feel like mine again. I noticed real change by the end of the second bottle, so give it time. Silky texture, no smell, lovely under makeup.

Winter used to mean flaky patches around my nose no matter what cream I piled on. This went on under my usual moisturizer every night and by the end of week two the patches were gone. It is watery enough to spread with one pump but somehow keeps my face comfortable until morning.

Between IPL sessions my clinic insists on this serum and now I understand why. My skin stays calm and hydrated instead of tight and blotchy, and each session heals faster than the one before. No fragrance, no sting, no drama.

Effective but boring, which is honestly what my reactive skin needs. No actives drama, no tingle, just steady hydration that made my winter flaking manageable. I'd call it an 8 out of 10, held back only by the price to size ratio.

Doctor suggested this after a series of RF microneedling appointments. Healing time dropped from five days of pink to about two. Even between treatments I noticed firmer feeling skin, which I assume is the PPM6 peptide doing something. It became my daily first layer.

r.t: Finally an HA that works here
r.b: Was skeptical because plain hyaluronic acid usually makes my skin feel drier in our climate. This one doesn't. Whatever the supercharged HA plus peptide combination is doing, my skin holds moisture through the night instead of feeling tight by 3 am. Converted.

Solid HA serum with a nicer finish than most, no tackiness at all. My skin is comfortable and my flaky patches are gone. Knocking off a star because I honestly can't tell if it outperforms serums at half the price, though the texture is definitely more elegant.

Layers beautifully. Under vitamin C in the morning, under retinal at night, never a single pill or ball of product. My skin went from squeaky tight to comfortable in the first week. Understated but essential, the kind of product you notice only when you skip it.

Can't overstate how much this helped my skin survive a Minnesota winter while on adapalene. The flaking around my mouth just stopped. I press it into damp skin after cleansing and follow with a cream. It disappears in seconds and never balls up.

Pleasantly surprised, and I am a skeptic about clinic-brand serums. Dry patches settled in about ten days and it never pilled under my SPF. Only reason for four stars is I wish the results on my fine lines matched the hydration results. Those are unchanged so far.

Not bad at all, just slow. Around week five I finally saw calmer, better hydrated skin, and the improvement is real but modest. At this price I wanted the improvement to be obvious, not something I squint for. Sputtering pump near the end too.

Since starting tretinoin my face was constantly shedding. Adding this underneath at night cut the peeling way down within a week. It is unscented and watery-light so it doesn't interfere with the tret. Genuinely the buffer I needed.

Works well, just slowly. I saw nothing for the first three weeks and almost returned it, then somewhere in week four my skin turned a corner. Softer, calmer, less reactive to my glycolic toner. Patience required, which they should mention on the box.

Rosacea flare-ups used to take two weeks to settle. With this, more like four days. The texture is a lightweight gel serum from a pump, no fragrance, no burn, and it layers fine under azelaic acid. My derm was the one who suggested it and I'm grateful.

At 61 my skin barely holds moisture anymore. This serum changed the morning mirror situation noticeably. Cheeks look cushioned instead of deflated, and the fine crosshatching on my cheekbones softened by around week four. I pair it with a ceramide cream at night.

Retinol burn around my mouth healed in three days with this instead of the usual week. Keep it in the fridge, the cool serum on angry skin is bliss. Texture is like a silky water gel and the pump gives exactly the right amount.

Genuinely the first serum my reactive skin has accepted on the first try. No burning, no bumps, no waiting period. Hydrates deeply enough that I skipped night cream all summer. The kakadu plum gives it a faint natural tang, otherwise scent free.

Honestly didn't expect a hyaluronic serum to do anything my drugstore one didn't. Wrong. Within a month the tight after-cleansing feeling was gone and my retinol stopped wrecking me. The peptide and kakadu plum combo apparently does more than plain HA. Pump is precise, one is enough.

Middle of the road for me. The texture is lovely and it absorbs beautifully, but my dehydration lines looked exactly the same after six weeks. No irritation, no complaints on gentleness, just not enough visible payoff at this price point for my skin.

Like it a lot for morning use, hydrates without any film under sunscreen. At night I found I still needed a proper moisturizer on top or I woke up tight. So it is a great first layer rather than a standalone. Skin has been noticeably smoother since May.

r.t: Quietly the best in my routine
r.b: This is the one product I have repurchased three times without thinking twice. It doesn't tingle or transform anything overnight, it just keeps my reactive skin flat and calm and hydrated so everything else can work. My cheeks stopped doing that itchy red thing entirely.

r.t: Light as water, works like magic
r.b: So light it feels like nothing going on, then an hour later my skin is noticeably bouncier. I was using it just post-procedure but now it is every single day. The pump means no wasted product and no gunky dropper. Small bottle, but a pump goes far.

Disappointed because I so wanted this to work for my reactive skin. Within a week I had small congested bumps along my jaw that cleared only after I stopped using it. Patch test first if you are acne-prone. Gentle formula for most I'm sure, just not for me.

Dermatologist put me on this after a round of IPL and it has stayed in my routine ever since. Hydration without heaviness, no clogged pores, and my pigment treatments absorb better over it. A little goes far, one pump does my whole face and neck.

Fresh off a lactic peel my face was hot and tight, and one pump of this cooled the whole thing down within a minute. I keep it front and center on the shelf now. Hydration lasts through the night and it never stings, even on exfoliated skin.

r.t: The serum I never skip now
r.b: My esthetician handed me a sample after microneedling and I get the hype. Absorbs in about twenty seconds, never pills under my SPF, and my skin stopped feeling like paper by day three. One pump in the morning under moisturizer, one at night after cleansing.

Sensitive skin here, the type where new products mean a week of burning. This gave me nothing but comfort from day one. It is more hydrating than any HA serum I've used, and I have used many. My redness has visibly dialed down after two months.

r.t: Feels like a drink for skin
r.b: It sinks in like water but hydrates like something much richer. I use two pumps on damp skin before moisturizer at night. Fine lines around my mouth look softer after about a month. No fragrance, no tackiness, plays nice with everything I layer over it.

Really lovely serum that does what it claims, my skin is calmer and better hydrated since starting it. Four stars only because the price stings for a bottle this size. If it were twenty dollars cheaper it would be a forever repurchase instead of a sometimes one.

Post microneedling my skin drinks this stuff. The clinic uses it right after the treatment and sent me home with a bottle. Redness that used to linger for three days was mostly gone by the next morning. No sting on freshly needled skin, which says a lot.

Just okay for the money. It hydrates, it is gentle, nothing pilled. But after two full bottles I cannot point to anything my old HA serum at a third of the price wasn't already doing. If you are post-procedure maybe the peptides matter more. For daily use I'm unconvinced.

Two pumps of this under a basic moisturizer beat my expensive cream on its own, which was a humbling discovery. Skin looks dewy without shine and my chronic dry patches by my ears cleared in two weeks. Buying again without hesitation.

Nothing else calmed the eczema patches near my hairline without a prescription. This did, in about a week. It is genuinely fragrance free, absorbs before I finish brushing my teeth, and one bottle lasts me two months. Worth every dollar to me.

r.t: Bought for mom, stole it back
r.b: Ordered this for my mother post facelift on her surgeon's advice, tried a pump out of curiosity, and immediately ordered a second bottle for myself. Her incision area healed beautifully and my dehydrated combination skin finally stopped flaking around my brows.

Bought this after a fractional laser left my cheeks tight and flaky. Two pumps twice a day and the flaking stopped within four days. Thin, slightly slippery texture, absorbs fast, zero sting even on raw skin. No scent whatsoever. Expensive, yes, but it earned a permanent spot in my routine.

Nice texture, absorbs quick, plays well under tretinoin. My skin is less angry overall. I docked a star because the bottle is small for the money and I burn through it in about six weeks using it twice daily. Would love a bigger size option.

Wanted to give five stars because the serum itself is excellent, gentle and deeply hydrating with zero scent. But my bottle's pump jammed in the first week and I had to unscrew the top and dig around to fix it. For this price the packaging should be flawless.

Bounced back from a medium depth peel way faster than last time, and this serum was the only variable I changed. Applied it four times a day per my clinic. Zero sting on day two skin, which surprised me. The pump makes it easy to keep things sanitary while healing.
